issues.issue_title: Early intrusive pop-ups
issues.user_problem: Users are interrupted before understanding the site
signals_to_detect: Modal or overlay element appears on page load (no user interaction required)
Popup blocks main content with no visible dismiss button or skip option
Newsletter signup or permission request modal appears immediately on homepage
Modal or fullscreen layer appears before user can interact with product content
issues.recommendation: Delay all non-essential pop-ups (newsletter, discount offers, app download prompts) until the user has demonstrated intent — either by scrolling 50%+ of the page, spending 30+ seconds on site, or triggering exit intent. Use a time delay of at least 30 seconds for any modal that must appear on the homepage. Always include a clearly visible dismiss option (X button or 'No thanks' link) in the top-right corner of the overlay.
acceptance_criteria: No modal or overlay appears within the first 5 seconds of page load
All non-legal pop-ups trigger only after 30s dwell time, 50% scroll depth, or exit intent
Every modal includes a clearly visible dismiss button (min 44x44px tap target)
User can click outside the modal to close it on desktop
Legal/cookie consent banners exempt from delay rule but must not block full viewport
negative_signals: Pop-ups appear only after user has scrolled 50%+ of page or spent 30+ seconds
Modals include clear X button or 'No thanks' option in visible corner
User can click outside modal to dismiss it
Pop-up appears only on exit intent or after meaningful interaction
issues.context_notes: Only flag pop-ups that appear within first 5 seconds or before user interacts. Do not flag: Exit-intent modals, scroll-triggered (>50% page), or time-delayed (30s+). Industry context: Legal compliance pop-ups (cookies) may appear immediately; flag intrusive marketing/newsletter pop-ups.

issues.issue_title: Hidden language selector
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to change language/location
signals_to_detect: Language or location selector hidden in footer or buried in menu
No language/location toggle visible in header or navigation
Language selector present but not easily identifiable (generic icon or text label)
Multi-region ecommerce site without visible language switching option
issues.recommendation: Move the language and region selector to a permanently visible location in the site header — ideally top-right — using a globe icon combined with the current language/region label (e.g., 'EN | GBP'). Ensure the selector is present on every page template including checkout. On mobile, include it in the primary navigation menu at the top level.
acceptance_criteria: Language/region selector visible in the header on every page without scrolling
Selector uses both a globe icon and a text label (language code or country name)
Clicking the selector opens a panel showing all available language/region options
Selected language persists across the full session and for returning users
Selector accessible on mobile via the primary navigation menu
negative_signals: Language/country selector visible in header without scrolling
Flag icon or language name clearly displayed in top navigation
Current language/country shown with dropdown arrow indicator
Selector accessible within one click from any page
issues.context_notes: Only flag if language selector genuinely hard to find (requires >2 clicks or hidden). Do not flag: Footer placement if clearly visible, or flag/language name in header. Industry context: Single-market sites may not need prominent language selector.

issues.issue_title: CTA overload
issues.user_problem: Too many CTAs overwhelm users
signals_to_detect: Multiple competing CTAs for the SAME user action (e.g., 3+ variations of 'Buy Now' or 'Add to Cart')
Primary CTA not visually distinguished from secondary CTAs (same size, color, prominence)
Homepage hero section contains 3+ CTAs with equal visual weight competing for immediate action
Multiple checkout CTAs visible simultaneously (e.g., 'Checkout', 'Express Checkout', 'Quick Buy' all equally prominent)
issues.recommendation: Audit each page for the number of CTAs and establish a strict visual hierarchy: one dominant primary CTA (filled, high contrast), one optional secondary CTA (outlined or lower contrast), and no more than two CTAs competing at equal visual weight on any single page section. Remove or de-emphasise tertiary actions. Apply this hierarchy consistently across all page templates.
acceptance_criteria: Each page section contains no more than one primary CTA at dominant visual weight
Secondary CTAs are visually subordinate (outline style or reduced size) relative to the primary
No two filled CTAs of equal colour, size, and weight appear adjacent to one another
CTA hierarchy documented in the design system and applied consistently site-wide
User testing confirms primary action is identifiable within 5 seconds on key pages
negative_signals: Service category buttons with clear color-coding for different features (e.g., 'Used Products' green, 'Rent Now' blue)
Navigation menu items are text links or minimal buttons, not primary action CTAs
Primary CTA uses solid color while secondary actions use outlined/ghost button style
CTAs lead to different features/services, not competing for same conversion action
issues.context_notes: Do not count: (1) Navigation category links, (2) Service feature buttons with clear differentiation, (3) Secondary utility links. Only flag when multiple CTAs compete for the SAME conversion action.

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent product cards
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to scan products
signals_to_detect: Product cards vary in layout, height, or content structure across listing
Add-to-cart button placed inconsistently (bottom for some, hover for others)
Product price, rating, or image placement differs between cards on same page
Some cards show additional info (SKU, tags) while others do not
issues.recommendation: Define a single standardised product card template covering: image aspect ratio, title truncation rules, price placement, rating display, and CTA position. Apply this template across all PLPs, carousels, and recommendation widgets. Enforce consistency through a shared component in the design system or component library — not ad-hoc per-page CSS overrides.
acceptance_criteria: All product cards share the same image aspect ratio across every listing context
Price, title, and rating appear in the same position on every card variant
CTA (Add to Cart / Quick View) appears in a consistent position on hover or always-visible
Card component defined in the design system with no page-level style overrides
Cards visually consistent across homepage carousels, PLP grids, and recommendation widgets
negative_signals: All product cards show same information in same positions (image top, price bottom, title middle)
Rating stars appear in same location on all cards that have reviews
All cards use same image aspect ratio and size
Badges (sale, new, low stock) appear in consistent corner position
issues.context_notes: Variation in card content is acceptable if information hierarchy is consistent (e.g., always price at bottom, image at top). Only flag when: Critical info (price, title, image) appears in different locations across cards OR some cards missing essential data. Do not flag: Intentional variations for different product types (digital vs physical) or optional information (ratings only shown when reviews exist).

issues.issue_title: Missing policy info near title
issues.user_problem: Users lack trust before purchase
signals_to_detect: No delivery timeframe visible anywhere on PDP (not near price, not in product details, not in any section)
Shipping cost only revealed at checkout, not shown anywhere on PDP
Return policy link completely absent from PDP (not in footer, not in product info, not anywhere visible)
No trust indicators (warranties, guarantees) visible anywhere in product area or details
issues.recommendation: Display a concise summary of the key purchase policies (shipping cost or free shipping threshold, return window, and estimated delivery time) directly on the PDP near the product title or within the purchase zone — above the Add to Cart button. Link each policy summary to its full policy page for users who need more detail.
acceptance_criteria: Shipping cost or free shipping threshold visible on PDP without scrolling
Return window (e.g., '30-day free returns') stated near the Add to Cart button
Estimated delivery time or date range shown on PDP
Each policy item links to the full corresponding policy page
Policy information visible on both desktop (1280px) and mobile (375px) without scroll
negative_signals: Delivery timeframe displayed anywhere on PDP (near price, in details section, or clearly visible)
Shipping cost calculator or flat rate shown on PDP before add-to-cart
Return policy clearly linked or mentioned in product section (footer counts)
Trust badges (warranty, guarantee, returns) visible on PDP in any section
issues.context_notes: Only flag if 3+ policy items are COMPLETELY missing from PDP (not just suboptimally placed). Presence in footer, expandable sections, or anywhere visible on page counts as 'available'. Focus on complete absence of: (1) delivery time, (2) shipping cost info, (3) return policy, (4) warranties. If 2 or fewer missing, do not flag.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.issue_title: Unclear add-to-cart flow
issues.user_problem: Users don't know required steps
signals_to_detect: Mandatory selection steps (size, color, quantity) not clearly marked as required
Add-to-cart button disabled or grayed out without explanation until options selected
No visible instruction text explaining option selections before add-to-cart is available
Error messages appear only after attempting to add product without required selections
issues.recommendation: Ensure that required selections (size, colour, quantity) are clearly presented and must be completed before the Add to Cart action is triggered. If a user attempts to add to cart without making required selections, scroll to and highlight the unselected option with an inline error message rather than a generic alert. Show a clear confirmation (mini-cart overlay or toast) once the item is successfully added.
acceptance_criteria: Required variant selections (size, colour) clearly labelled as required on PDP
Attempting Add to Cart without required selections highlights the missing field with an inline error
Page does not reload or navigate away when a selection error occurs
Successful add to cart triggers a visible confirmation (mini-cart flyout or toast notification)
Confirmation shows the added item name, selected variant, and a link to view cart
negative_signals: Required dropdowns marked with asterisk (*) or 'Required' label before interaction
Helpful text above dropdowns explains why selection is needed
Add-to-cart button clearly disabled with tooltip explaining what's needed
Default option shown for non-critical selections
issues.context_notes: Only flag if requirements are unclear AND user gets error. Do not flag: Visual indicators (disabled button, asterisks) even if not perfect. Industry context: Configurable products (tech, apparel) require option selection; flag unclear communication, not the requirement itself. NEW: Bundle products require especially clear communication. All components must show: (1) which selections are required, (2) visual progress if multi-step, (3) what happens if skipped. Use checklists, steppers, or completion indicators for complex configurations.

issues.issue_title: Forced cart redirection
issues.user_problem: Users cannot continue shopping
signals_to_detect: Add-to-cart action immediately redirects to checkout without option to continue shopping
No Continue Shopping or Back to Products link visible after item added
Cart page forces checkout with no navigation back to product browsing
Shopping cart overlay or modal lacks return option to keep shopping
issues.recommendation: Replace full-page cart redirects on Add to Cart with a mini-cart drawer or overlay that slides in from the right, showing the added item and cart summary. Include a 'Continue Shopping' button as the primary action and 'View Cart / Checkout' as secondary options. Reserve full cart page navigation for when the user explicitly clicks the cart icon.
acceptance_criteria: Add to Cart action opens a mini-cart drawer or overlay — not a full page redirect
Mini-cart displays: added item image, name, variant, quantity, and subtotal
'Continue Shopping' button closes the drawer and returns focus to the PDP
'View Cart' and 'Checkout' CTAs present in the mini-cart
Mini-cart dismissible by clicking outside it or pressing Escape key
negative_signals: 'Continue Shopping' button visible after add-to-cart action
Add-to-cart triggers mini-cart drawer that allows continuing or going to cart
User remains on PDP after adding item, with confirmation message
Cart page includes prominent 'Back to Shopping' or category links
issues.context_notes: Only flag if no way to continue shopping after add-to-cart. Do not flag: Brief redirect followed by continue option, or mini-cart that allows continuing. Industry context: Some niches (tickets, limited items) may intentionally push to checkout.

issues.issue_title: Limited payment methods
issues.user_problem: Users abandon due to missing options
signals_to_detect: Only credit card option available (no digital wallets, COD, or alternative payments)
Payment method selection limited to single provider (Stripe only, or single card type)
No Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, or regional payment methods visible
Checkout flow does not offer installment plans or BNPL options where available
issues.recommendation: Expand payment options to include at minimum: credit/debit card, one digital wallet (PayPal, Apple Pay, or Google Pay), and one Buy Now Pay Later option (Klarna, Afterpay, or Clearpay) where available in the target market. Display payment method logos on the PDP, cart, and checkout entry page so users know before committing to the checkout flow.
acceptance_criteria: At least one digital wallet option (PayPal, Apple Pay, or Google Pay) available at checkout
BNPL option present for markets where it is available (Klarna, Afterpay, etc.)
Payment method logos visible on cart page and checkout entry step
Express checkout (Apple Pay / Google Pay) offered on PDP and cart for one-tap purchase
All offered payment methods fully functional end-to-end (tested with test transactions)
negative_signals: At least 3 payment methods available (card, digital wallet, COD)
Popular local payment options included (e.g., Tabby, PayPal)
Payment icons visible before checkout to set expectations
Guest checkout allows multiple payment types

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent CTA styles
issues.user_problem: Users can't identify primary actions
signals_to_detect: Shop Now button uses different color or style across different pages (Homepage vs PLP vs PDP)
Primary CTAs (Add to Cart) mix button styles (outline, solid, ghost) across pages
Same action has different button text or visual treatment on different pages
CTAs within same page use conflicting colors, sizes, or typography weight
issues.recommendation: Define a two-tier button system: a single primary button style (filled, brand colour, high contrast) for the most important action on any screen, and a single secondary style (outlined or ghost) for supporting actions. Remove any third or fourth button style variants unless they serve a documented distinct purpose. Apply the system consistently via a shared component library.
acceptance_criteria: Only two CTA styles used site-wide: one filled primary and one outlined secondary
Primary button colour and style identical across all page types (homepage, PDP, checkout)
No page contains two filled buttons of equal weight competing for the primary action
Button component defined in design system with no ad-hoc colour or size overrides
Design system documentation specifies when each button style should be used
negative_signals: Primary CTA uses solid color, secondary actions use outline or ghost style
All primary CTAs use consistent color throughout site
Button hierarchy clear through size and color differentiation
Destructive actions use different color from primary
issues.context_notes: Only flag if CTA styling is genuinely inconsistent AND confusing. Do not flag: Intentional variations for different action types (destructive vs. primary). Focus on: Whether user can identify what's clickable and primary action.

issues.issue_title: Low text contrast
issues.user_problem: Low-vision users struggle to read
signals_to_detect: Body text or product descriptions use light gray text on white or light background
Secondary text or labels appear in very light gray without sufficient contrast to background
Product pricing or discount information difficult to read due to color contrast
Navigation links or interactive elements use low-contrast colors (light on light)
issues.recommendation: Audit all text and background colour combinations across every page type using the WebAIM Contrast Checker or Axe browser extension. Update failing combinations to meet WCAG 2.1 AA minimums: 4.5:1 for body text (under 18px), 3:1 for large text (18px+ or 14px+ bold). Pay particular attention to light grey on white body copy, placeholder text, and button labels. Document passing colour pairs in the design system.
acceptance_criteria: All body text (under 18px) achieves minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
All large text (18px+ regular or 14px+ bold) achieves minimum 3:1 contrast ratio
CTA button label text passes contrast ratio against the button fill colour
Placeholder text in form fields meets minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Axe accessibility audit shows zero colour contrast violations across all page types
negative_signals: Body text meets WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 minimum)
All text readable without zooming or straining
Light gray text reserved only for truly optional secondary content
Important information (price, availability) uses high-contrast colors

issues.issue_title: Unclear error messages
issues.user_problem: Error messages use technical jargon or unclear language
signals_to_detect: Error messages use technical terms (Invalid SSL cert, 403 Forbidden, Malformed request)
Form validation errors do not specify what was wrong or how to fix it
Error text is vague (Error occurred, Try again later) without explanation
Multiple error messages appear without guidance on which field to correct first
BUNDLE/CONFIG ERRORS: Product configuration errors don't explain what selections are required
issues.recommendation: Rewrite all system error messages to follow a three-part structure: (1) what went wrong in plain language, (2) why it happened if helpful, and (3) a specific next action the user can take to recover. Place error messages inline adjacent to the source of the problem rather than at the top of the page. Avoid technical codes, passive voice, and blame-oriented language ('You entered an invalid...').
acceptance_criteria: All error messages explain what went wrong in plain, non-technical language
Each error message includes at least one actionable recovery step
Inline field-level errors appear adjacent to the offending field, not only at page top
No error message uses jargon, error codes, or blames the user
Error messages tested with 5 users who can accurately describe the problem and recovery step after reading
negative_signals: Error messages use plain language explaining what's wrong
Messages explain what went wrong and how to fix it
No technical codes or jargon visible to users
Error messages are contextual to the specific field or action
issues.context_notes: Only flag truly unclear error messages. Do not flag: Technical but understandable terms for technical audience. Industry context: Developer tools may use technical errors appropriately. Focus on: Whether target audience understands message. NEW: Configuration errors (bundles, customization) must clearly state what's required. Example: 'Please select size and color to continue' vs. 'Configuration error'. Industry context: Complex product configurations (bundles, kits) need explicit requirement communication.

issues.issue_title: Lack of personalization
issues.user_problem: Users receive generic content despite sharing preferences
signals_to_detect: Homepage or product recommendations appear identical for all users (no user-specific content)
Browse history, saved items, or wishlist not used to customize recommendations
Search results or category pages show same products regardless of user segment
No personalized messaging (Hello {name}, Your recent items, etc.) throughout site
issues.recommendation: Implement a minimum viable personalisation layer using available signals: browsing history for 'Recently Viewed' on homepage and cart, purchase history for 'Buy Again' in the account, and category affinity for personalised product recommendations on PLPs. Use a cookie or session token for guest users and sync to account for logged-in users.
acceptance_criteria: 'Recently Viewed' product carousel present on homepage and cart for returning visitors
Logged-in users see personalised product recommendations on homepage based on browsing or purchase history
'Buy Again' or 'Your Favourites' section visible in the account area
Personalisation works for both logged-in users (account-synced) and guests (session/cookie-based)
No personalisation module shows empty or irrelevant results — fallback to bestsellers if no history
negative_signals: Homepage shows personalized recommendations based on browsing history
Returning users see 'Welcome back' with recently viewed items
Product suggestions based on previous purchases or viewed categories
User preferences (language, currency) remembered across sessions

issues.issue_title: No anticipatory guidance
issues.user_problem: App does not proactively help users during journeys
signals_to_detect: No contextual help, tooltips, or onboarding prompts visible during key tasks
Absence of cart abandonment reminders, discount alerts, or time-sensitive offers
No helpful suggestions (Did you know?, Tips, Try searching for) on empty states or slow pages
Product pages lack suggestions for next steps or related items to explore

Complex multi-step or domain-specific features (simulations, configuration flows, financial tools) provide no pre-task orientation, purpose explanation, or sample output before the user encounters inputs
issues.recommendation: Add contextual guidance at key decision points in the user journey: show estimated delivery dates on PDP before users add to cart, surface return policy reminders on the cart page, prompt users to save their cart or create an account before navigating away, and send abandoned cart reminders (email or push) for users who leave mid-checkout.
acceptance_criteria: Estimated delivery date shown on PDP near the Add to Cart button
Return policy summary visible on cart page near the Checkout CTA
Users who have items in cart and attempt to navigate away see a save-cart prompt or confirmation
Abandoned cart email or notification sent within 1 hour of cart abandonment for opted-in users
Guidance text is contextually accurate and not shown when irrelevant (e.g., no delivery estimate for digital products)
negative_signals: System suggests next steps contextually
Helpful tips appear at right moment
Proactive error prevention shown
Smart defaults based on previous behavior

issues.issue_title: Missing global search
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to find content quickly
signals_to_detect: No search bar, search icon, or search field visible in header on Homepage
Search missing from header on Product Listing Pages (category/collection pages)
Search missing from header on Product Detail Pages
Search functionality accessible only through footer links or hidden menu (not in main header)
issues.recommendation: Add a clearly visible search bar or search icon to the primary header navigation, present and accessible on all page types. On desktop, show a visible search input bar or an expandable field that opens on icon click. On mobile, show a search icon that opens a full-screen search overlay with autofocus on the input field.
acceptance_criteria: Search icon or input visible in the header on every page without scrolling
Desktop: search expands to a full input bar on click or is always-visible in header
Mobile: search icon opens a full-screen overlay with the input field auto-focused
Search is operable by keyboard (Tab to reach, Enter to submit)
Search accessible from all page types including checkout and account pages
negative_signals: Search bar prominently placed in header across Homepage, PLP, and PDP
Search icon visible in mobile header (collapsible or icon-only is acceptable)
Search accessible via one click from all major pages
Absence from checkout or cart overlay is acceptable (focused conversion flows)
issues.context_notes: Search must be missing from at least 2 of: Homepage, PLP, PDP, Category pages. Absence from checkout is acceptable. NEW: Research shows users often prefer category browsing over search, especially in gift/inspiration contexts. Only flag if search is genuinely missing; do not flag if categories are primary navigation by design. Consider product type: Search is critical for large catalogs (1000+ SKUs), less critical for curated gift selections (<500 SKUs).

issues.issue_title: Missing error recovery guidance
issues.user_problem: Users receive errors but no clear path or instructions to fix them
signals_to_detect: Error message text does not specify what was wrong or how to fix (e.g., 'Invalid input')
No indication of which form field contains error or needs correction
Help text or examples absent when form field error occurs
No link to support, FAQ, or undo action after error state
issues.recommendation: Design all error states to include three recovery pathways where applicable: (1) a retry action (e.g., 'Try Again' button), (2) an alternative path (e.g., 'Browse All Products' if search fails), and (3) a support contact link for errors the user cannot self-resolve. Never show a dead-end error with no onward journey. Use friendly, action-oriented language throughout.
acceptance_criteria: All error states include at least one actionable recovery CTA (retry, alternative path, or support link)
No error page or state is a dead end with no navigation or next step
Search no-results pages include alternative pathways (popular categories, related terms)
Form submission errors retain valid field data and highlight only the failing field
Support contact link visible on errors that cannot be self-resolved by the user
negative_signals: Error messages include 'How to fix' instructions
Links to help articles or support provided with errors
Contact information shown when errors can't be self-resolved
Retry or alternative action buttons included
issues.context_notes: Only flag if error provides no path forward. Do not flag: Clear error with obvious fix even without explicit instructions. Focus on: Whether user knows what to do next. Common false positive: Flagging messages that are clear from context.

issues.issue_title: Non-sticky headers
issues.user_problem: Users lose context when scrolling
signals_to_detect: Header/navigation menu disappears when user scrolls down the page
Logo not visible after scrolling below initial viewport
Shopping cart or account icon not accessible while scrolling content
No sticky breadcrumb trail or context indicator visible during scroll
issues.recommendation: Implement a sticky header that remains visible as the user scrolls down the page. On scroll-down, collapse the header to a compact version showing only the logo, search icon, cart, and primary navigation trigger to minimise viewport footprint. On scroll-up, restore the full header. Ensure the sticky header does not overlap fixed bottom bars or floating elements on mobile.
acceptance_criteria: Header remains accessible at all scroll depths on desktop and mobile
Header collapses to a compact version on scroll-down to preserve viewport space
Full header restores on scroll-up
Sticky header does not overlap or obscure page content or CTAs
Cart, search, and navigation all accessible from the sticky header without returning to top
negative_signals: Header with navigation and cart remains visible during scroll
Product title and price stick to top on PDP when scrolling
Filter sidebar header remains visible during long filter lists
Key information accessible without scrolling back up
issues.context_notes: Only flag for long-scrolling pages where losing context hinders task completion. Do not flag: Short pages, sticky headers with limited info, pages where scrolling up is natural. Context: PDP with long descriptions benefits more than short homepage. Mobile vs desktop may differ.

issues.issue_title: Small touch targets (general)
issues.user_problem: Interactive elements under 44x44px cause tap errors on mobile
signals_to_detect: Links or buttons appear significantly smaller than 44px square on mobile viewport
Navigation menu items closely spaced with insufficient padding
Add-to-cart or checkout buttons appear cramped without adequate spacing
Icon-only buttons without visible text label or adequate button size
issues.recommendation: Increase the tap target size of all interactive elements to a minimum of 44x44px on mobile viewports, using CSS padding rather than increasing the visual element size where needed. Audit all icon buttons, navigation links, filter chips, and form controls. Ensure at least 8px spacing between adjacent tap targets to prevent accidental mis-taps.
acceptance_criteria: All interactive elements have a minimum 44x44px tap target area on mobile (375px viewport)
Icon-only buttons padded to meet 44px minimum without changing visual size
Minimum 8px gap between adjacent tap targets throughout the interface
Footer links, filter tags, and breadcrumb items all meet tap target minimum
Chrome DevTools mobile emulation shows no overlapping or undersized tap targets on key pages
negative_signals: All interactive elements minimum 44x44px on mobile
Adequate spacing between touch targets (8px+ gap)
Icon buttons have sufficient padding around the icon
Clickable areas extend beyond visible button edges
issues.context_notes: All interactive elements should be minimum 44x44px on mobile viewports. Do not flag: Desktop-only interfaces, elements that expand on tap, or when adequate spacing prevents mis-taps. Only flag when: Mobile users would genuinely struggle to tap accurately. Test on actual mobile devices/viewports below 768px.

issues.issue_title: Weak value proposition above the fold
issues.user_problem: Users cannot quickly understand what the site offers
signals_to_detect: Hero section heading is vague (Welcome, Best Selection, Shop Now) without clear site mission
No supporting subheading or description explaining what products/services are offered
Value proposition buried below large visuals or placed lower on page
Unclear if site is for shoes, electronics, furniture, etc. from initial view
issues.recommendation: Add a concise value proposition headline (8–12 words maximum) and a supporting sub-line (under 20 words) to the hero section of the homepage, visible above the fold on both desktop (1280px) and mobile (375px). The headline should state what the brand sells and for whom or what benefit it delivers. Pair with a single high-contrast primary CTA.
acceptance_criteria: A clear headline describing the brand's core offer visible in the hero without scrolling
Headline is 12 words or fewer and intelligible to a first-time visitor
Supporting sub-line provides context or benefit in under 20 words
Hero includes one primary CTA linked to the main conversion path
Value proposition visible on mobile (375px) without scrolling or being clipped by the header
negative_signals: Videos include captions or transcripts
Audio content has text alternative available
Video player has accessible controls with keyboard navigation
Captions can be toggled on/off by user

issues.issue_title: Hero visuals distract from task
issues.user_problem: Large visuals delay task completion
signals_to_detect: Hero image takes up more than 50% of initial viewport height
Primary CTA button difficult to spot amid large hero graphic
Users must scroll significantly to see main navigation or product categories
Hero section provides no clear entry point to primary user task (search, browse, etc.)
issues.recommendation: Reduce the visual dominance of the hero image by constraining its height to a maximum of 70% of the viewport on desktop and 50% on mobile. Ensure a primary task CTA or navigation entry point is always visible below or alongside the hero without scrolling. If the hero must be full-bleed, overlay the CTA directly on the image with sufficient contrast.
acceptance_criteria: A primary task CTA or navigation entry point visible without scrolling on desktop (1280px)
Hero image height does not exceed 70vh on desktop or 50vh on mobile
CTA or navigation visible simultaneously with the hero, not pushed below it
Text overlaid on hero images passes 4.5:1 contrast ratio
User can identify the primary next action within 5 seconds of landing on the page
negative_signals: Hero section occupies less than 40% of viewport height
Primary CTA clearly visible above fold without scrolling
Hero provides immediate access to main shopping task (search, browse, featured products)
Hero content is relevant product photography, not generic lifestyle imagery
issues.context_notes: Only flag if hero occupies >50% of initial viewport AND pushes primary shopping task below fold. Do not flag if: Hero is large but includes product showcase or clear shopping entry point. Industry context: Lifestyle/brand-focused sites may intentionally use large heroes; flag only when it hinders task completion.

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent icon usage
issues.user_problem: Icons mean different things across pages
signals_to_detect: Cart icon used differently on Homepage vs PDP (different style, color, or placement)
Search icon represented differently across navigation and header
Star/heart icon for favorites shown in different style on different pages
Menu icon burger/hamburger design changes between layouts
issues.recommendation: Establish an icon usage standard specifying: which icons are used for which actions, whether icons are always accompanied by text labels, and which icon library or style (filled, outlined, two-tone) is used consistently. Enforce this through a shared icon component. Remove any icons used for decorative purposes that duplicate adjacent text labels or create visual noise.
acceptance_criteria: All icons across the site come from a single consistent style (all outlined or all filled — not mixed)
Every icon used for navigation or action is accompanied by a text label on desktop
No two different icons are used for the same action across different pages
No two different actions are represented by the same icon
Icon usage documented in the design system with the canonical meaning of each icon
negative_signals: Same icon represents same function sitewide
Icon style consistent (all outlined or all filled)
Icon meanings follow common conventions
Icon + text label used consistently for clarity

issues.issue_title: Overloaded main navigation
issues.user_problem: Too many menu items overwhelm users
signals_to_detect: Main navigation contains 10+ top-level items without clear grouping or hierarchy
Navigation menu items compete for attention without clear visual organization
No differentiation between primary categories and secondary utility links in navigation
Navigation requires horizontal scrolling or wrapping to show all items
issues.recommendation: Reduce top-level navigation to a maximum of 7 items (ideally 5–6) by grouping related categories under a single parent label. Use card sorting with real users to determine the most intuitive groupings. Apply plain, customer-facing labels — not internal product taxonomy names. Use a mega menu or flyout only if the sub-categories genuinely cannot be reduced further.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level navigation items reduced to 7 or fewer labels
Category labels use customer-language validated by card sorting or user research
Sub-categories grouped logically under parent labels with no overlap between groups
Navigation accessible in 2 clicks or fewer to any major section from the homepage
Mobile navigation uses a collapsible accordion pattern with a visible back button at each level
negative_signals: Main navigation has 5-7 top-level items maximum
Categories logically grouped with clear labels
Mega menu organizes subcategories with visual hierarchy
Less important links moved to footer or utility navigation
issues.context_notes: Only flag if navigation has 10+ top-level items AND lacks clear organization. Standard 7-9 item navigation is acceptable if well-organized. Do not flag: Mega menus with good categorization, or navigation with clear primary/secondary distinction. Industry context: Large marketplaces may legitimately have more categories. Focus on: Whether navigation is overwhelming, not just number of items.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.issue_title: No clear active state
issues.user_problem: Users don't know where they are
signals_to_detect: Current page menu item not visually distinguished from other navigation items
No color, underline, bold, or highlight indicating which page user is on
Breadcrumb trail absent or not highlighting current location
Page title does not match active navigation item language/style
issues.recommendation: Apply a clear active/current-page state to navigation links using at minimum two visual cues (e.g., bold weight + colour change, or underline + background highlight). Ensure the active state is set programmatically using aria-current='page' for accessibility. The active state must not be removed or obscured by hover styles, and must apply consistently across primary nav, breadcrumbs, and any secondary navigation.
acceptance_criteria: Current page/section link is visually distinct from inactive links using at least 2 visual properties
Active state implemented with aria-current='page' for screen reader support
Active state persists and is not overridden by hover or focus styles
Active state applied consistently in primary nav, mobile nav, and any secondary navigation
Colour difference between active and inactive states meets 3:1 contrast ratio
negative_signals: Clear visual hierarchy with distinct heading sizes
Important content uses larger fonts and bolder weights
Related content visually grouped with whitespace
Call-to-action elements stand out through size and color

issues.issue_title: Missing sorting options
issues.user_problem: Users can’t control product order
signals_to_detect: Product listing page displays no sort options dropdown or buttons
Sort controls hidden in secondary menu instead of prominently displayed with results
Only basic sort available (oldest to newest) without common options (price, relevance, popularity)
No ability to reverse sort order (ascending/descending)
acceptance_criteria: Sort dropdown visible at the top of every PLP without scrolling
Minimum sort options: Relevance, Price Low–High, Price High–Low, Newest, Best Sellers
Selected sort option clearly indicated in the dropdown and in the page state
Sort selection persists across all pages of paginated results
Sort state reflected in the URL query string (e.g., ?sort=price_asc) for bookmark/share support
negative_signals: Sort dropdown offers at least 3 relevant options (Price, Popularity, Newest)
Sort controls prominently displayed above product grid
Sort includes both ascending and descending for price/date
Default sort option clearly indicated
issues.context_notes: Single-category pages with <10 products may not need sorting. B2B sites may prioritize different sorts than B2C. Medical/regulated products may limit sort by price for compliance reasons. Only flag when: PLP has 15+ products AND sort completely absent AND would benefit user decision-making.
issues.recommendation: Add a sort control to all product listing pages with a minimum set of options: Relevance, Price: Low to High, Price: High to Low, Newest Arrivals, and Best Sellers. Place the sort dropdown at the top-right of the product grid, visible without scrolling. Ensure the selected sort option persists across pagination and is reflected in the URL for shareability.

issues.issue_title: Filters reset unexpectedly
issues.user_problem: Users lose applied filters
signals_to_detect: Applied filters (e.g., color=red, price=0-50) disappear after navigating to related page
Filter state not preserved in URL or via page back navigation
User must re-apply filters after clicking individual product or pagination
No indicator or reminder showing filters are active when returning to listings
acceptance_criteria: Applied filters persist when navigating between paginated result pages
Filters persist when using browser back button from a PDP
Filter state stored in URL query string (e.g., ?colour=red&size=M)
Active filters displayed as removable chips or tags above the product grid
'Clear all filters' option visible whenever any filter is active
negative_signals: Applied filters persist when navigating to product and back
Filter state maintained in URL parameters
Browser back button restores previous filter selections
Badge shows active filters when returning to PLP
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filters reset unexpectedly during same session. Do not flag: Filter reset between different sessions (acceptable), or when navigating to unrelated category. Common false positive: Browser back button behavior that's actually browser-standard.
issues.recommendation: Preserve applied filter selections whenever the product grid refreshes, paginated pages are navigated, or the browser back button is used. Store filter state in the URL query string so filters survive page reloads and can be bookmarked or shared. Display a visible 'Clear all filters' and per-filter remove option at the top of the results to give users control.

issues.issue_title: Filter labels unclear
issues.user_problem: Users don’t understand filter meaning
signals_to_detect: Filter labels use jargon or abbreviations (SKU, GTIN, Material Code) instead of common terms
Filter options unclear (e.g., 'Fit Type: A, B, C' without explanation what A/B/C mean)
Filter categories not organized logically (Price before Size, Color below Weight, etc.)
No help text or examples showing what filtering by each option does
acceptance_criteria: All filter labels use plain language a first-time visitor would understand without explanation
No filter label uses internal codes, abbreviations, or jargon
Ambiguous filter options include a tooltip or parenthetical explanation
Most-used filters (price, size, colour) shown expanded by default
Filter labels tested with 5 target users — all can accurately predict what each filter will do
negative_signals: Filter labels use common terms not codes
Filter options clearly describe what they do
Help tooltips available for complex filters
Filter categories organized in logical order
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filter labels are genuinely unclear (codes, abbreviations, jargon). Do not flag: Industry-standard terms (e.g., 'Bluetooth 5.0' for electronics is clear to target audience). Industry context: Technical products may use technical terms appropriately. NEW: Filters that duplicate category navigation reduce clarity and usage. Do not flag: Different organizational schemes that serve distinct purposes. Flag: Filters that create confusion by overlapping with already-prominent category navigation (e.g., 'Occasion' filter when 'Occasions' category exists).
issues.recommendation: Rename all filter labels to use plain customer-facing language. Replace internal codes or ambiguous abbreviations with full descriptive terms. Where a filter option may be misunderstood (e.g., technical specs, material names), add a brief tooltip or helper text. Group filter attributes logically and display the most commonly used filters (price, size, colour) expanded by default.

issues.issue_title: Product images lack zoom/detail
issues.user_problem: Users can’t inspect product properly
signals_to_detect: Product images appear small or pixelated on PDP
Single static image shown without thumbnail gallery or additional views
No zoom functionality available (click to enlarge, magnifying glass, etc.)
Images from different angles or details not provided for product inspection
acceptance_criteria: Desktop: hovering over product image triggers zoom/magnification or a zoom icon is visible
Mobile: pinch-to-zoom functional on all product images
Full-screen lightbox accessible via click/tap on all product images
Minimum 4 product images per SKU including at least one detail and one lifestyle shot
All product images have descriptive alt text (product name + key visual attribute)
negative_signals: Product images clickable to open large view or zoom
Zoom functionality available on hover or click
Multiple images at high resolution provided
360-degree view or video available for complex products
issues.context_notes: Only flag if no way to view product detail (no zoom, single small image, no enlargement). Do not flag: High-res images even without explicit zoom. Industry context: Digital products may not need zoom; physical products typically do.
issues.recommendation: Add a zoom functionality to all product images: on desktop, enable hover-triggered magnification or a click-to-expand full-screen lightbox. On mobile, enable pinch-to-zoom on the image gallery. Ensure the gallery includes at least 4 images per product covering front, back, detail, and lifestyle/in-use angles. Provide alt text for all images.

issues.issue_title: Stock availability unclear
issues.user_problem: Users unsure if item is available
signals_to_detect: Product cards on PLP lack any stock status indicator (no 'In Stock', 'Out of Stock', 'Low Stock' badges)
Stock information inconsistent (some products show status, others don't for no clear reason)
Out-of-stock items displayed without clear unavailability indication or disabled add-to-cart
PDP shows no stock status before user attempts to add to cart
acceptance_criteria: In-stock, low-stock, and out-of-stock states all communicated on PDP before variant selection
Out-of-stock variants visually indicated (greyed out, strikethrough) in the size/colour selector
Low-stock threshold message shown when inventory below 5 units (e.g., 'Only 2 left')
Add to Cart button disabled or replaced with 'Notify Me' for out-of-stock items
Back-in-stock email/SMS notification sign-up available for all out-of-stock products
negative_signals: All product cards consistently show stock status (In Stock, Out of Stock, Low Stock)
Stock availability visible without hovering or clicking
Out-of-stock items clearly marked with Add to Cart disabled
Stock status uses consistent color coding (green=available, red=unavailable)
issues.context_notes: Must test multiple scenarios: (1) In-stock products, (2) Out-of-stock products, (3) Low-stock products. Only flag if: Inconsistent display (some show, some don't) OR out-of-stock items not clearly marked OR completely missing from all products. Do not flag: Consistent 'In Stock' on all available items if out-of-stock products are removed from display or clearly marked. Industry context: Some luxury brands intentionally hide stock levels.

refinement_v3_4.sehaa_finding: Flagged when condition not fully met

issues.recommendation: Display real-time stock availability on the PDP, clearly showing in-stock, low-stock (e.g., 'Only 3 left'), and out-of-stock states before the user selects a variant. Grey out or strike through unavailable size/colour options in the variant selector rather than allowing selection and only revealing unavailability after an Add to Cart attempt. Offer a 'Notify me when back in stock' option for out-of-stock items.

issues.issue_title: Pricing lacks breakdown
issues.user_problem: Users surprised by final cost
signals_to_detect: Product price displayed without showing tax, duty, or shipping fees on PDP
Final cost only revealed at checkout, not in cart summary
No breakdown showing base price vs. taxes vs. shipping before purchase
Discount or promotion applied but final savings amount not clearly calculated
acceptance_criteria: Product price shown on PDP including VAT/tax status (e.g., 'inc. VAT' or 'excl. tax')
Free shipping threshold or estimated shipping cost visible on PDP
Cart page shows: item subtotal, shipping cost, discount, estimated tax, and order total
No new cost lines introduced for the first time during the checkout payment step
Order total on cart matches order total shown throughout the checkout flow
negative_signals: Price breakdown shows subtotal, tax, shipping before checkout
Final price with all fees visible on cart page
Each line item shows individual price and quantity
Currency and VAT/tax inclusion clearly stated
issues.recommendation: Display a full price breakdown at the earliest possible point in the journey — on the PDP, show the base price, any applicable taxes, and the free shipping threshold or shipping cost. On the cart page, show itemised subtotal, shipping cost (or 'Free'), applicable discounts, estimated tax, and the final order total before the user proceeds to checkout.

issues.issue_title: Editable cart items unclear
issues.user_problem: Users don’t know how to update cart
signals_to_detect: Edit quantity or remove buttons for cart items not visible or clearly labeled
Quantity field not easily editable (requires right-click menu, special click, etc.)
Remove/delete option hidden in submenu or requires multiple steps
Cart line items appear uneditable or static without clear affordance
acceptance_criteria: Every cart line item has + and − quantity controls and a Remove/Delete button
Cart subtotal and order total update immediately on quantity change (no page reload)
Quantity cannot be reduced below 1 using the − button (use Remove for deletion)
Low-stock items cap quantity at available stock with a visible explanation
Keyboard users can operate quantity controls and remove items without a mouse
negative_signals: Edit quantity with clearly visible +/- buttons or input field
Remove button visible on each cart item
Edit options accessible without re-adding product
Save for later option available
issues.context_notes: Only flag if edit/remove actions are genuinely hidden or unclear. Do not flag: Standard patterns (trash icon, +/- buttons) even if not labeled. Focus on: Whether average user can modify cart without help.
issues.recommendation: Add clearly visible quantity increment/decrement controls (+ and − buttons) and a remove item button to every line item in the cart. Ensure the cart total updates immediately (without page reload) when quantity is changed. For low-stock items, cap the quantity selector at the available stock count and display a message explaining why the limit exists.

issues.issue_title: Shipping costs revealed late
issues.user_problem: Users abandon due to surprises
signals_to_detect: Cart page shows subtotal but no shipping cost estimate above checkout button
Shipping cost only calculated after entering address at checkout
No visible shipping cost in cart summary or order total
Free shipping threshold not indicated if applicable (e.g., 'Free shipping on orders over $50')
acceptance_criteria: Shipping cost or free shipping status visible on PDP near the Add to Cart button
Cart page shows shipping cost or 'Free shipping' before the Proceed to Checkout CTA
Free shipping threshold displayed if applicable (e.g., 'Add £15 more for free shipping')
Shipping cost does not appear for the first time on the checkout payment step
Postcode/ZIP-based shipping estimator available on cart page for variable-rate shipping
negative_signals: Shipping cost calculated and shown on cart or early in checkout
Shipping calculator available with postal code input
Free shipping threshold clearly displayed
Shipping costs visible before payment information
issues.context_notes: Only flag if shipping cost hidden until final checkout step. Do not flag if: Cost shown on cart page, shipping calculator available, or free shipping clearly stated. Industry context: Some regions require checkout for accurate shipping; flag based on when user learns cost relative to commitment level.
issues.recommendation: Show shipping cost information (or a free shipping confirmation) on the PDP near the Add to Cart button, on the cart page, and at the first step of checkout. Where the exact cost depends on address, display the free shipping threshold and a 'calculate shipping' prompt. Never introduce a shipping cost for the first time on the payment step of checkout.

issues.issue_title: Guest checkout not available
issues.user_problem: Users forced to create accounts
signals_to_detect: Checkout page requires account creation before proceeding with order
No prominent Guest Checkout or Continue as Guest option visible
Guest option buried deep in checkout flow rather than offered upfront
Account creation mandatory with no skip or bypass available
acceptance_criteria: 'Continue as Guest' or 'Guest Checkout' button clearly visible on checkout entry page
Guest option at minimum the same size and visual weight as the Sign In option
Guest checkout completes without requiring password creation at any step
Post-purchase account creation offered but skippable with a single click
Guest order confirmation includes order number and tracking without requiring login
negative_signals: Guest checkout prominently offered as primary option
'Continue as Guest' button equal or larger than account login
Guest checkout doesn't require account creation
Account creation offered after purchase, not forced
issues.context_notes: Only flag if account creation is REQUIRED to complete purchase. Do not flag if: Guest checkout available even if account login is prominent. Industry context: B2B or regulated products (alcohol, pharma) may legitimately require accounts; flag based on industry norms.
issues.recommendation: Add a prominent 'Continue as Guest' option on the checkout entry screen, displayed at equal or greater visual prominence than the 'Sign In' option. Guest checkout should require only email, shipping address, and payment — no password creation. After order completion, offer account creation as an optional step with the password pre-set from the order email.

issues.issue_title: Form fields not grouped logically
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to complete checkout
signals_to_detect: Checkout form displays billing and shipping fields randomly mingled (address line 1, city, billing address, zip, shipping address line 2)
No visual grouping or section headers separating billing, shipping, payment information
Fields not organized in typical flow order (shipping address, billing address, payment)
Form lacks spacing or dividers making sections unclear
acceptance_criteria: Form fields grouped into labelled sections with clear visual separation between groups
Related fields (name, date parts, card number) on the same row with consistent spacing
fieldset and legend elements used for grouped form sections
Each section heading is visually distinct from field labels
Users can scan the form and understand all required information before starting to fill it in
negative_signals: Form fields grouped logically
Related fields visually grouped with borders or spacing
Clear section headings separate different form areas
Logical tab order follows visual grouping
issues.recommendation: Reorganise checkout and account form fields into logical groups separated by clear section headings and visual spacing: e.g., 'Contact Information', 'Delivery Address', 'Payment Details'. Use fieldset and legend elements for grouped fields. Ensure related fields (first name / last name, expiry month / year) sit on the same row with consistent spacing.

issues.issue_title: No inline validation
issues.user_problem: Users discover errors too late
signals_to_detect: Form field errors only shown when user submits entire form, not during entry
No real-time feedback as user types (e.g., email field doesn't check format until blur/submit)
Required fields not marked until user attempts submission
No character count or validation hints as user fills field
acceptance_criteria: Validation triggers on field blur for all form inputs across checkout and account forms
Error message appears directly below or beside the invalid field (not only at page top)
Error messages are specific and instructional, not generic (e.g., 'Invalid input')
Required fields marked with an asterisk (*) before the user begins interacting
Valid fields show a positive confirmation state (green border or tick) after blur
issues.context_notes: Cannot verify from static screenshots. Requires: (1) Video of form interaction, (2) Testing email/phone validation, (3) Observing error timing.
negative_signals: Form fields show validation as user types or on blur
Checkmarks appear when field correctly filled
Error messages appear immediately when user leaves invalid field
Password strength indicator updates in real-time
issues.recommendation: Implement inline validation that triggers on field blur (when the user leaves a field) for all form inputs. Show error messages immediately adjacent to the invalid field with specific guidance on what to correct (e.g., 'Enter a valid UK postcode like SW1A 1AA'). Mark required fields with an asterisk before interaction. Do not wait for full-form submission to surface individual field errors.

issues.issue_title: Primary CTA below the fold on page load
issues.user_problem: Main conversion button not visible without scrolling down initially
signals_to_detect: Complete Checkout or Place Order button located far down page requiring scroll after loading
Primary CTA button not visible in initial viewport on checkout page
Pay Now or Submit Order button positioned below fold on mobile
CTA obscured by sticky elements or overlaid content
acceptance_criteria: Primary CTA visible above the fold on desktop (1280px) without scrolling
Primary CTA visible above the fold on mobile (375px) without scrolling
Long PDPs include a sticky Add to Cart bar that activates after original CTA scrolls out of view
Sticky bar includes product name, price, and Add to Cart button
CTA visible and not obscured by cookie banners, chat widgets, or other sticky elements
negative_signals: Primary CTA visible in initial viewport without scrolling
Add-to-cart or checkout button appears above fold
Mobile layout ensures CTA visible in first screen
Sticky CTA appears if main button scrolls out
issues.context_notes: Only flag if: Primary CTA not visible on initial page load AND no sticky CTA appears when scrolling. Do not flag: Mobile layouts where some scroll expected, or if CTA becomes sticky when main scrolls out. Context: 'Above fold' varies by device; focus on accessibility within first screen.
issues.recommendation: Ensure the primary CTA on every key page is visible above the fold without scrolling on both desktop (1280px) and mobile (375px). On long PDPs, implement a sticky Add to Cart bar that appears after the user scrolls past the original CTA, keeping the purchase action always accessible. Test at common viewport sizes before and after implementation.

issues.issue_title: Security reassurance missing
issues.user_problem: Users doubt payment safety
signals_to_detect: Checkout page lacks trust badges, security icons, or SSL certificate indicators
No reassuring text about payment security (e.g., Your payment is secure, Encrypted, PCI compliant)
Payment section does not display security logos (Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, etc.)
No privacy policy disclosure or data protection statement near payment form
DATA SHARING: Third-party integrations don't clarify what data is shared and privacy protections
acceptance_criteria: Site served over HTTPS with browser padlock visible on all pages
Payment security badge(s) visible adjacent to the payment form in checkout
Reassurance copy (e.g., 'Secure checkout' or 'SSL encrypted') visible on the payment step
Trust signals (security badge + returns guarantee) visible on the cart page
No security-related browser warnings on any page of the checkout flow
negative_signals: Security badges visible on checkout
Trust indicators shown near payment input fields
Privacy policy link clearly available during checkout
Secure connection emphasized
issues.context_notes: Only flag if security reassurance genuinely absent on checkout pages. Do not flag: Implicit HTTPS indicators or standard payment form patterns. Focus on: Whether users are reassured during the most sensitive part of the transaction. NEW: When third-party services are integrated (WhatsApp, Maps, social platforms), users need privacy reassurance. Include clear statements like 'Your location is never shared with the sender' or 'We'll only contact recipient for delivery confirmation.' Industry context: Regional markets (GCC) may use WhatsApp for delivery - privacy clarity is critical.
issues.recommendation: Add visible security and trust signals throughout the checkout flow: SSL/padlock indicator in the browser, payment security badges (Verified by Visa, Mastercard SecureCode, Norton Secured) near the payment form, and a brief reassurance statement (e.g., 'Your payment is encrypted and secure'). Repeat trust signals on the cart page to reduce anxiety before checkout entry.

issues.issue_title: Password requirements unclear or missing
issues.user_problem: Users don't know password rules, leading to weak passwords or frustration
signals_to_detect: Password creation field shows no guidance on requirements (length, special chars, numbers)
Requirements text appears only AFTER entering password instead of upfront
No met/unmet validation checklist (✓ 8 characters, ✗ Special character needed, etc.)
Password meter or strength indicator absent
acceptance_criteria: Password requirements listed below the field before any interaction
Requirements written in plain language with specific examples
Real-time strength indicator updates as the user types
Show/hide password toggle (eye icon) present on all password fields
Confirmation field validates match in real time and shows a tick when passwords match
negative_signals: Password requirements shown next to password field
Real-time validation shows which requirements are met
Requirements displayed as checklist
Password strength meter visible as user types
issues.context_notes: Flag even if password requirements are shown only post-error — best practice is requirements visible before or during input. Do not flag if a real-time checklist (✓/✗ per rule) is present. Industry context: B2B and fintech registration flows where failed attempts erode trust in a financial or compliance platform require especially clear upfront guidance. Blocking users at password creation is a critical friction point in high-trust product categories.
issues.recommendation: Display password requirements visibly below the password field before the user begins typing — not only after a failed attempt. Show requirements in plain language (e.g., 'At least 8 characters, one number, and one uppercase letter'). Add a real-time strength indicator (weak / medium / strong progress bar) that updates as the user types. Include a show/hide password toggle on all password fields.

issues.issue_title: Insufficient colour contrast
issues.user_problem: Text and UI elements are difficult to read for users with low vision or colour blindness
signals_to_detect: Body text on white/light background uses light grey colour (e.g. #999, #aaa) that fails 4.5:1 ratio
CTA button label colour does not meet contrast ratio against button fill colour
Placeholder text in form fields too faint to read comfortably
Coloured text on coloured background (e.g. white text on light blue) used for key content
Data visualisation uses colour combinations that are indistinguishable for colour-blind users
acceptance_criteria: All body text under 18px achieves minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background colour
All large text (18px+ regular or 14px+ bold) achieves minimum 3:1 contrast ratio
CTA button label text passes contrast ratio against the button fill colour on all states (default, hover, disabled)
Placeholder text in form fields meets minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Axe or WAVE automated accessibility audit shows zero colour contrast violations across all key page types
negative_signals: Body text passes 4.5:1 contrast ratio verified by WebAIM Contrast Checker
Button labels pass contrast check on all interactive states
Placeholder and hint text meets 4.5:1 minimum
No colour contrast violations flagged by Axe browser extension on homepage, PLP, PDP, and checkout
issues.recommendation: Audit all text and background colour combinations using WebAIM Contrast Checker or the Axe browser extension. Update every failing combination to meet WCAG 2.1 AA minimums: 4.5:1 for body text (under 18px regular or 14px bold), 3:1 for large text and UI components (borders, icons). Pay particular attention to light grey body copy, placeholder text, disabled states, and data visualisation colour pairs. Document all passing colour combinations in the design system to prevent regression.
issues.context_notes: Run Axe browser extension on each key page type. Do not flag: Decorative or purely visual elements with no informational value. Industry context: Colour contrast failures affect 8%+ of users globally with colour vision deficiency. WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is a legal requirement in many jurisdictions. Focus on: Body copy, navigation text, CTA buttons, and form field labels first.

issues.issue_title: Horizontal scrolling issues
issues.user_problem: Content overflows screen
signals_to_detect: Content or layout extends beyond screen width on mobile, requiring horizontal scroll
Images or tables overflow viewport without responsive scaling
Navigation menu does not adapt to mobile (still wide desktop layout)
Form fields or buttons too wide for mobile screen
acceptance_criteria: No horizontal scrollbar appears at 375px viewport width on any page type
No content is clipped or cut off at the right edge on mobile
All images have max-width: 100% applied so they scale to their container
Tables on mobile are scrollable horizontally within a wrapper (not causing page-level scroll)
document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals window.innerWidth at 375px (verified in browser console)
negative_signals: All content fits within viewport width without horizontal scroll
Images and containers scale to screen size
Tables responsive or scrollable within container
No fixed-width elements exceeding viewport
issues.recommendation: Audit the site at 375px viewport width for any element causing horizontal overflow. Common causes include: fixed-width containers, images without max-width: 100%, tables wider than their container, and absolute-positioned elements with large left/right values. Apply overflow-x: hidden on the body only as a last resort — fix the root cause of each overflow individually.

issues.issue_title: Primary CTAs too small on mobile
issues.user_problem: Critical conversion buttons are undersized for mobile touch interaction
signals_to_detect: Button with less than 44px height or width on mobile viewport
Primary CTA missing adequate padding or spacing from other elements
Add-to-cart or checkout button appears cramped or overlaps other controls
Mobile view shows button smaller than recommended 44x44 touch target
issues.recommendation: Increase the size and tap target area of all primary CTAs on mobile to a minimum height of 48px (preferably 56px for prominent actions like Add to Cart and Checkout). Use full-width buttons for primary mobile CTAs where layout allows. Ensure at least 12px vertical spacing between stacked CTAs to prevent accidental double-taps.
acceptance_criteria: All primary CTAs on mobile have a minimum height of 48px
Add to Cart and Checkout CTAs are full-width on mobile (375px)
At least 12px vertical gap between stacked CTA buttons on mobile
All CTAs meet the 44x44px minimum tap target standard including padding
No CTA is obscured by the mobile browser's bottom navigation bar or safe-area insets
negative_signals: Primary CTAs (Add to Cart, Checkout, Buy Now) are minimum 44x44px on mobile
Conversion buttons have adequate padding and spacing from other elements
Critical action buttons sized appropriately for thumb-friendly interaction
Mobile CTAs meet accessibility guidelines for touch targets
issues.context_notes: Critical conversion buttons (Add to Cart, Checkout, Buy Now) must be minimum 44x44px on mobile. Do not flag: Desktop sizing, buttons that expand on tap, or adequate spacing prevents mis-taps. Industry context: Touch target requirements are accessibility standard, not opinion.

issues.issue_title: Slow perceived load
issues.user_problem: Users think site is broken
signals_to_detect: No loading indicator spinner or progress bar visible during page load
No skeleton screens or placeholder content shown while loading
Long delay before main content appears without any feedback
Loading animation missing from above-the-fold content area
issues.recommendation: Implement skeleton screens or content placeholder animations for all sections that load asynchronously (product grids, personalised recommendations, reviews). Show a progress bar or loading spinner for actions that take longer than 1 second to complete (form submissions, payment processing, search). Provide estimated wait times for actions that consistently take over 3 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Skeleton screens or placeholder animations shown for all async-loaded content sections
Spinner or progress indicator shown for any action taking over 1 second
Loading state triggered immediately on user action (no delay before feedback appears)
Estimated wait time or progress percentage shown for actions taking over 3 seconds
No blank white sections visible during page load — placeholders maintain layout
negative_signals: Page loads to usable state within 3 seconds
Critical content appears before non-critical elements
Loading skeleton screens show where content will appear
Progressive enhancement loads secondary content after primary

issues.issue_title: No loading indicators
issues.user_problem: Users unsure system is responding
signals_to_detect: Search results or filtered list returns without spinner element
Form submission completes without loading state indicator
Ajax requests show no visual feedback during processing
Content loads dynamically with no progress indicator shown
issues.recommendation: Add explicit loading indicators for all asynchronous operations: a spinner or animation for data fetches, a 'Processing...' state on buttons during form submission (button disabled + label change), and a progress bar for multi-step async operations like file uploads. Ensure the loading state is visible, accessible (aria-live region), and dismisses cleanly when the operation completes.
acceptance_criteria: Buttons enter a loading state (disabled + loading label or spinner) immediately on click
Page sections that load data asynchronously show a spinner or skeleton until data arrives
aria-live region announces loading state changes to screen readers
Loading indicators dismiss cleanly when content loads — no lingering spinners
Button loading state prevents duplicate submissions (button non-interactive while processing)
negative_signals: Spinner or loading animation appears during async operations
Button shows loading state when clicked
Progress indicator for multi-step operations
Skeleton screens show during content loading

issues.issue_title: Missing focus states
issues.user_problem: Keyboard users lose context
signals_to_detect: Interactive elements lack visible outline or border when focused
No color change or visual indicator on focused button or link
Focus ring completely hidden or removed via CSS outline none
Keyboard navigation makes header navigation lose visible focus state
issues.recommendation: Restore visible focus indicators on all interactive elements by removing any CSS rule that sets outline: none or outline: 0 globally. Replace the default browser focus ring with a custom high-visibility focus style (2px solid brand colour or 2px offset outline) that meets WCAG 2.2 requirements. Test by tabbing through every page and confirming focus is always visible and never hidden.
acceptance_criteria: Visible focus ring present on all interactive elements when navigated to by keyboard
Focus indicator meets WCAG 2.2 minimum: 2px solid with 3:1 contrast against adjacent colour
No global outline: none or outline: 0 CSS rules removing focus styles
Focus style is distinct from hover style so keyboard and pointer states are distinguishable
Full page navigation by Tab key shows a continuously visible, moving focus indicator
negative_signals: Forms auto-save draft data every 30-60 seconds
Browser remembers form data if user navigates away
Warning shown before losing unsaved changes
Return to saved progress option available

issues.issue_title: Images missing alt text
issues.user_problem: Screen reader users miss context
signals_to_detect: Product images in PDP or PLP have empty alt attributes
Decorative images lacking role=presentation or aria-hidden
Hero image or banner lacks descriptive alt text
Category or product thumbnail missing alt description
issues.recommendation: Add descriptive alt text to all meaningful images across the site. Alt text should describe the image content specifically and be useful to someone who cannot see it (e.g., 'Navy wool overcoat, front view, worn by model' not 'product image'). Purely decorative images should have an empty alt attribute (alt='') so screen readers skip them. Audit using an accessibility tool and check for empty, missing, or generic alt attributes.
acceptance_criteria: All product images have descriptive alt text including product name and key visual attribute
Decorative images use empty alt attribute (alt='')
No image has missing, null, or generic alt text ('image', 'photo', 'IMG_001')
Banner and promotional images include the full text content of any text displayed in the image
Axe or WAVE audit shows zero 'Image alternative text' violations across all page types
negative_signals: All images have descriptive alt attributes
Alt text describes image content and context
Decorative images have empty alt or marked decorative
Complex images include longer descriptions
issues.context_notes: Only flag missing alt text on functional images. Do not flag: Decorative images with empty alt. Industry context: Accessibility requirement, not opinion. Focus on: Screen reader usability.

issues.issue_title: Jargon-heavy copy
issues.user_problem: Users don't understand terminology
signals_to_detect: Product description uses technical specifications without layman explanation
Form labels use domain jargon unfamiliar to general users
Error message contains technical terminology without plain language
Feature explanation uses industry acronyms or terms without definition
Required fields or form inputs use legal/regulatory terminology unfamiliar to the user's role (e.g., 'UBO', 'List of Ultimate Beneficial Owners') without inline explanation or help link
issues.recommendation: Conduct a copy audit across all key page types and replace technical jargon, industry abbreviations, and internal terminology with plain-language equivalents that match the vocabulary your target customers use. Use the Hemingway App or Flesch-Kincaid readability test to benchmark content. Establish a plain-language writing guide and apply it to all future content.
acceptance_criteria: All body copy reads at a Flesch-Kincaid grade level appropriate for the target audience (grade 8–10 for general retail)
No unexplained acronyms, abbreviations, or technical terms in user-facing copy
Product descriptions avoid internal SKU codes, supplier jargon, or manufacturing terminology
Error messages and system notifications written in conversational, plain language
Plain-language style guide created and available to all content contributors
negative_signals: Important content accessible with keyboard
Focus indicators visible on all interactive elements
Skip navigation link available
Dropdowns and modals operable without mouse

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent terminology
issues.user_problem: Same concept named differently
signals_to_detect: Navigation uses both product and item to describe same concept
Headers reference shopping cart on one page and cart summary on another
Button labels vary (Save vs Store, Buy vs Purchase) for same action
Footer links use different terminology than header for same destination
issues.recommendation: Audit all user-facing terminology for consistency — identify all variations of the same concept (e.g., 'basket' vs 'cart', 'checkout' vs 'purchase', 'account' vs 'profile') and standardise to a single term throughout the interface, emails, error messages, and support documentation. Document the approved terminology in a content style guide.
acceptance_criteria: Single consistent term used for each key concept site-wide (cart/basket, account/profile, etc.)
Terminology consistent across UI, transactional emails, error messages, and help content
Content style guide documenting approved terminology created and shared with all contributors
No conflicting terms used for the same action on the same page or within the same journey
Navigation labels, CTA text, and page headings use the same term for the same destination
negative_signals: Same concept uses same term throughout site
UI labels match menu labels match page titles
Action verbs consistent
Terminology guide followed

issues.issue_title: Weak error recovery and dead-end handling
issues.user_problem: When something goes wrong (error, unavailable option, failed action), users don’t know what to do next and feel stuck.
signals_to_detect: Error message lacks actionable recovery instructions or next steps
Error modal or alert shows problem but no solution or retry button
Failed transaction leaves user stuck without clear back navigation
Form error only highlights field but doesn't explain how to fix it
issues.recommendation: Design all error and empty states to offer at least two recovery pathways: a primary action (retry, go back, search again) and a secondary fallback (homepage link, popular categories, or contact support). Write error copy that explains what happened and what the user should do next. Test each error state to confirm it renders correctly and never shows a blank or broken UI.
acceptance_criteria: All error states include a clear explanation of what went wrong in plain language
Every error state offers at least one primary recovery action (retry or alternative path)
A secondary fallback (homepage, popular categories, or support link) present on all error pages
No error state renders as a blank page or broken layout
Error copy reviewed for tone — empathetic and action-oriented, never blaming the user
negative_signals: Errors include actionable next steps or retry buttons
Alternative options offered when primary path fails
Contact support easily accessible from error states
Clear path back to working state provided
