issues.context_notes: Only flag genuine dead-ends (error with no recovery path). Do not flag: Errors with back button, contact option, or obvious recovery. Focus on: Whether user has ANY way forward from error state.

issues.issue_title: Insufficient system feedback during multi-step actions
issues.user_problem: Users aren’t sure whether the system is processing their action, causing anxiety and abandonment.
signals_to_detect: Progress indicator or step counter missing during checkout process
Submit button shows no loading state or disabled state when processing
Form submission lacks spinner or visual indication during processing
Multi-step flow lacks visual progress bar or breadcrumb navigation
issues.recommendation: Implement immediate system feedback for every user-initiated action: disable and update the label of submit buttons during processing (e.g., 'Placing order…'), show step-completion confirmations in multi-step flows, and use aria-live regions to announce status changes to screen readers. For actions taking over 2 seconds, show a progress indicator with an estimated completion state.
acceptance_criteria: Submit/confirm buttons enter a disabled loading state immediately on click
Multi-step flows show which steps are complete, in-progress, and pending
Status changes announced to screen readers via aria-live regions
Actions taking over 2 seconds display a progress indicator or estimated time
Completion of each step confirmed visually (e.g., green tick, success message) before advancing
negative_signals: Loading states, confirmations, and processing feedback provided
User knows system is working
Multi-step actions show which step is in progress
Completion confirmation appears after action finishes
issues.context_notes: Only flag if feedback is genuinely absent during clearly multi-step processes. Do not flag: Single-step actions, instant responses, or flows where step count is obvious. Focus on: Whether user knows where they are and what happens next. NEW (B2B/SaaS workflows): In multi-party approval flows, 'submitted' is not the end state — the system must communicate what the next step is, who owns it, and how the current user will be notified. A simple success toast is insufficient when further action from another party is required.

issues.issue_title: Poor expectation setting before irreversible actions
issues.user_problem: Users commit to an action without understanding prerequisites, constraints, or consequences, leading to surprise and frustration.
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and the real world
signals_to_detect: Booking or purchase button lacks clear terms or cancellation policy link
Checkout submit button missing warning about non-refundable charges
Irreversible action triggered without confirmation dialog or summary
Booking date/time selection unclear about timezone or availability constraints
REQUIRED ACTIONS: Multi-step processes don't show what's required before proceeding
issues.recommendation: Add a confirmation step or clear pre-action summary before all irreversible or high-consequence actions (order placement, account deletion, unsubscribe, address removal). The summary should show the key details and consequences, and require an explicit confirmation click. For destructive actions, use a confirmation modal with a clearly labelled destructive action button (e.g., 'Yes, delete my account') separate from a cancel option.
acceptance_criteria: All irreversible actions require an explicit confirmation step before executing
Confirmation step shows a summary of what will happen (e.g., what will be deleted, what will be charged)
Destructive action button labelled specifically (e.g., 'Delete account' not just 'Confirm')
A clear Cancel option present on all confirmation dialogs
Confirmation modal dismissible via Escape key and clicking outside the modal
negative_signals: Actions with consequences show preview or confirmation
Irreversible actions require explicit confirmation
Prerequisites clearly stated before action button
Warning messages explain what will happen
issues.context_notes: Only flag irreversible actions without ANY confirmation. Do not flag: Delete with undo option, or consequence is obvious. Industry context: Bulk actions, payments, deletions should require confirmation. Focus on: Risk level of action. NEW: For multi-step configurations (bundles, custom products), use prompts/tooltips/highlights to show users what's required before they can proceed. Don't just disable buttons - explain why and what's needed.

issues.issue_title: Mismatch between explanatory content and interaction behavior
issues.user_problem: What the UI says (help text/FAQs/tooltips) doesn't match what actually happens, causing confusion or distrust.
signals_to_detect: Help text mentions free shipping but checkout shows shipping charges
Label says optional but form validation requires the field
Tooltip promises real-time updates but feature works with delay
FAQ describes process different from actual implementation in UI
issues.recommendation: Audit all instructional copy, help text, and tooltips against the actual user journey to identify mismatches. Update any guidance that describes a different flow, uses outdated terminology, or sets false expectations about what the next step involves. Assign content ownership so that copy is reviewed and updated whenever the underlying feature or flow changes.
acceptance_criteria: All instructional copy accurately describes the current UI flow and outcome
No help text references UI elements, steps, or labels that no longer exist
Tooltips and inline guidance reviewed and approved as part of any feature change process
Content review checklist includes a 'Does the copy match the current experience?' sign-off step
Users testing 5 key journeys can follow on-screen guidance without confusion or contradiction
negative_signals: Help text accurately describes what happens
FAQs match actual system behavior
Tooltips provide accurate information
Examples reflect current UI

issues.issue_title: Weak post-action reassurance and next-step clarity
issues.user_problem: After completing an action, users aren't clearly told what happened or what to do next, increasing uncertainty and repeat actions.
signals_to_detect: Confirmation page lacks order number or clear confirmation message
Post-checkout page shows no next steps like tracking, account, or email receipt
Order complete page missing email confirmation or download receipt link
Confirmation missing guidance on when product will arrive or booking confirmed
After submitting for approval, no indication of who the next approver is or expected timeline
Workflow completion state (submitted, pending, approved) doesn't clarify what the current user should do or expect next
No email confirmation triggered after high-stakes B2B actions (off-boarding, transaction initiation, simulation approval)
issues.recommendation: Design post-action confirmation states for all key user actions: after checkout show an order confirmation with order number, summary, and delivery estimate; after form submission show a success message with next steps; after account creation show a welcome screen with immediate value. Always tell the user what just happened, confirm it worked, and explain what happens next.
acceptance_criteria: Order confirmation page shows order number, item summary, delivery estimate, and next steps
Form submission success states explain what the user can expect next (e.g., 'We'll email you within 24 hours')
Account creation success screen provides immediate onboarding value or next action
All confirmation states visible without scrolling on mobile (375px)
Confirmation emails sent within 5 minutes of the action and contain the same key information as the on-screen confirmation
negative_signals: Success confirmation message appears after action
Next steps clearly indicated
Clear path to continue journey
Confirmation includes summary of what was accomplished
issues.context_notes: Only flag if post-action state genuinely leaves users uncertain about outcome or next steps. Do not flag: Simple confirmations for low-stakes actions. Focus on: Whether user is reassured and oriented after completing a meaningful action. NEW (B2B/SaaS): Applies to workflow completions beyond e-commerce — after submitting for approval, initiating a financial transaction, or completing a multi-department handoff. Users must know what happened, what happens next, and who is responsible.

issues.issue_title: Disabled search button forcing keyboard entry
issues.user_problem: Users cannot submit search by clicking button, forced to use keyboard
signals_to_detect: Search button appears disabled or grayed out until text is entered
Search magnifying glass icon button lacks click handler
Submit button missing from search form, requiring only Enter key
Search button grayed out with cursor-not-allowed appearing on hover
issues.recommendation: Ensure the search submit button responds to both mouse clicks and keyboard Enter key presses. The search input field should also trigger a search on Enter key. Remove any JavaScript that disables the search button before sufficient characters are entered — instead, validate on submission and show a helpful inline message if the query is too short.
acceptance_criteria: Search triggers correctly on Enter key press within the search input field
Search submit button responds to mouse click, keyboard Enter, and Space key
Search button never disabled in a way that prevents keyboard-only users from submitting
If query is too short, an inline validation message explains the minimum length
No JavaScript error thrown when search is submitted via keyboard
negative_signals: Search button functional and clickable at all times
Both button click and Enter key submit search
Search icon button has clear hover/focus state
Empty search handled gracefully
issues.context_notes: Only flag if search button completely non-functional. Do not flag: Search that works via Enter key, or button that triggers on input focus. Common false positive: Styling that looks disabled but button actually works.

issues.issue_title: No spelling suggestions or error handling in search
issues.user_problem: Users receive no feedback when search terms are misspelled
signals_to_detect: No zero results message or suggestion when query returns no matches
Search missing Did you mean or autocorrect for misspelled terms
Empty search results page without related searches or trending terms
Misspelled query fails to return corrected suggestions or alternatives
issues.recommendation: Add spelling correction and typo tolerance to the search engine so that common misspellings still return relevant results. Show a 'Did you mean X?' suggestion above results when a correction was applied. On zero-results pages caused by misspelling, show the corrected search suggestion prominently rather than returning an empty page. Use fuzzy matching or phonetic matching as a fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Common single-character misspellings return relevant results or a 'Did you mean?' suggestion
'Did you mean [corrected term]?' shown above results when a correction is applied
Zero-results pages caused by misspelling show the corrected suggestion as a CTA
Fuzzy or phonetic matching active for product names with common alternate spellings
Search analytics monitored for high-volume no-results queries to identify gaps in tolerance
negative_signals: 'Did you mean' suggestions appear for misspelled searches
Zero results page offers corrected spelling alternatives
Similar search terms suggested
Related categories shown on no results
issues.context_notes: Only flag zero-results pages with no helpful alternatives. Do not flag: Sites with small catalogs where misspelling suggestions aren't feasible. Focus on: Whether user has path forward after no results.

issues.issue_title: Search bar occupies excessive screen space
issues.user_problem: Search element takes up too much real estate, cluttering navigation
signals_to_detect: Search input field takes up more than 50% of header or navigation bar width
Search bar doesn't collapse or resize on mobile viewports below 480px
Search functionality not accessible via icon-only button on mobile
Search bar remains full-width even when header needs space for other elements
issues.recommendation: Constrain the search bar width so it occupies no more than 40% of the header width on desktop and does not push other header elements (logo, cart, account) into overflow or wrapping. On mobile, replace the visible search bar with a search icon that opens a full-screen overlay to maximise available space. Ensure the search bar height matches other header elements for visual consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop search bar occupies no more than 40% of header width
Search bar does not cause header elements to wrap or overflow at any standard viewport width
Mobile header shows a search icon, not a full visible input bar
Search bar height consistent with other header navigation elements
Header layout tested at 320px, 375px, 768px, 1024px, and 1280px without layout breakage
negative_signals: Search bar proportionate to header space
Search collapses to icon on mobile
Search size balanced with other header elements
Compact search design doesn't dominate
issues.context_notes: Only flag if search genuinely dominates header (>50% width) and crowds out other elements. Do not flag: Prominent but proportionate search, or search that's primary site function. Industry context: Search-heavy sites (marketplaces) may legitimately emphasize search.

issues.issue_title: Limited filter categories without count previews
issues.user_problem: Users cannot see how many results each filter option will return
signals_to_detect: Filter options lack count in parentheses showing matching results
Price filter missing range indicator or min/max values
Category filter shows no indication of product count per category
Availability filter omits number of available vs unavailable items
issues.recommendation: Display a result count in parentheses next to each filter option showing how many products match that filter given current selections (e.g., 'Blue (24)'). Update these counts dynamically as other filters are applied so users can see which combinations will yield results before committing. Hide or grey out filter options with zero matching results to prevent dead-end filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Result count shown in parentheses next to every filter option
Counts update dynamically as additional filters are applied or removed
Filter options with zero results are hidden or visually disabled (greyed out)
Count updates happen without a full page reload (AJAX or client-side filtering)
Counts accurate — not showing stale or approximate values
negative_signals: Filter options show result counts in parentheses (e.g., 'Blue (24)')
Price filter displays min-max range of available products
Disabled filter options indicate no results or are hidden
Filter counts update dynamically as filters are applied
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filter counts completely absent AND would help user decision. Do not flag: Small catalogs (<50 products), filters where counts don't add value (color options), or when counts load progressively. Focus on: User benefit of count information. NEW: Users often want SORT options (price low-high, popularity) more than FILTER counts. If sort is missing but filters have counts, prioritize adding sort. Focus on: Whether users can effectively narrow/organize results, not just whether counts are shown.

issues.issue_title: Counterproductive sort options
issues.user_problem: Sort options like 'lowest rating' may reduce trust and conversion
signals_to_detect: Sort dropdown offers Lowest Rating or Worst Reviewed option
Sort options include Most Returns or Highest Complaints
Product list sortable by negative attributes instead of positive traits
Sort menu shows options that highlight poor quality rankings
issues.recommendation: Audit sort options and remove or rename any that are confusing or unhelpful (e.g., 'Position', 'ID', or technical sort keys). Ensure sort options are labelled from the user's perspective (e.g., 'Price: Low to High' not 'Price ascending'). Default sort should be 'Relevance' or 'Best Sellers' depending on context — never an arbitrary technical default.
acceptance_criteria: All sort option labels written from the user's perspective (e.g., 'Price: Low to High')
No technical or internal sort keys exposed in the dropdown (e.g., 'Position', 'ID', 'SKU')
Default sort set to Relevance (for search results) or Best Sellers (for category pages)
Sort options consistent across all PLPs — same options in same order on every listing page
Sort option labels tested with 5 users who can predict sort behaviour from the label alone
negative_signals: Sort options focus on positive attributes
Negative sort options clearly labeled if present
Default sort is quality-focused
Options prioritize customer benefit
issues.context_notes: Only flag if negative sort options are default or prominently featured. Do not flag: Presence of 'Low to High' price sort (this is useful). Flag: 'Lowest Rated', 'Most Returns', 'Worst Reviewed' sorts that highlight poor products. Context: Academic/research sites may legitimately need all sort options.

issues.issue_title: Cannot deselect filter options once selected
issues.user_problem: Users cannot remove single filter selections without clearing all
signals_to_detect: Filter checkbox remains checked with no way to uncheck individually
Only Clear All button available to remove filters
Selected filter chips lack X button to remove single selections
Filter appears selected but clicking again does not deselect it
issues.recommendation: Enable deselection of active filters by clicking on the active filter option a second time, by clicking an X icon on the active filter chip displayed above the results, or by using a 'Remove' control within the filter panel. Ensure users can remove individual filters without clearing all filters at once. Applied filters should be clearly visible as removable chips above or alongside the product grid.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking an already-selected filter option deselects it
Active filters displayed as removable chips above the product grid
Each active filter chip has an X or Remove button that removes only that filter
'Clear all filters' option available when 2 or more filters are active
Deselecting a filter updates the product grid without a full page reload
negative_signals: Filter checkboxes can be clicked again to deselect
Selected filters shown as removable chips with X buttons
Radio filters include 'Any' or 'All' option to clear selection
Each active filter has individual remove option
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filters are one-way (can apply but cannot remove individually). Do not flag: Radio buttons (one selection by design), or if 'Clear All' is acceptable pattern for simple filters. Focus on: Whether user can modify selections without starting over.

issues.issue_title: Icon-only filters without text labels
issues.user_problem: Users must guess what filter icons represent
signals_to_detect: Filter section shows only icons without accompanying text label
Price range filter lacks From / To labels on input fields
Size or color filter appears as icons only without tooltip on hover
Sorting option represented by arrow icon without descriptive text
issues.recommendation: Add visible text labels alongside all icon-only filter controls. For icon-based filter categories (e.g., a size icon, a colour palette icon), display the filter category name as a text label either always-visible or on hover for desktop, and always-visible on mobile. Ensure every filter option is identifiable without relying on the icon alone.
acceptance_criteria: All filter category icons accompanied by a visible text label on desktop
Text labels always visible alongside filter icons on mobile (no hover required)
Icon + label combinations used consistently across all filter panels site-wide
Filter labels pass a recognition test — 5 users can identify each filter's purpose without instruction
aria-label attributes present on all icon-only filter elements for screen reader accessibility
negative_signals: Filter options include text labels alongside icons
Icon meanings follow universal conventions
Tooltips appear on hover explaining icons
Screen readers can interpret filters
issues.context_notes: Only flag icon-only filters that are genuinely ambiguous. Do not flag: Universal icons (star for rating, $ for price) or when tooltips clarify. Industry context: Fashion sites may use color swatches (acceptable), technical sites need text labels.

issues.issue_title: Missing country code prefix for phone input
issues.user_problem: Users unclear on phone number format, especially international users
signals_to_detect: Phone input field lacks placeholder showing format like +1 (555) 123-4567
No country code dropdown or prefix selector before phone number input
Phone field validation rejects international numbers without country code
Help text or example absent explaining phone format requirements
issues.recommendation: Add a country code prefix selector (dropdown or auto-detected flag + code) before the phone number input field on all forms that collect phone numbers. The default should reflect the user's detected or selected country. Include a placeholder or helper text showing the expected format for the selected country (e.g., '+44 7700 900123'). Ensure the country code and phone number are submitted together as a valid international number.
acceptance_criteria: Country code selector present before the phone number input field on all phone-collecting forms
Default country code matches the user's selected shipping country or detected locale
Placeholder text shows expected format for the selected country code
Country code updates automatically when the user changes their country selection
Submitted phone number combines country code and local number as a valid international format
negative_signals: Country code prefix updates automatically when country selected
Phone field includes integrated country selector
Single country selector controls both shipping and phone
Default country code matches selected country
issues.context_notes: Only flag actual mismatches (selected country code doesn't match phone prefix). Do not flag: Working dynamic updates, or static fields for single-market sites. Industry context: Common in international checkouts. Focus on: Whether country and phone code are synchronized.

issues.issue_title: Confusing visual similarity between menu and breadcrumbs
issues.user_problem: Users confuse navigation menu with breadcrumb trail due to similar appearance
signals_to_detect: Breadcrumbs and navigation menu use identical styling
Both breadcrumbs and menu lack visual differentiation like color or typography
Menu expandable indicators and breadcrumb separators visually indistinguishable
Hover states on breadcrumbs identical to hover states on navigation items
issues.recommendation: Apply visually distinct styling to the main navigation menu and breadcrumb trail so they cannot be confused with one another. Use differentiated typography (size, weight, colour), position (header vs below-hero), and layout (horizontal block vs slash-separated trail) to make each element's purpose immediately clear. Ensure breadcrumbs use a smaller, lighter treatment than primary navigation.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation menu and breadcrumb trail use visually distinct font sizes and weights
Breadcrumbs positioned consistently below the hero/banner, not adjacent to the main navigation
Breadcrumb separator (/ or >) clearly distinguishes it from menu link styling
5 users shown both elements simultaneously can identify which is the navigation and which is the breadcrumb without instruction
Both elements maintain visual distinction across all breakpoints (desktop, tablet, mobile)
negative_signals: Breadcrumbs styled distinctly from navigation
Navigation menu clearly separated from breadcrumb
Breadcrumbs use separator, navigation uses buttons
Visual hierarchy makes breadcrumb secondary
issues.context_notes: Only flag if breadcrumbs and navigation are genuinely confusing (same styling, position). Do not flag: Similar-ish styling if clear contextually. Focus on: Whether user can distinguish navigation from location trail.

issues.issue_title: Auto-advancing carousel with poor usability
issues.user_problem: Rotating carousel content advances before users can read it, and lacks clear navigation controls or end indicators
signals_to_detect: Hero or content carousel auto-advances without user interaction
Carousel slides advance faster than 5 seconds, before text is readable
No pause/stop control visible on auto-advancing carousel
Navigation dots or arrow controls missing, too small, or overlapping carousel content
No visual indicator showing which slide the user is on or how many slides exist
Carousel continues showing navigation arrows even when all items fit without scrolling
issues.recommendation: Disable carousel auto-rotation or set a minimum 6-second interval with a visible pause/play control. Add clearly visible dot indicators showing current position and total slide count. Ensure navigation arrows are only shown when there are more items than the visible viewport can display. Set arrow touch targets to minimum 44x44px and position them so they do not overlap content text. Respect the prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query to disable animation for users who have opted out of motion.
acceptance_criteria: Carousel does not auto-advance, or advances after a minimum 6-second interval
A pause/play control is visible and functional for any auto-advancing carousel
Dot indicators show current slide position and total number of slides
Navigation arrows are hidden when all carousel items fit within the visible container without scrolling
Arrow and dot controls meet 44x44px minimum tap target and do not overlap slide text content
prefers-reduced-motion media query disables or halts all carousel animation
negative_signals: Carousel does not auto-advance or has pause control
Dot indicators and arrows clearly show position and slide count
Arrows hidden when no overflow exists
All navigation controls accessible and not overlapping content
Motion respects OS reduced-motion preference
issues.context_notes: Check both homepage hero carousels and product carousels on PLPs. Do not flag: Static image galleries with manual-only navigation. Industry context: Auto-advancing carousels are a well-documented UX anti-pattern — static hero or 2-slide-max with manual control is preferred. Flag both the auto-advance issue and the missing end/position indicator as part of the same finding.

issues.issue_title: Missing breadcrumbs for navigation
issues.user_problem: Users cannot easily track their location or navigate back through hierarchy
signals_to_detect: No breadcrumbs visible on category or product detail pages
Breadcrumbs present only on some pages but not others
Breadcrumb links non-clickable or inactive for navigation
Multi-level page hierarchy lacks breadcrumb trail showing path
issues.recommendation: Implement breadcrumb navigation on all pages that are two or more levels below the homepage. Each breadcrumb segment must be a clickable link to the corresponding parent page, with the current page shown as plain text (non-linked) at the end. Use schema.org BreadcrumbList structured data to enable breadcrumb display in search results. Position breadcrumbs consistently below the header and above the page title.
acceptance_criteria: Breadcrumbs present on all pages 2+ levels from homepage (category, product, article pages)
Each intermediate breadcrumb is a working link to the correct parent page
Current page shown as the final non-linked breadcrumb item
Breadcrumbs positioned above the page title on all templates
schema.org BreadcrumbList markup present and validated in Google's Rich Results Test
negative_signals: Breadcrumb navigation visible on all pages beyond homepage
Breadcrumbs show full path (Home > Category > Product)
Each breadcrumb level is clickable
Breadcrumbs differentiated from main navigation
issues.context_notes: Only flag if breadcrumbs completely absent on deep category/product pages. Do not flag: Homepage or single-level pages. Industry context: Simple sites (single category) may not need breadcrumbs. Focus on: Whether user can navigate back through hierarchy.

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent icon styles (outlined vs filled)
issues.user_problem: Mixed icon styles create visual inconsistency and confusion
signals_to_detect: Some icons in navigation are outlined, others are solid filled
Shopping cart, favorites, and profile use different styles
Top navigation icons differ in style from footer navigation icons
Mixed icon stroke weight and fill patterns throughout interface
issues.recommendation: Standardise all icons across the site to a single visual style — either all outlined, all filled, or all two-tone. Avoid mixing outlined and filled variants of the same icon set or using icons from multiple different libraries. Implement an icon component in the design system that sources all icons from the single approved set and prevents ad-hoc additions of off-style icons.
acceptance_criteria: All icons across the site use a single consistent visual style (all outlined or all filled)
No mixing of outlined and filled variants of the same icon on any page
Icons sourced from a single library or icon set — no mixing of libraries
Icon component in design system is the single source of truth for all icon usage
Design system documents the approved icon set and prohibits off-library additions
negative_signals: All icons consistently use same style
Icon family consistent across site
Mixing styles intentional for emphasis
Style consistency extends to weight and corners

issues.issue_title: Ambiguous icon meaning
issues.user_problem: Users cannot immediately understand what certain icons represent
signals_to_detect: Navigation icon lacks accompanying text label or tooltip
Custom or non-standard icons without clear meaning
Action button uses icon that doesn't match user expectations
Feature represented by icon with no hover explanation
issues.recommendation: Replace any ambiguous or non-standard icons with universally recognised alternatives, or add a visible text label alongside the icon. Conduct a recognition test: show each icon to 5 target users without context — if fewer than 4 can identify its meaning, add a text label or replace the icon. Apply aria-label attributes to all icon-only interactive elements for screen reader users.
acceptance_criteria: All icons pass a recognition test with 80%+ of target users identifying the correct meaning
Any icon failing the recognition test has a visible text label added
All icon-only interactive elements have aria-label attributes
Non-standard or custom icons include a tooltip on hover (desktop) and a visible label on mobile
Icon meaning is consistent site-wide — the same icon is never used for two different purposes
negative_signals: Icons paired with text labels for clarity
Icons follow common conventions
Tooltips available on hover for icon-only buttons
Important actions use recognized icons

issues.issue_title: Low visibility of favorite/bookmark icons
issues.user_problem: Users miss opportunity to save items due to faint or hard-to-see icons
signals_to_detect: Wishlist icon very small or light gray blending with background
Favorite button appears only on hover, not visible by default
Bookmark icon uses very low contrast color
Save icon lacks visual prominence compared to primary CTAs
issues.recommendation: Increase the visual prominence of the favourite/bookmark icon on product cards by ensuring it has sufficient size (minimum 24x24px visual area), adequate contrast against the product image background, and a visible active/inactive state. On mobile, make the icon always visible rather than hover-only. Ensure the touch target meets the 44x44px minimum. Add an aria-label that reflects the current state (e.g., 'Add to wishlist' / 'Remove from wishlist').
acceptance_criteria: Favourite icon visually distinct and legible against both light and dark product image backgrounds
Icon always visible on mobile product cards (not hover-dependent)
Icon meets 44x44px minimum tap target on mobile
Active (wishlisted) and inactive states are visually distinct with clear differentiation
aria-label reflects current state: 'Add to wishlist' when inactive, 'Remove from wishlist' when active
negative_signals: Favorites icon prominently visible in header
Icon includes count badge showing items
Filled heart indicates items saved
Wishlist accessible within one click

issues.issue_title: Spelling and grammar errors in content
issues.user_problem: Errors damage credibility and professionalism of brand
signals_to_detect: Product descriptions or marketing copy contains obvious misspellings
Grammar errors like missing articles or incorrect verb tenses visible
Punctuation errors such as missing periods or misplaced commas in content
Repeated typos or autocorrect failures in product titles or descriptions
issues.recommendation: Implement a content quality workflow that includes spell-checking and grammar review before publication. Run all existing content through a tool like Grammarly, Hemingway App, or a CMS-integrated spell-checker. Set up automated spell-checking in the CMS or CI/CD pipeline to flag new errors before they reach production. Assign content ownership so errors are reported and fixed within 24 hours.
acceptance_criteria: All user-facing content passes a spell-check and grammar review before publication
Zero spelling or grammatical errors on homepage, PDP, checkout, and account pages
CMS or publishing workflow includes a mandatory spell-check step
Reported spelling errors fixed within 24 hours of identification
Automated spell-check integrated into the content publishing pipeline
negative_signals: Content reviewed for spelling and grammar
Professional tone maintained
No obvious typos in critical content
Product descriptions clearly written
issues.context_notes: Only flag obvious, disruptive spelling errors in critical content (CTAs, headings, product names). Do not flag: Minor typos in long-form content or user-generated content. Focus on: Errors that damage credibility or clarity.

issues.issue_title: Empty content sections without messaging
issues.user_problem: Page sections with no content appear broken or still loading
signals_to_detect: Featured products section shows empty space with no placeholder
Recommendations carousel appears blank without No items message
Account section shows empty boxes where benefits should display
Related items section visible but contains no content or message
issues.recommendation: Design explicit empty states for all content sections that may be empty: empty search results, empty wishlists, empty order history, empty cart. Each empty state should include an illustration or icon, a plain-language explanation of why the section is empty, and a primary CTA guiding the user to take a meaningful next action. Never show a blank container with no message.
acceptance_criteria: All potentially empty sections have a designed empty state (not a blank container)
Empty state includes an explanation of why the section is empty
Empty state includes a primary CTA guiding the user to a relevant next action
Empty states tested for: cart, wishlist, order history, search results, and account sections
Empty state copy is encouraging and helpful, not apologetic or technical
negative_signals: Empty sections show helpful message
Empty states include icon and text
Sections with no content removed from layout
Alternative content suggested when empty

issues.issue_title: Entire pages blank without empty state design
issues.user_problem: Empty pages (notifications, search results, cart) show nothing, appearing broken
signals_to_detect: Empty cart shows completely blank page with no message
No search results page shows blank screen instead of empty state
Notifications page appears empty without Try searching or Browse items message
Account orders section blank when no orders exist
issues.recommendation: Identify all pages that can render with no content (empty account pages, first-time user dashboards, empty categories) and design a full-page empty state for each. Include a welcoming headline, a brief explanation, and a clear primary action that helps the user populate the page or navigate to relevant content. Treat the first-time experience as a distinct design state requiring its own UI.
acceptance_criteria: All pages that can render empty have a designed first-time / empty full-page state
Empty page states include a headline, explanation, and primary CTA
First-time user account dashboard shows onboarding prompts rather than blank sections
Empty category pages show alternative navigation (related categories, search) rather than 'No products found'
Empty states reviewed and approved as part of every new feature or page design process
negative_signals: Empty states include helpful illustration and message
Clear CTA on empty pages
Empty pages explain why nothing shown
Navigation to relevant content provided

issues.issue_title: UI state not updating after account creation
issues.user_problem: Users unsure if registration succeeded due to stale UI state
signals_to_detect: Header shows Login button after successful signup
Account menu or user name does not update after registration
Navigation still displays Create Account option after login
User profile icon or personalized greeting absent post-signup
issues.recommendation: Ensure that the navigation UI updates immediately after account creation or login to reflect the authenticated state — showing the user's name or account icon and removing the Sign In / Register CTAs. Trigger this state change synchronously upon authentication without requiring a full page reload. Use a JWT or session state listener to update all header elements in real time.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation updates to show logged-in state immediately after account creation or login
Sign In and Register CTAs replaced by account name or avatar icon on authentication
State change occurs without a full page reload where technically feasible
Cart count syncs to the account's saved cart on login
Logging out immediately reverts the navigation to the logged-out state
negative_signals: UI updates immediately when state changes
Real-time feedback shows action completed
Visual indicators reflect current state
Animations show state changes smoothly

issues.issue_title: No visual confirmation when item added to cart
issues.user_problem: Users uncertain whether add-to-cart action succeeded
signals_to_detect: Add-to-cart button lacks success state or loading indicator when clicked
No toast notification appears confirming item added to cart
Cart icon badge count doesn't update or show animation after add
No minicart preview or slide-out drawer showing added item
issues.recommendation: Provide immediate visual confirmation whenever an item is added to the cart: show a mini-cart drawer sliding in from the right, or a toast notification in the top-right corner that confirms the item name, variant, and updated cart count. Update the cart icon count badge in the header simultaneously. Ensure the confirmation is visible on both desktop and mobile.
acceptance_criteria: Cart count badge on the header icon updates immediately when an item is added
A mini-cart drawer or toast notification appears within 300ms of Add to Cart click
Confirmation shows the added item name, selected variant (size/colour), and new cart total
Confirmation dismisses automatically after 4–6 seconds or on user interaction
Confirmation visible on both desktop and mobile without scrolling
negative_signals: Toast notification appears when item added
Cart icon shows updated count with animation
Mini cart preview shows added item
Add to Cart button shows success state (checkmark, 'Added!')
issues.context_notes: Only flag if NO feedback after add-to-cart. Do not flag: Subtle confirmation (cart count update, button state change). Focus on: Whether user knows action succeeded. Industry context: Minimal design may use subtle indicators; flag only complete absence.

issues.issue_title: Technical status labels unclear to users
issues.user_problem: System-facing language confuses non-technical users
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Order status shows technical terms like 'fulfilling' or 'processing' instead of user-friendly labels
Error message contains system error codes or technical jargon
Status indicator uses abbreviations like 'INVC' or 'PRCS' without explanation
Sidebar or status section shows database or API terminology instead of plain language
Workflow statuses (draft, submitted, pending approval, rejected) don't indicate who needs to act next or what the status means for the currently logged-in user
issues.recommendation: Replace all technical or system-generated status labels with plain-language equivalents that clearly communicate the current state to non-technical users. Create a status label glossary mapping internal system states to customer-facing language (e.g., 'AWAITING_FULFILMENT' → 'Being prepared', 'SHIPPED_PARTIAL' → 'Partly shipped'). Apply this mapping consistently across order history, account dashboard, and transactional emails.
acceptance_criteria: All order and account status labels use plain, customer-facing language
No internal status codes, system terms, or all-caps values visible to end users
Status label glossary created and integrated with the order management system
Status labels consistent across order history page, account dashboard, and emails
5 target users shown each status label can accurately describe the meaning without assistance
negative_signals: Status labels use plain language
Technical codes translated to user-friendly terms
Status meanings clear without help
Progress indicators show order status visually
issues.context_notes: Only flag if status labels are genuinely unclear to the target user. Do not flag: Technical statuses on pages intended for technical users. Focus on: Whether the target audience understands what state their item is in. NEW (B2B/approval workflows): Status labels must communicate role-specific meaning — 'Pending' is ambiguous if the user doesn't know whether they or someone else needs to act. Prefer labels like 'Awaiting finance approval' over generic 'Pending'.

issues.issue_title: Contradictory inactive CTAs for completed actions
issues.user_problem: Disabled buttons for already-completed actions create confusion
signals_to_detect: Delivered order shows grayed-out Cancel button without explanation
Completed booking displays disabled Modify button instead of hiding it
Processed refund shows faded Request Refund button still present on order
Cancelled appointment has disabled Reschedule button instead of Remove
issues.recommendation: Audit all account and order management pages to ensure CTAs are contextually appropriate to the current order or account state. Completed or delivered orders should not show 'Cancel Order' as an active CTA. Refunded orders should not show 'Request Refund'. Map each order status to its valid action set and implement conditional CTA rendering based on the current state.
acceptance_criteria: CTAs shown on order cards or detail pages are appropriate for the current order status
Delivered orders show: 'View Details', 'Buy Again', 'Write a Review' — not 'Cancel'
Cancelled orders show: 'View Details', 'Shop Again' — not 'Track Shipment'
Order status to valid-actions mapping documented and implemented
No contradictory or inactive CTAs visible on any order in any status state
negative_signals: Completed actions use positive styling
Inactive CTAs for completed actions hidden
Clear indication of what's accomplished
Next steps shown instead of redundant buttons
issues.context_notes: Only flag if disabled button for completed action is confusing. Do not flag: Clear success messaging even if button remains. Focus on: Whether user understands action is complete.

issues.issue_title: Non-responsive mobile layout and sizing
issues.user_problem: Elements shift, overlap, or become unusable on mobile devices
signals_to_detect: Content overflows horizontally requiring pinch-zoom on mobile viewport
Text or buttons overlap or become illegible on phones under 375px wide
Images scale incorrectly causing distortion or leaving whitespace on mobile
Navigation or product cards stack incorrectly causing layout breaks
issues.recommendation: Test the site on real mobile devices (iOS Safari and Android Chrome) at 375px and 390px viewport widths. Fix all layout issues including: elements overflowing their containers, text too small to read without zooming, images not scaling correctly, and interactive elements too close together. Ensure the viewport meta tag is set correctly (width=device-width, initial-scale=1) and zoom is not disabled.
acceptance_criteria: Site layout correct and fully functional on iOS Safari (iPhone 14, 390px) and Android Chrome (375px)
No content overflow, clipping, or horizontal scroll on mobile viewports
Viewport meta tag set to width=device-width, initial-scale=1 — zoom not disabled
All text readable at default zoom level without manual pinch-zoom required
Core journeys (browse, PDP, cart, checkout) tested and functional on real mobile devices
negative_signals: Layout adapts smoothly to different screen widths
Content stacks appropriately on mobile
Touch targets sized appropriately
Text readable without zooming
issues.context_notes: Only flag critical layout breaks (horizontal scroll required, text unreadable, overlapping content). Do not flag: Intentional differences in mobile layout, elements that adapt differently but function correctly. Test on: Multiple viewport sizes 320px-768px.

issues.issue_title: Mobile menu fails to expand
issues.user_problem: Users cannot access navigation menu on mobile devices
signals_to_detect: Hamburger menu icon present but not clickable or functional
Menu toggles briefly then collapses without showing navigation items
Mobile menu button has no touch feedback or click event handler
Navigation menu hidden behind fixed header making items inaccessible
issues.recommendation: Debug and fix the mobile menu expansion. Common causes include: JavaScript errors preventing event listeners from firing, CSS transitions that render the menu off-screen, z-index conflicts with other fixed elements, or touch event conflicts. Test on iOS Safari and Android Chrome. Implement a fallback: if JavaScript fails, the navigation should degrade to visible inline links.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile menu opens reliably on first tap on iOS Safari and Android Chrome
Menu displays all navigation options when open without any items being clipped
Menu close button or swipe-to-close dismisses the menu reliably
No JavaScript console errors thrown when the menu is opened or closed
If JavaScript fails, fallback navigation links are visible without the menu toggle
negative_signals: Mobile menu toggle functional and responsive
Menu opens smoothly with clear animation
Touch target for menu button large enough
Menu accessible within one tap
issues.context_notes: Only flag if mobile menu completely non-functional. Do not flag: Different menu pattern on mobile (if functional), delayed loading, or alternative navigation present. Test on: Touch devices, not browser resize.

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent tone of voice (dialect vs formal)
issues.user_problem: Mixed formality levels in content confuse users
signals_to_detect: FAQs use conversational 'hey' tone while product descriptions use formal 'hereby'
Navigation uses casual slang 'check out' while checkout uses formal 'proceed'
Help content mixes contractions with full formal sentences inconsistently
Some pages use 'you' directly while others use passive or third-person language
issues.recommendation: Define a brand voice and tone guide specifying: the register (formal vs conversational), vocabulary preferences, sentence length guidelines, and examples of on-brand vs off-brand copy. Apply the guide to all customer-facing touchpoints. Conduct a content audit to identify and rewrite all copy that deviates from the defined tone, paying particular attention to inconsistencies between marketing copy and functional/UI copy.
acceptance_criteria: Brand voice and tone guide documented and available to all content contributors
Consistent tone applied across homepage, PDP, checkout, error messages, and emails
No jarring shifts between formal and casual register on the same page
Content audit completed identifying all off-tone copy instances
New content reviewed against the tone guide before publication
negative_signals: Consistent tone throughout
Same dialect used across all content
Voice matches brand consistently
Copy style guide followed

issues.issue_title: No confirmation for language selection
issues.user_problem: Users uncertain if language change took effect
signals_to_detect: Language dropdown closes without page refresh or notification
No toast or confirmation message shown after language selection
Page doesn't update immediately with changed language
Language selector has no submit button or confirmation required
issues.recommendation: When a user selects a new language from the language selector, either: (a) immediately switch the interface language and show a brief toast/banner confirming the change (e.g., 'Language changed to French'), or (b) if a page reload is required, show a confirmation prompt (e.g., 'Switch to French? Your current page will reload') before proceeding. Never change the language silently without any visual confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Language change triggers a visible confirmation (toast, banner, or prompt) in all cases
If a page reload is required, user is informed before the reload occurs
Confirmation message visible for at least 3 seconds
Language change persists on navigation to other pages
Confirmation accessible to screen readers via an aria-live region announcement
negative_signals: Language change confirmation message appears
Page refreshes to show selected language
Visual indicator shows active language
Success message confirms selection
issues.context_notes: Only flag if language change provides no feedback (no page reload, no confirmation). Do not flag: Obvious page refresh or language name update in selector. Focus on: Whether user knows change took effect.

issues.issue_title: Language selector not functioning
issues.user_problem: Users cannot change site language despite selector being present
signals_to_detect: Language selector dropdown disabled or non-interactive
Selecting different language doesn't update page content
Language toggle button unresponsive to clicks or touches
Language preference doesn't persist across page navigation
issues.recommendation: Debug and fix the language selector functionality across all affected pages. Test by selecting each available language and verifying that the full UI text switches correctly including navigation, product names, checkout labels, and error messages. Check for common failure causes: JavaScript errors, missing translation files for certain language codes, or session/cookie conflicts preventing the preference from persisting.
acceptance_criteria: Language selector successfully switches the interface language for all available language options
Language preference persists across page navigation and browser session
Full UI text switches on language change — no mixed-language pages
No JavaScript errors in the console when a language is selected
Language selector tested and functional on both desktop and mobile browsers
negative_signals: Language selector dropdown functional
Language options load and display correctly
Selected language applied immediately
No errors preventing language change
issues.context_notes: Only flag if language selector completely broken. Do not flag: Slow loading, different-than-expected behavior (opens new page vs. in-place). Focus on: Whether language can be changed at all.

issues.issue_title: Small clickable area for video play button
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to activate video playback due to tiny hit target
signals_to_detect: Video play icon button smaller than 30x30 pixels
Video thumbnail has no clickable region beyond center play icon
Play button lacks adequate padding or hover state expansion
Touch target for play action below 44x44 pixel minimum on mobile
issues.recommendation: Increase the video play button size to a minimum of 64x64px and position it centred over the thumbnail. Make the entire thumbnail area a clickable play target, not just the button icon itself. Use a semi-transparent overlay on the thumbnail to improve play button visibility against varied image backgrounds. Ensure the play button is keyboard-accessible (Tab-focusable) and announced correctly to screen readers.
acceptance_criteria: Video play button minimum 64x64px and visually centred on the thumbnail
Entire thumbnail area is clickable/tappable to trigger video playback
Play button visible and legible against both light and dark thumbnail backgrounds
Play button keyboard-accessible (Tab-focusable, Enter/Space to activate)
aria-label on play button reads 'Play [video title or description]' for screen readers
negative_signals: Video play button minimum 48x48px clickable area
Play button easily tappable on touch devices
Video controls have adequate spacing
Alternative text indicates video content
issues.context_notes: Only flag if video play button genuinely tiny (<40px clickable area). Do not flag: Standard player controls, or when entire video is clickable. Focus on: Whether user can easily initiate playback.

issues.issue_title: Unclear purpose of account features
issues.user_problem: Users confused by unexplained features like credits or points
signals_to_detect: Account loyalty points or credits section lacks explanation of purpose
Feature icon or label uses jargon like 'Rewards Equilibrium' without definition
Settings section shows options without hover tooltips explaining what they do
Account benefit sections missing info icons or help links for clarity
issues.recommendation: Add a short descriptive label or subtitle to each account feature section explaining its purpose and benefit (e.g., 'Saved Addresses — Save time at checkout by storing your delivery addresses'). For complex or unfamiliar features (loyalty points, referral schemes), add a 'How it works' tooltip or expandable info panel. Ensure the purpose of every section is clear before the user interacts with it.
acceptance_criteria: Every account section has a headline and a 1–2 sentence description of its purpose
Complex features include a 'How it works' tooltip or expandable explanation
Feature benefits stated from the user's perspective (time saved, money earned, etc.)
No account section requires the user to interact with it to understand what it does
5 first-time users can accurately describe the purpose of every account section without help
negative_signals: Account features explained with brief descriptions
Icons or labels clarify what each section contains
Onboarding or tooltips guide users
Feature benefits clearly communicated

issues.issue_title: Misleading CTA leads to wrong flow
issues.user_problem: CTA labeled "Book" takes users to search instead of booking flow
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Primary CTA says 'Book Now' but href or onclick points to search page
Button labeled 'Complete Booking' instead navigates to cart or checkout
Booking link text contradicts actual destination in navigation structure
CTA tooltip or help text differs from where button actually navigates to
issues.recommendation: Audit all CTAs across the site to verify that the label accurately predicts the destination and outcome. Replace vague labels ('Click here', 'Learn more', 'Submit') with specific, outcome-oriented labels ('View size guide', 'See delivery options', 'Place my order'). Test by asking users to predict where each CTA will take them — if fewer than 4 in 5 are correct, rewrite the label.
acceptance_criteria: All CTAs use specific, outcome-oriented labels that describe the destination or action
No CTAs labelled 'Click here', 'Submit', 'Learn more', or other generic phrases
CTA labels tested with 5 users — 80%+ correctly predict the destination or outcome
CTA labels match the page title or heading of the destination page
Labels consistent — the same action uses the same CTA label throughout the site
negative_signals: CTA labels accurately describe destination or action
Button text matches resulting page
No misleading promises
Action preview shown before execution
issues.context_notes: Only flag genuinely misleading CTAs (promises something, delivers different). Do not flag: Minor wording differences between button and page. Industry context: Marketing CTAs vs. exact page titles differ slightly. Focus on: Actual deception.

issues.issue_title: Map component failing to load
issues.user_problem: Users cannot view location information when map fails
signals_to_detect: Map iframe or embed shows 403/404 error or blank space
Google Maps or map library fails to initialize with API error
Map container visible but displays only gray tiles without content
Location information missing fallback when map fails to load
issues.recommendation: Add robust error handling and a fallback state for the map component: if the map API fails to load (network error, API quota exceeded, JavaScript error), display a static image of the map or a plain-text address with a link to Google Maps as an alternative. Implement retry logic on API timeout and log map load failures to an error monitoring tool.
acceptance_criteria: Map loads correctly on initial page load under normal network conditions
If the map API fails, a fallback static image or plain-text address with Google Maps link is shown
Fallback state is visually acceptable and contains all necessary location information
Map load failures logged to error monitoring (e.g., Sentry) for tracking
Retry logic attempts to reload the map once on timeout before falling back
negative_signals: Map loads and displays correctly
Error message shown if map fails with alternative
Address text provided alongside map
Map interactive with working controls
issues.context_notes: Only flag if map completely fails AND no alternative provided. Do not flag: Maps that load slowly, or alternative (address text) present. Focus on: Whether user can get location information by any means.

issues.issue_title: Results display glitch (temporary visibility)
issues.user_problem: Filtered results appear briefly then revert to full list
signals_to_detect: Product list shows filtered items then reverts to full list within 2 seconds
Filter checkbox appears checked then unchecks automatically
Result count updates briefly to filtered number then resets to total
URL reflects filter but page display shows all products
issues.recommendation: Debug the filter application state management to identify why results temporarily revert or flicker. Common causes include race conditions between filter requests, optimistic UI updates that are incorrectly rolled back, or CSS transitions revealing intermediate states. Implement a loading state during filter application (skeleton or overlay) so users do not see the un-filtered state during processing.
acceptance_criteria: Applying a filter does not cause the product grid to revert to an unfiltered state
No visible flicker or flash of unfiltered results during filter application
Loading/skeleton state shown during filter processing to prevent layout shift
Filter results stable and consistent across 10 consecutive filter interactions
No race conditions between concurrent filter requests — most recent request wins
negative_signals: Filter results remain stable after applied
No flickering or content reloading
Results update once and stay updated
Loading state shown during application
issues.context_notes: Only flag if filter results flicker or reload multiple times. Do not flag: Single loading state during filter application. Focus on: Whether results are stable after filtering.

issues.issue_title: Cluttered dropdown with poor information scent
issues.user_problem: Navigation menu has too many items (7+) without clear grouping
signals_to_detect: Navigation menu displays more than 7 top-level items without grouping
Dropdown lacks visual dividers or section headers to organize categories
Menu items use inconsistent naming or appear in random order
Navigation lacks mega menu structure or category grouping for clarity
issues.recommendation: Redesign the cluttered dropdown by reducing the number of top-level items (aim for 5–7 maximum), grouping related sub-items under clear category headings, and removing redundant or low-traffic links. Use visual hierarchy (font weight, colour, spacing) to distinguish categories from individual items. Test the revised structure with a tree test or first-click test to validate information scent.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level dropdown items reduced to 7 or fewer
Sub-items grouped under clear category headings with visual hierarchy
Related items logically grouped — no overlap or duplication between categories
Dropdown structure validated with a tree test showing 80%+ task success rate
Dropdown visually scannable in under 3 seconds — verified with eye-tracking or user observation
negative_signals: Dropdown menu limited to 5-7 main items
Categories grouped with visual separators
Mega menu uses columns for organization
Long lists use progressive disclosure
issues.context_notes: Only flag if dropdown/menu is genuinely overwhelming (10+ items, no grouping). Do not flag: Well-organized mega menus, or 5-7 clear categories. Focus on: Cognitive load and clarity.

issues.issue_title: Missing video transcriptions or captions
issues.user_problem: Deaf/hard-of-hearing users cannot access video content
signals_to_detect: Video player lacks captions or subtitles option in controls
No transcript link or download available for video content
Video iframe missing title or description of audio content
Closed captions button absent from video player interface
issues.recommendation: Add synchronised closed captions (CC) to all video content containing speech. Host captions as a separate WebVTT (.vtt) file linked via a <track> element in the HTML5 video tag. For videos hosted on YouTube or Vimeo, enable captions in the platform settings and verify accuracy. Provide a full text transcript linked below or adjacent to each video.
acceptance_criteria: All videos with speech have synchronised closed captions available
Captions implemented as a WebVTT file with a <track kind='captions'> element or platform CC
CC toggle visible and accessible in the video player controls
Captions are accurate — tested against the spoken audio
Text transcript linked from the page for all videos over 30 seconds
negative_signals: Videos include caption toggle button
Transcripts provided below or linked
Auto-generated captions available at minimum
Deaf users can access video content
issues.context_notes: Only flag video content with no text alternative. Do not flag: Decorative videos, videos with auto-captions. Industry context: Accessibility requirement for informational video. Focus on: Whether deaf users can access information.

issues.issue_title: Active filters not displayed at top
issues.user_problem: Users forget which filters are applied and cannot easily review them
signals_to_detect: No chip or tag display showing currently applied filters
Active filters visible only in sidebar, not above product results
Filter status hidden or requires scrolling to see applied criteria
Applied filters lack individual remove buttons or clear all option
issues.recommendation: Display all currently active filters as removable chips or tags in a clearly visible area above the product grid, immediately below the filter controls. Each chip should show the filter name and value (e.g., 'Colour: Blue ×') with an X to remove it. Include a 'Clear all' control when multiple filters are active. This active filter display should update dynamically without page reload.
acceptance_criteria: Active filters displayed as chips above the product grid immediately after selection
Each filter chip shows the filter name and selected value (e.g., 'Size: M')
Each chip has an X or Remove button that deselects only that filter
'Clear all' button visible when 2 or more filters are active
Active filter chips update dynamically — no page reload required to see the updated state
negative_signals: Active filters displayed as removable chips or pills at top of results
Applied filters visible above product grid with individual X buttons
Filter summary section shows current selections clearly
Each active filter can be removed individually without clearing all
issues.context_notes: Only flag if active filters completely hidden (user can't see what's applied). Do not flag: Filters shown in sidebar or clear from URL. Focus on: Whether user can identify and review current filter state. Common false positive: Filters visible but not in 'perfect' position.

issues.issue_title: Insufficient spacing and grouping of elements
issues.user_problem: Users struggle to identify which elements belong together
signals_to_detect: Related form fields or sections lack visual grouping or borders
Spacing between unrelated elements equals spacing between related items
Elements appear clustered together without clear visual separation
Margins and padding inconsistent across similar component groups
issues.recommendation: Apply consistent spacing and visual grouping across all page layouts using an 8px spacing grid. Increase white space between distinct sections (minimum 48px between major content blocks), between form field groups (minimum 24px), and between adjacent interactive elements (minimum 12px). Use visual proximity to group related elements — elements that belong together should be closer to each other than to unrelated elements.
acceptance_criteria: Consistent spacing scale applied based on an 8px grid (8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64px)
Major content sections separated by at least 48px vertical spacing
Form fields within the same group have consistent 16–24px spacing
Adjacent interactive elements (buttons, links) have at least 12px separation
Visual grouping clearly communicates which elements are related — verified with a Gestalt proximity test
negative_signals: Related elements grouped with whitespace or borders
Clear spacing between distinct sections
Form fields have adequate padding
Visual rhythm through consistent spacing

issues.issue_title: Primary CTA missing from bottom of long pages
issues.user_problem: Users must scroll back to top after reading content to take action
signals_to_detect: Buy button or CTA visible only at top of page requiring scrolling to find
Page longer than 2000px without sticky or repeated CTA
After-the-fold footer lacks secondary CTA for user action
Long product description without Add to Cart button at bottom
issues.recommendation: On all long-form pages where the primary CTA is positioned near the top (above the fold), repeat the CTA or implement a sticky CTA bar that appears after the user scrolls past the original. The sticky bar should appear at the bottom of the viewport on mobile and in the lower area on desktop, and should not obscure content. Alternatively, place a full-width CTA at the end of the page content before the footer.
acceptance_criteria: Primary CTA accessible at both the top and bottom of all long-form pages
Sticky CTA bar appears after the original CTA scrolls out of view
Sticky bar does not obscure page content or other interactive elements
Bottom CTA text matches the top CTA for consistency
Sticky CTA disappears when the user reaches the footer to avoid duplication
negative_signals: Primary CTA repeated at bottom of long pages
Sticky CTA appears when main scrolls out
Multiple conversion points throughout
Bottom includes clear next step
issues.context_notes: Only flag long pages (>2000px) with no repeat CTA at bottom. Do not flag: Short pages, pages with sticky CTAs. Focus on: Whether user must scroll all way back up after reading content to take action.

issues.issue_title: Missing individual item prices in cart
issues.user_problem: Users cannot verify pricing of individual items in cart
signals_to_detect: Cart item rows show only total without unit price breakdown
No price per item column or price multiplication display
Quantity and price visible but subtotal per item missing
Only grand total shown without itemized pricing detail
issues.recommendation: Display a clear price breakdown for each individual line item in the cart: the unit price, the quantity selected, and the line total (unit price × quantity). If any item has a discount applied, show both the original and discounted unit prices with a strikethrough. Ensure the cart total reflects the sum of all visible line totals so users can verify the arithmetic themselves.
acceptance_criteria: Each cart line item displays: product name, unit price, quantity, and line total
Discounted items show original price (strikethrough) and discounted price
Line total for each item equals unit price × quantity and is visibly displayed
Cart subtotal equals the sum of all line totals — users can verify mentally
Price breakdown consistent between the cart page and the checkout order summary
negative_signals: Each cart item shows unit price, quantity, and line total
Price breakdown visible
Individual product pricing clear
Price per item and total both displayed
issues.context_notes: Only flag if price breakdown genuinely unclear (user can't verify math). Do not flag: Minimal presentation if calculation is transparent. Focus on: Whether user can understand 'quantity × unit price = line total'.

issues.issue_title: Inconsistent font usage across interface
issues.user_problem: Multiple different fonts create unprofessional appearance
signals_to_detect: Navigation uses serif font while body uses sans-serif without hierarchy reason
More than 2 different font families visible across the page
Form labels use different font than form inputs or buttons
Price display uses entirely different font family from product titles
issues.recommendation: Establish a typography system using a maximum of 2 typefaces: one for headings/display and one for body/UI text. Remove all ad-hoc font-family declarations outside the design system. Enforce the system through CSS custom properties (--font-heading, --font-body) referenced in a single global stylesheet. Audit for any pages or components importing additional font files not part of the approved system.
acceptance_criteria: Maximum 2 typefaces used across the entire interface (1 heading, 1 body)
Typography defined via CSS custom properties in a single global stylesheet
No ad-hoc or page-level font-family overrides outside the design system
All font files loaded via a single consolidated import — no duplicate or redundant font loads
Typography consistent across all page types including checkout, account, and error pages
negative_signals: Consistent font family throughout site
Font sizes follow typographic scale
No random font changes between sections
Type system documented and applied

issues.issue_title: Filter section requires extra click to show all options
issues.user_problem: Users must click "Show more" to see all available filters
signals_to_detect: Filter options collapsed with Show more / See all button
Filter section displays only first 3-5 options then requires expansion
Scrollable filter list with cutoff text indicating hidden options
Accordion-style filters collapsed by default requiring clicks to expand
issues.recommendation: Show the top 5–6 most-used filter options expanded by default within each filter category, with a 'Show more' control to reveal additional options. Remove the need for an extra click just to see available filter values. For filter categories with fewer than 6 options, display all options expanded with no 'Show more' needed.
acceptance_criteria: Top 5–6 filter options visible by default within each filter category without additional clicks
Filter categories with 6 or fewer options are fully expanded by default
'Show more' control present only when there are more than 6 options to show
'Show more' expands inline without navigating away or opening a modal
No filter category requires more than 1 interaction to see its most relevant options
negative_signals: All filter options visible without requiring expansion
Filter categories show all options upfront (no 'Show more' needed)
Long filter lists use scrolling within section, not collapse/expand
Critical filters (Price, Size) always fully visible without clicking
issues.context_notes: Only flag if critical filters (price, size, category) are collapsed by default requiring clicks. Do not flag: Less-used filters (brand with 50+ options) in collapsed state. Focus on: Whether most-used filters require unnecessary clicks to access.

issues.issue_title: RTL/LTR directional inconsistencies
issues.user_problem: Interface elements not properly mirrored for RTL languages
signals_to_detect: RTL language selection shows LTR layout without proper mirroring
Icons and arrows point wrong direction in RTL mode
Left sidebar appears on left in RTL instead of right
Text alignment remains left-to-right when RTL language selected
issues.recommendation: Implement full RTL (right-to-left) layout support for all RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu) using CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start instead of margin-left) and the dir='rtl' attribute on the <html> element. Test every page template in RTL mode and fix: text alignment, icon mirroring, navigation order, form field direction, and any components that use fixed left/right positioning.
acceptance_criteria: dir='rtl' attribute on <html> correctly mirrors the full page layout for RTL languages
All text aligns right and reads correctly in RTL mode
Navigation, breadcrumbs, and pagination reverse direction in RTL layout
Icons that imply direction (arrows, chevrons, back buttons) are mirrored in RTL
All page templates tested in RTL mode with zero layout breakage or LTR remnants
negative_signals: RTL layout properly mirrors LTR layout
Icons and UI elements flip appropriately
Text alignment correct for RTL
Navigation flows right-to-left consistently
issues.context_notes: Only flag if RTL implementation breaks functionality or readability. Do not flag: Minor visual inconsistencies that don't hinder use. Industry context: RTL support is complex; flag critical breaks, not perfection. Test on: Actual RTL language selection.

issues.issue_title: Intrusive chat widget appearing immediately
issues.user_problem: Users interrupted by chat prompts before assessing site
signals_to_detect: Chat widget/bubble appears within 5 seconds of page load
Chat assistant message displayed before user interaction
Chat widget overlays content without user requesting help
Proactive chat appears before user browsed products
negative_signals: Chat appears collapsed as icon until user clicks
Chat opens only after 30+ seconds of inactivity
Chat appears only on support/help pages
issues.recommendation: Delay chat until user shows intent (30s+, 2+ pages, or exit intent)
acceptance_criteria: Chat does not open within first 30 seconds
Remains icon-only until user initiates
All form labels use sentence case consistently across checkout, account, and search forms
Label capitalisation documented in the content style guide and enforced via design system tokens

issues.issue_title: Phone country code doesn't match selected country
issues.user_problem: Incorrect country code prefix doesn't match selected country
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Phone shows static country code regardless of country selected
Country dropdown shows one country while phone shows different code
No automatic update of phone prefix when country changes
Phone lacks country code dropdown synchronized with country field
negative_signals: Phone prefix updates automatically when country changes
Integrated phone input with country selector
Single selector controls both country and phone prefix
issues.recommendation: Synchronise the phone country code prefix with the country selected in the shipping or billing address dropdown. When a user selects a country, the phone prefix should update automatically to match. If the phone field appears before the country field, set the default prefix to the user's detected locale and allow manual override via the country code dropdown.
acceptance_criteria: Phone prefix updates automatically when the user changes their country selection
Default prefix matches the user's detected locale or selected shipping country
User can manually override the auto-detected prefix via the country code dropdown
Phone prefix and country are synchronised at time of form submission
Phone field validated with the selected country's number format rules
issues.context_notes: Check country dropdown matches phone prefix. Common: UAE selected but +91 shown.

issues.issue_title: Persistent banner cannot be dismissed
issues.user_problem: Promotional banner permanently occupies header space
signals_to_detect: Promotional banner visible on every page without dismiss option
Banner lacks X button or close control
Banner persists across pages without ability to hide
Banner takes 40+ pixels on all pages
negative_signals: Banner includes X or close button
Banner appears only on homepage
Banner auto-dismisses after interaction
issues.recommendation: Add dismiss button or limit to homepage. Store preference in session.
acceptance_criteria: Banner includes dismiss button
Dismissed state persists for session
Does not reappear after dismissal

nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and the real world
issues.recommendation: Improve the relevance of cart product recommendations by basing suggestions on: (1) items frequently bought together with the current cart contents, (2) complementary product categories (e.g., accessories for apparel, cables for electronics), or (3) the customer's browsing history. Remove any recommendations that are identical to items already in the cart, out of stock, or from a completely unrelated category.
acceptance_criteria: Cart recommendations are from the same or complementary category as cart items
No cart recommendation duplicates an item already in the cart
Out-of-stock items excluded from cart recommendations
Recommendation logic based on 'frequently bought together' or category affinity data
Fallback to bestsellers in the same category if no personalised data is available
issues.issue_title: Product recommendations unrelated to cart items
issues.user_problem: Suggested add-ons don't complement main purchase, reducing perceived value
signals_to_detect: Add-on suggestions show products from unrelated categories to cart items
Cross-sell products don't complement or enhance main purchase
Recommended items lack contextual relevance to user's shopping journey
Suggestions appear random rather than based on 'frequently bought together' logic
negative_signals: Add-ons match cart item category or occasion (e.g., chocolates with flowers)
Recommendations labeled 'Frequently bought together' with social proof
Suggestions enhance main purchase (complementary, not competing products)
