Algorithm considers browsing path and cart context
issues.context_notes: Only flag if add-ons are genuinely unrelated to cart contents. Do not flag: Cross-category suggestions that logically complement (cards with gifts, gift wrap with products). Industry context: E-commerce with strong gift/occasion focus needs contextually relevant upsells.

nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and the real world
issues.recommendation: Rewrite all delivery and shipping option labels to be self-explanatory without requiring users to read additional fine print. Each option should include: the delivery method name, the estimated delivery timeframe, and the cost (or 'Free'). Avoid vague labels like 'Standard' or 'Express' without dates. Where possible, show a specific estimated delivery date (e.g., 'Arrives by Thursday, 15 May — Free').
acceptance_criteria: Every delivery option shows: method name, estimated delivery timeframe, and cost
No option labelled with only 'Standard' or 'Express' without a timeframe
Estimated delivery date shown where calculable (e.g., 'By Thursday 15 May')
Free shipping options clearly labelled 'Free' rather than '£0.00'
5 users shown the delivery options can select the appropriate one for their need without clarification
issues.issue_title: Delivery/shipping options unclear or ambiguous
issues.user_problem: Users confused by delivery option labels and can't determine which method to choose
signals_to_detect: Delivery options use ambiguous terms (e.g., 'ask for address', 'recipient option', 'team delivery')
Multiple options use same terminology making them indistinguishable
No explanation or example provided for unfamiliar delivery methods
Labels don't clearly communicate what happens when selected
negative_signals: Delivery options use plain, action-oriented text (e.g., 'We'll ask recipient for address')
Each option includes brief explanation or example of how it works
Distinct labeling for each method with no repeated ambiguous terms
Help tooltips or icons clarify unusual delivery methods
issues.context_notes: Only flag if delivery option labels are genuinely ambiguous. Common patterns: Regional-specific delivery (GCC 'ask for address'), third-party delivery (courier coordination), time slot selection. Do not flag: Standard options (home, office) even without descriptions. Industry context: International e-commerce may have region-specific delivery patterns unfamiliar to some users.

issues.recommendation: Add a brief explanation panel or tooltip for each third-party integration (social login, payment provider, loyalty programme connector) that describes: what data will be shared, what the user gets in return, and how to disconnect it later. Display this information before the user commits to the integration, not only in the privacy policy.
acceptance_criteria: Each third-party integration has a visible explanation of what data is shared
User benefit clearly stated alongside the integration option
Instructions or link for disconnecting the integration available in account settings
Explanation visible before the user clicks to connect — not only discoverable after connection
5 users can accurately describe what data is shared before connecting any third-party integration
issues.issue_title: Third-party integration purpose unclear
issues.user_problem: Users don't understand what external service (WhatsApp, Maps, etc.) will do in the flow
signals_to_detect: Third-party service option (WhatsApp, Telegram, Maps) lacks explanation of purpose
Users can't determine what data will be shared or what action will occur
Integration appears without context (e.g., WhatsApp button with no explanation)
No preview or example shown of what recipient/user will receive via third-party service
negative_signals: Clear explanation of what happens when third-party service is selected
Sample message or screenshot shown of what recipient will receive
Privacy statement clarifies what data is shared and with whom
Integration labeled with specific purpose (e.g., 'Share location via WhatsApp')
issues.context_notes: Only flag if integration purpose is genuinely unclear. Do not flag: Standard social share buttons, obvious integrations (Google Maps for location). Industry context: Regional e-commerce may use WhatsApp for delivery coordination (common in GCC), payment apps for checkout. Focus on: Whether user understands what will happen and what data is shared.

issues.recommendation: Expand delivery options to offer at least two distinct speed tiers (standard and express) with clearly differentiated timeframes and pricing. Where technically feasible, offer date or time-slot selection for premium delivery. Send pre-delivery notifications (email or SMS) with a tracking link at least 24 hours before the expected delivery date.
acceptance_criteria: Minimum two delivery speed tiers available (standard and express or equivalent)
Each tier shows a distinct estimated timeframe and price
Date or time-slot selection available for at least one premium delivery tier
Pre-delivery notification (email or SMS) sent at least 24 hours before delivery
Tracking link included in the pre-delivery notification
issues.issue_title: Limited delivery time/date flexibility
issues.user_problem: Users can't select delivery timing that meets their needs (express, specific slots, notifications)
signals_to_detect: Only standard delivery available with no express/rush option
Delivery time slots too broad (e.g., only 3-4 hour windows) with no narrower options
No ability to select specific delivery time even for premium fee
No pre-delivery notification options (call, text, WhatsApp confirmation)
negative_signals: Multiple delivery speed options available (standard, express, rush)
Flexible time slot options (3-hour windows AND 1-hour slots for premium)
Pre-delivery notifications offered (text/call 30min before arrival)
Special occasion options with more precise timing
issues.context_notes: Only flag if flexibility genuinely limited for product category. Do not flag: Perishable goods with fixed delivery windows, made-to-order items with necessary lead times. Industry context: Time-sensitive products (flowers, food) benefit from flexible delivery. Luxury/gift items often need precise timing. Focus on: Whether timing options match user expectations for product category.

issues.recommendation: For any feature that produces a complex or non-obvious output (product customisation, gift builder, recommendation engine, subscription calculator), show a live preview or sample result as the user configures their choices. Use progressive disclosure to reveal the preview as inputs are completed. If a live preview is not technically feasible, show representative example outputs with similar inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Live preview of the feature output shown as the user makes configuration choices
Preview updates in real time (or near-real time) as selections change
If real-time preview is not possible, representative examples shown for similar configurations
Preview is visually representative of the actual output the user will receive
5 users testing the feature can accurately predict the final output from the preview alone
issues.issue_title: Feature outcome or result not visualized
issues.user_problem: Users can't visualize what feature will do or how result will appear
signals_to_detect: Feature offered without showing what final output will look like
Users can't preview or visualize how feature will function
Instructions explain feature but don't show example of result
Complex features lack visual demonstration or sample output
negative_signals: Preview or mockup shown of feature outcome
Sample image demonstrates what user will receive
Before/after or step-by-step visual guide provided
Feature includes 'see example' or 'preview' option
issues.context_notes: Only flag if visualization would meaningfully improve comprehension. Do not flag: Simple, self-explanatory features, standard e-commerce functions. Focus on: Novel features, complex personalization, digital-to-physical transitions (QR codes, custom printing). Industry context: Gift/customization products benefit from outcome visualization.

issues.issue_title: Multi-party approval status not communicated
issues.user_problem: Users complete an action but don't know that another party must approve it, leaving them uncertain whether anything happened
signals_to_detect: After submitting a request, no message indicates that a second approver (manager, finance, admin) is required
Approval workflows show a generic success state with no named next approver or department
Users have no way to see the current approval stage or who holds the pending action
Status remains unchanged after user completes their step, giving impression the action failed or is stuck
No notification or email confirms the handoff to the next approver
negative_signals: Confirmation message explicitly names the next approver or department (e.g., 'Sent to Finance for approval')
Approval chain visualised as a step indicator showing current stage and remaining steps
User receives email or in-app notification when their approval stage is complete and next party has been notified
Status label updates to reflect the new owner of the action (e.g., 'Awaiting senior manager approval')
issues.recommendation: Show explicit approval chain status after submission: who has it, what they need to do, and how the user will be notified of the outcome
acceptance_criteria: After any submission requiring further approval, the user sees the name/role of the next approver and expected next step
Status labels reflect role-specific meaning, not generic 'Pending' states
Subscription management page accessible within 2 clicks from the account dashboard
Cancellation flow completes within 3 steps maximum with a clear confirmation message
Subscription status and renewal date visible on the account dashboard
issues.context_notes: Only flag in flows where multi-party approval is genuinely required and the system does not communicate it. Do not flag: Single-approver flows where the submitter is also the approver, or flows where all steps are completed by the same user. Industry context: Critical in B2B SaaS, fintech, HR/finance platforms, and any workflow involving regulatory or financial sign-off. The absence of this causes users to re-submit, contact support, or assume failure.

issues.issue_title: Interface not adapted to user role or permission level
issues.user_problem: Users see information, dashboards, or features designed for a different role, creating confusion and misaligned mental models
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and the real world
signals_to_detect: Dashboard or homepage surfaces data and metrics irrelevant or confusing to the logged-in user's role
Navigation exposes features the current user role cannot access or should not prioritise
Users from different roles (e.g., HR vs Finance, admin vs viewer) see the same interface with no role-specific adaptation
Primary entry points lead users into workflows owned by a different role, causing disorientation
Labels, terminology, or metrics on shared screens use vocabulary from a different department's domain
negative_signals: Dashboard content and primary metrics are tailored to the logged-in user's role
Navigation items irrelevant to the current role are hidden or deprioritised
Role-specific onboarding or welcome state sets correct expectations before first use
Shared screens clearly label which sections belong to which role (e.g., 'HR section', 'Finance section')
issues.recommendation: Adapt dashboard content, navigation priority, and feature surfacing based on the logged-in user's role; use role-specific onboarding to set expectations on first login
acceptance_criteria: Each user role lands on a dashboard and navigation structure relevant to their primary tasks
Users are not exposed to primary workflows belonging to a different role without contextual signposting
All onboarding steps completable without contacting support
Progress saved automatically between onboarding steps so users can resume if interrupted
Onboarding completion rate tracked in analytics with a target of 70%+
issues.context_notes: Only flag when role differentiation is genuinely needed and absent. Do not flag: Single-role platforms, or platforms where all users share the same tasks. Industry context: Applies to B2B SaaS, enterprise tools, HR/finance platforms, multi-tenant systems, and any product with distinct user roles (admin/member, HR/finance, manager/employee). Role confusion is a leading cause of task failure in multi-role products.

issues.issue_title: Missing feature-level onboarding for complex or novel functionality
issues.user_problem: Users encounter a complex or domain-specific feature with no orientation, causing them to abandon or misuse it
signals_to_detect: Feature with multiple inputs or domain-specific logic presents no introductory explanation of its purpose before use
First-time users encounter a complex screen (simulation, configuration, financial tool) with no guided walkthrough or tooltip sequence
No sample output, template, or dummy data available to demonstrate what the feature does
Feature name or label does not communicate its purpose and no supporting copy explains it
Users must attempt (and fail) the feature before understanding what it requires
negative_signals: Feature landing page or modal explains purpose in plain language before inputs are shown
Guided walkthrough, tooltip sequence, or short explainer video available on first visit
Sample or dummy data option lets users see the feature output before committing real data
Feature name is accompanied by a one-line description of what it does and who it's for
issues.recommendation: Add a feature-level orientation layer for any complex or novel functionality: purpose statement, guided first-use flow, or sample output — before exposing users to inputs
acceptance_criteria: Users can understand the purpose of a complex feature without attempting it first
A sample, demo, or guided walkthrough is available for any feature requiring domain knowledge
Filter state persists when user navigates back from a PDP to the PLP
Applied filters survive a page reload via URL query string storage
Filter persistence tested across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox
issues.context_notes: Only flag for features that are genuinely complex, novel, or domain-specific. Do not flag: Standard e-commerce functions (cart, checkout, filters), features with self-evident purpose. Focus on: Features requiring user education before meaningful interaction — financial simulations, regulatory tools, multi-step configuration wizards, analytics modules. Industry context: Critical in B2B SaaS, fintech, compliance, and any platform where the feature vocabulary is not part of everyday user knowledge.

issues.issue_title: Data visualisation inaccessible to colour vision deficiency users
issues.user_problem: Charts and graphs rely solely on colour to convey data differences, making them unreadable for users with colour vision deficiency
signals_to_detect: Charts or graphs use colour as the only differentiator between data series (no patterns, textures, or labels)
Low-contrast colour combinations used for adjacent data segments (e.g., light blue and light green on a pie chart)
Graph legend uses colour swatches only, with no text labels or patterns alongside
Multiple shades of the same hue used across a single chart without secondary encoding (shape, pattern, direct label)
No accessible colour mode or high-contrast alternative offered for data visualisations
negative_signals: Data series distinguished by both colour AND pattern, texture, or shape
Direct data labels on chart segments reduce reliance on colour-coded legend
Colour palette passes WCAG 1.4.1 non-text contrast check and avoids red/green-only differentiation
Platform offers accessible or high-contrast theme option
issues.recommendation: Encode data differences using colour plus a secondary channel (pattern, texture, direct label, or shape); audit chart palettes against WCAG 1.4.1 and avoid red/green-only or same-hue differentiation
acceptance_criteria: All charts are interpretable without relying on colour alone
Chart palette passes WCAG 1.4.1 non-text contrast ratio requirements
Empty wishlist state includes a primary CTA directing user to browse products
Wishlist items show current availability — out-of-stock items clearly indicated
Wishlist count badge on the account icon updates immediately when items are added or removed
issues.context_notes: Only flag if colour is the sole encoding mechanism and contrast is insufficient. Do not flag: Charts with direct data labels on every segment, or single-series charts using one colour. Focus on: Multi-series charts, pie/donut charts, stacked bars, line graphs with multiple series. Industry context: Affects approximately 8% of male users and 0.5% of female users globally. Increasingly required under WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, which many enterprise and government procurement processes mandate.

issues.issue_title: Render-blocking CSS or JavaScript resources
issues.user_problem: Page load delayed by CSS/JS files that block rendering
signals_to_detect: CSS files loaded in <head> without async or defer attributes
JavaScript files block HTML parsing during page load
Multiple synchronous script tags in critical rendering path
Large CSS/JS files loaded before content appears
negative_signals: CSS minified and loaded asynchronously where possible
JavaScript uses async or defer attributes
Critical CSS inlined for above-fold content
Non-critical resources loaded after initial paint
issues.recommendation: Eliminate render-blocking resources by deferring non-critical JavaScript (add defer or async attributes), moving critical CSS inline for above-the-fold content, and loading the rest asynchronously. Use tools like Chrome DevTools Coverage tab to identify unused CSS/JS on initial load.
acceptance_criteria: Zero render-blocking JavaScript resources on homepage per Lighthouse audit
Critical CSS for above-the-fold content is inlined or loaded with high priority
Non-critical CSS loaded with media='print' trick or link rel=preload
Lighthouse Performance score improves by at least 10 points post-fix
First Contentful Paint (FCP) reduced by at least 500ms

issues.issue_title: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) issues
issues.user_problem: Content jumps around during page load causing misclicks and frustration
signals_to_detect: Images load without defined width/height causing layout shifts
Ads or embeds insert above existing content pushing it down
Web fonts load late causing text reflow
Dynamic content injected without reserved space
negative_signals: All images have explicit width and height attributes
Space reserved for ads and dynamic content before loading
Font loading uses font-display: swap with fallback metrics
CLS score < 0.1 on PageSpeed Insights
issues.recommendation: Fix CLS by explicitly setting width and height attributes on all images and video embeds so the browser reserves space before assets load. Reserve space for dynamically injected content (ads, banners, consent bars) using min-height. Use font-display: optional or font-display: swap with a system fallback to prevent text reflow.
acceptance_criteria: CLS score below 0.1 on both mobile and desktop in Lighthouse
All images and iframes have explicit width and height attributes in HTML
Dynamically injected content (ads, banners) has reserved layout space
Web fonts load without causing visible text reflow
CLS measured and passing in Google Search Console Core Web Vitals report

issues.issue_title: Large JavaScript bundles impacting performance
issues.user_problem: Slow page interactivity due to excessive JavaScript download and execution
signals_to_detect: JavaScript bundle size exceeds 200KB (uncompressed)
Total Blocking Time (TBT) > 300ms
Unused JavaScript detected in coverage analysis
No code splitting or lazy loading implemented
negative_signals: JavaScript bundles under 150KB with code splitting
Route-based code splitting for multi-page apps
Third-party scripts loaded asynchronously
Tree shaking removes unused code
issues.recommendation: Reduce JavaScript bundle size by implementing code splitting (split by route or component), tree-shaking unused library exports, and lazy loading non-critical components. Audit the bundle with tools like webpack-bundle-analyzer to identify the largest contributors and remove or defer them.
acceptance_criteria: Initial JavaScript bundle under 150KB gzipped for the critical path
Total Blocking Time (TBT) below 200ms on desktop Lighthouse test
Route-level code splitting implemented so pages only load what they need
Third-party scripts deferred or loaded asynchronously
Unused JavaScript below 20% of total JS loaded per Chrome Coverage audit

issues.issue_title: Unoptimized images (large file sizes)
issues.user_problem: Slow page load and data usage due to unnecessarily large image files
signals_to_detect: Images exceed 200KB without compression
High-resolution images served at small display sizes
No modern formats (WebP, AVIF) used
No responsive images with srcset attribute
negative_signals: Images compressed and optimized for web delivery
Modern image formats served with fallbacks
Responsive images using srcset for different screen sizes
Lazy loading implemented for below-fold images
issues.recommendation: Compress all images using modern formats (WebP for photos, AVIF where supported), serve appropriately sized images using srcset and sizes attributes, and implement maximum quality settings of 75–85% for lossy compression. Automate optimisation in the build pipeline or CMS upload flow to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All images served in WebP or AVIF format with JPEG/PNG fallback
No image exceeds 200KB for standard product photography
srcset attribute provides at least 3 size variants (400w, 800w, 1200w) for key images
Lighthouse 'Properly size images' and 'Use modern image formats' audits pass
Total image payload on homepage below 1MB

issues.issue_title: Unoptimized web font loading
issues.user_problem: Flash of invisible text (FOIT) or flash of unstyled text (FOUT) during font load
signals_to_detect: Custom fonts loaded without font-display property
Multiple font weights/styles loaded unnecessarily
Fonts loaded from slow external CDNs
No font preloading for critical text
negative_signals: Font-display: swap used to show fallback fonts immediately
Only necessary font weights and styles loaded
Critical fonts preloaded with <link rel='preload'>
Fonts subset to include only used characters
issues.recommendation: Add font-display: swap (or font-display: optional for body text) to all @font-face declarations to prevent FOIT. Preload the most critical font files using <link rel='preload' as='font'>. Subset fonts to include only the character ranges actually used on the site.
acceptance_criteria: font-display: swap applied to all custom @font-face declarations
Primary heading and body fonts preloaded in the <head>
No visible flash of invisible text (FOIT) on page load
Font file sizes reduced by subsetting to used character sets (target: under 50KB per font file)
Lighthouse 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' audit passes

issues.issue_title: No lazy loading for images or videos
issues.user_problem: Initial page load slowed by loading all media upfront
signals_to_detect: All images loaded immediately regardless of viewport position
Below-fold images load before user scrolls to them
No loading='lazy' attribute on img tags
Videos load on page load instead of when visible
negative_signals: Images use loading='lazy' attribute for below-fold content
Intersection Observer used for progressive image loading
Videos load only when scrolled into view
Above-fold images load immediately, below-fold lazily
issues.recommendation: Implement lazy loading for all images and videos that appear below the fold using the native loading='lazy' attribute on and
acceptance_criteria: loading='lazy' attribute present on all below-fold images and iframes
Hero and above-fold images explicitly excluded from lazy loading (loading='eager' or no attribute)
Lighthouse 'Defer offscreen images' audit passes
Initial page payload (images) reduced by at least 40% on image-heavy pages
No layout shift (CLS increase) introduced by lazy loaded elements

issues.issue_title: Third-party scripts blocking performance
issues.user_problem: Page performance degraded by slow or excessive third-party scripts
signals_to_detect: Multiple analytics/tracking scripts loaded synchronously
Third-party scripts account for >50% of JavaScript execution time
Social media widgets impact Time to Interactive
Ad scripts block rendering or cause layout shifts
negative_signals: Third-party scripts loaded asynchronously
Tag managers used to control script loading
Non-critical scripts deferred until after page interactive
Third-party impact monitored and optimized
issues.recommendation: Audit all third-party scripts (chat widgets, analytics, A/B testing, social embeds) using WebPageTest's waterfall view. Remove unused scripts entirely, load remaining scripts asynchronously or via a tag manager with a firing delay (e.g., 3-second delay post-interaction), and use resource hints (dns-prefetch, preconnect) for required third parties.
acceptance_criteria: All third-party scripts loaded asynchronously (async or defer attributes)
Non-essential scripts (live chat, social) deferred by at least 3 seconds or triggered on user interaction
Total third-party script payload below 300KB gzipped
Third-party scripts do not appear in the critical rendering path
Lighthouse 'Reduce the impact of third-party code' audit shows improvement

issues.issue_title: No caching strategy implemented
issues.user_problem: Repeat visits slow due to re-downloading unchanged resources
signals_to_detect: Static assets served without cache headers
Cache-Control headers missing or set to no-cache
No ETags for resource validation
Service worker not implemented for offline caching
negative_signals: Appropriate cache headers set for static assets
Versioned assets use long-term caching (1 year)
Dynamic content uses validation caching
Service worker caches critical resources
issues.recommendation: Implement a caching strategy using appropriate Cache-Control headers: long max-age (1 year) with content-hashing for static assets (JS, CSS, images), and shorter max-age (minutes to hours) for HTML. Use a CDN with edge caching for static assets. Implement service worker caching for returning visitors where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Static assets (JS, CSS, images) served with Cache-Control: max-age=31536000 and immutable
HTML pages served with appropriate Cache-Control (no-cache or short max-age)
CDN in place serving static assets from edge locations
Lighthouse 'Serve static assets with an efficient cache policy' audit passes
Repeat visit load time at least 50% faster than first visit in WebPageTest

issues.issue_title: No progressive enhancement strategy
issues.user_problem: Site broken or unusable when JavaScript fails or is disabled
signals_to_detect: Site completely non-functional without JavaScript
Core content not accessible if JS fails to load
Forms don't work without JavaScript
Navigation breaks when JavaScript disabled
negative_signals: Core content accessible without JavaScript
Forms have server-side fallbacks
Critical features work with HTML/CSS alone
JavaScript enhances but isn't required for basic functionality
issues.recommendation: Adopt a progressive enhancement approach: build core content and navigation as functional HTML, layer CSS for visual enhancement, and use JavaScript only to enrich existing functionality rather than create it. Test the site with JavaScript disabled to confirm core journeys (browse, view product, contact) remain functional.
acceptance_criteria: Core content (product listings, descriptions, contact info) visible with JavaScript disabled
Main navigation functional without JavaScript
Forms submit and show validation without JavaScript reliance
Site tested with JS disabled in Chrome DevTools — no blank pages or empty containers
Error handling in place for failed script loads (try/catch, noscript fallbacks)

issues.issue_title: Server response time too slow
issues.user_problem: Long wait for server to respond before page can start loading
signals_to_detect: Time to First Byte (TTFB) exceeds 600ms
Server processing time >500ms
Database queries not optimized
No CDN or edge caching for static content
negative_signals: TTFB under 200ms for static pages
Database queries optimized with indexing
CDN used for global content delivery
Server-side caching reduces processing time
issues.recommendation: Profile server response time using WebPageTest TTFB measurement and identify the bottleneck: database query time, server-side rendering time, or hosting tier limits. Implement server-side caching (Redis, Memcached, or full-page cache), upgrade hosting if necessary, and ensure a CDN is used for HTML delivery where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: TTFB below 200ms for cached pages and below 600ms for uncached pages
Server-side caching implemented for database queries and rendered pages
CDN used for HTML delivery on high-traffic pages
TTFB consistent across repeat measurements (no high variance indicating resource contention)
Google Search Console Core Web Vitals shows TTFB in 'Good' category

issues.issue_title: No resource hints (preconnect, prefetch)
issues.user_problem: Missed opportunity to improve load performance with resource hints
signals_to_detect: No preconnect hints for third-party domains
Critical resources not preloaded
DNS prefetch not used for external resources
No prefetch for likely next navigation
negative_signals: Preconnect used for critical third-party origins
Preload used for critical fonts and CSS
DNS prefetch implemented for external domains
Prefetch used for anticipated next-page resources
issues.recommendation: Add resource hints to the <head> of all pages: use dns-prefetch and preconnect for critical third-party origins (fonts, analytics, CDNs), and prefetch or preload for resources the browser will definitely need on the next navigation step (e.g., checkout CSS, product image).
acceptance_criteria: preconnect hints added for all critical third-party origins (Google Fonts, CDN, analytics)
dns-prefetch added for secondary third-party origins
Key above-fold resources (hero image, primary CSS) preloaded with rel=preload
Resource hints do not create redundant connections (audit with Chrome DevTools Network tab)
Lighthouse 'Preconnect to required origins' audit passes

issues.issue_title: Excessive DOM size impacting performance
issues.user_problem: Page interactions slow due to large DOM tree
signals_to_detect: DOM tree exceeds 1500 nodes
Maximum DOM depth exceeds 32 levels
Parent nodes with >60 child elements
Scroll performance degraded by DOM complexity
negative_signals: DOM tree optimized to under 1500 nodes
DOM depth kept shallow (< 20 levels)
Virtualization used for long lists
Unnecessary DOM nodes removed or simplified
issues.recommendation: Reduce DOM size by removing unnecessary wrapper elements, using CSS pseudo-elements instead of DOM nodes for decorative content, and virtualising long lists (product grids, search results) so only visible items are rendered in the DOM. Target under 1,500 total DOM nodes on any single page.
acceptance_criteria: Total DOM nodes below 1,500 on key page types (homepage, PLP, PDP)
DOM depth does not exceed 32 levels
Long lists (product grids >50 items) use virtual scrolling or pagination
Lighthouse 'Avoid an excessive DOM size' audit passes
Interaction to Next Paint (INP) improves measurably after DOM reduction

issues.issue_title: Missing ARIA labels and landmarks
issues.user_problem: Screen readers cannot identify page regions and interactive elements
signals_to_detect: No ARIA landmarks (banner, navigation, main, contentinfo)
Interactive elements lack aria-label or aria-labelledby
Form inputs missing associated labels
Dynamic content updates without aria-live regions
negative_signals: ARIA landmarks properly define page structure
All interactive elements have accessible names
Form inputs properly labeled with for/id association
Dynamic content uses aria-live for announcements
issues.recommendation: Add ARIA landmark roles to all key page regions (role='main', role='navigation', role='banner', role='contentinfo', role='search') or use equivalent semantic HTML5 elements (main, nav, header, footer). Add aria-label to all interactive components (carousels, tabs, modals, accordions) that lack visible text labels. Verify with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver).
acceptance_criteria: All key page regions have ARIA landmark roles or semantic HTML equivalents
Every interactive widget (carousel, modal, tab, accordion) has an aria-label or aria-labelledby
Screen reader announces all interactive components correctly (verified with VoiceOver or NVDA)
Axe or WAVE audit shows zero missing ARIA label violations
All icon-only buttons have aria-label describing their action

issues.issue_title: Keyboard navigation not fully supported
issues.user_problem: Users cannot navigate or operate site using keyboard alone
signals_to_detect: Interactive elements not reachable via Tab key
No visible focus indicators on keyboard navigation
Keyboard traps prevent escaping from components
Custom controls don't respond to keyboard commands
negative_signals: All interactive elements keyboard accessible
Clear visible focus indicators on all focusable elements
No keyboard traps, easy to navigate in/out of components
Custom controls support standard keyboard patterns
issues.recommendation: Audit the full site keyboard journey by tabbing through all interactive elements. Fix focus traps in modals (focus must be contained within open modal and returned to trigger on close), ensure all dropdowns and menus are operable with arrow keys, and restore any suppressed focus indicators. Every interactive element must be reachable and operable via keyboard alone.
acceptance_criteria: All interactive elements reachable via Tab key without mouse interaction
Modal dialogs trap focus correctly and return focus to trigger on close
Dropdown menus navigable with arrow keys; Escape key closes them
No keyboard traps — user can always Tab out of any component
Full checkout journey completable using keyboard only (verified by manual test)

issues.issue_title: Semantic HTML not used correctly
issues.user_problem: Poor document structure hinders accessibility and SEO
signals_to_detect: Divs used instead of semantic elements (nav, article, section)
Heading hierarchy broken or skipped (h1 to h4 with no h2/h3)
Lists created with divs instead of ul/ol elements
Tables used for layout instead of data
negative_signals: Semantic HTML5 elements used appropriately
Logical heading hierarchy from h1 to h6
Lists use proper ul/ol/li structure
Tables reserved for tabular data only
issues.recommendation: Audit the HTML structure and replace generic <div> and <span> elements used for structural purposes with appropriate semantic elements: <nav> for navigation, <main> for primary content, <article> for standalone content blocks, <section> for thematic groupings, <ul>/<ol> for lists, and <button> for interactive triggers. Ensure heading hierarchy is logical and unbroken.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation uses <nav> element with aria-label distinguishing multiple nav regions
Primary page content wrapped in <main> element (one per page)
Lists use <ul> or <ol> with <li> children, not <div> sequences
Heading hierarchy is sequential with no skipped levels (h1 → h2 → h3)
HTML5 semantic validator (W3C) shows no structural errors on key page types

issues.issue_title: Form inputs not properly labeled
issues.user_problem: Screen reader users cannot identify form field purposes
signals_to_detect: Input fields lack associated <label> elements
Labels not explicitly connected with for/id attributes
Placeholder text used instead of proper labels
Fieldsets lack <legend> elements for grouping
negative_signals: All form inputs have associated label elements
Labels connected with for/id attributes
Placeholders supplement but don't replace labels
Related fields grouped in fieldsets with legends
issues.recommendation: Associate every form input with a visible <label> element using matching for/id attributes. Never rely solely on placeholder text as a label, as it disappears on input and fails accessibility requirements. For icon-only inputs, use aria-label. Ensure error messages are linked to their field using aria-describedby.
acceptance_criteria: Every form input has an associated <label> element linked by for/id attributes
Placeholder text is supplementary only — not the only label for any field
Icon-only inputs have aria-label describing their purpose
Error messages linked to their input field using aria-describedby
Screen reader announces field label and error message correctly when field is invalid

issues.issue_title: Time-based content without user controls
issues.user_problem: Users cannot pause, stop, or control auto-playing content
signals_to_detect: Carousels auto-advance without pause button
Auto-playing videos cannot be paused
Timed content progresses without user control
Animations or transitions cannot be disabled
negative_signals: Carousels include pause/play controls
Videos provide pause, stop, and volume controls
Users can control timing of content updates
Prefers-reduced-motion respected for animations
issues.recommendation: Add visible play/pause controls to all auto-playing content (carousels, videos, animations). Respect the prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query to disable or reduce all animations for users who have opted out of motion in their OS settings. Ensure audio content can be muted and that no content auto-plays audio without user initiation.
acceptance_criteria: All auto-playing carousels have a visible pause/stop control
Auto-play videos are muted by default; audio cannot start without user action
prefers-reduced-motion media query disables or reduces all animations
Content does not flash more than 3 times per second (seizure safety)
WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) passes for all moving content

issues.issue_title: Link text not descriptive
issues.user_problem: Links lack context about their destination or purpose
signals_to_detect: Generic link text like 'Click here' or 'Read more'
Links only identified by URL
Icon links without text labels or aria-label
Link purpose unclear without surrounding context
negative_signals: Link text describes destination or action
URLs accompanied by descriptive text
Icon links include accessible labels
Link purpose clear from text alone
issues.recommendation: Audit all links site-wide and replace generic anchor text ('click here', 'read more', 'learn more') with descriptive text that communicates the destination or action without surrounding context. For icon-only links, add an aria-label. If the same descriptive phrase is used for different destinations, use aria-label to differentiate them for screen reader users.
acceptance_criteria: No links with generic text ('click here', 'read more') without additional context
All icon-only links have an aria-label attribute describing the destination or action
Links to the same destination use the same text; links to different destinations use different text
Screen reader reads link text in isolation and destination is clear
Axe audit shows zero 'Links must have discernible text' violations

issues.issue_title: Inaccessible PDF or document downloads
issues.user_problem: Downloadable documents not accessible to assistive technologies
signals_to_detect: PDFs lack proper tagging and structure
No alternative accessible format provided (HTML, text)
Scanned PDFs without OCR text layer
Document language not specified
negative_signals: PDFs properly tagged with reading order defined
HTML alternative provided for complex documents
Text layer present in all PDFs
Document language attribute set correctly
issues.recommendation: Audit all downloadable PDFs and documents for accessibility using Adobe Acrobat's Accessibility Checker or the PAC 3 validator. Add proper PDF tagging (reading order, heading structure, alt text for images), set the document language, and provide an HTML alternative for complex documents where full PDF remediation is impractical.
acceptance_criteria: All PDFs pass Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker with zero critical errors
PDFs have defined reading order, document language, and title metadata
Images within PDFs have alt text or are marked as decorative artifacts
HTML alternative provided for any PDF that cannot be fully remediated
Download links indicate file type and size (e.g., 'Policy Guide [PDF, 340KB]')

issues.issue_title: Audio-only or video-only content without alternatives
issues.user_problem: Media without transcripts excludes deaf or blind users
signals_to_detect: Audio podcasts or recordings lack transcripts
Video content without audio description
No text alternative for audio-only content
Visual-only content without text description
negative_signals: Audio content includes full transcripts
Video descriptions available for visual-only information
Text alternatives provided for all media
Captions AND transcripts available
issues.recommendation: Provide text transcripts for all audio-only content and synchronised captions (CC) for all video content that contains speech or meaningful audio. For video-only content (silent demonstrations), provide a text or audio description. Host captions as a separate VTT file for easy updating rather than burning them into the video.
acceptance_criteria: All podcast or audio-only content includes a full text transcript on the same page
All videos containing speech have synchronised closed captions (CC)
Captions are accurate and synchronised (no significant timing offset)
Video-only content has a text description of what is shown
CC toggle visible in the video player controls

issues.issue_title: Complex interactions without keyboard alternatives
issues.user_problem: Advanced UI patterns not operable via keyboard
signals_to_detect: Drag-and-drop without keyboard alternative
Slider controls only work with mouse
Color picker requires mouse interaction
Custom context menus not keyboard accessible
negative_signals: Drag-and-drop includes keyboard alternative (cut/paste)
Sliders operable with arrow keys
All controls have keyboard equivalents
Standard keyboard shortcuts for complex interactions
issues.recommendation: For every drag-and-drop interaction, provide a keyboard-accessible alternative (e.g., cut/paste via context menu or arrow-key reordering). For custom sliders, implement ARIA slider role with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and arrow key support. Test all complex interactions with keyboard-only navigation to confirm full operability.
acceptance_criteria: All drag-and-drop interactions have a documented keyboard-only alternative method
Custom sliders implement ARIA slider role and are operable with arrow keys
Date pickers and calendar widgets navigable by keyboard with arrow keys
All custom interactive components tested with keyboard-only and found fully operable
WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard) passes for all interactive components

issues.issue_title: Content too dense (wall of text)
issues.user_problem: Large text blocks without breaks overwhelm readers and reduce comprehension
signals_to_detect: Paragraphs exceed 6-7 lines without breaks
No subheadings in content longer than 500 words
No visual elements breaking up long text sections
Content lacks white space and breathing room
negative_signals: Paragraphs 3-5 lines maximum for readability
Subheadings every 150-250 words in long content
Images, quotes, or callouts break up text
Adequate white space around and within content blocks
issues.recommendation: Break up long-form content by limiting paragraphs to 3–5 sentences, adding descriptive subheadings every 150–250 words, and using pull quotes, images, or callout boxes to create visual breaks. Increase line-height to 1.5–1.6 and ensure adequate white space between sections. Aim for a reading experience that feels well-paced, not exhausting.
acceptance_criteria: No paragraph exceeds 5 sentences or approximately 7 lines at standard font size
Subheadings appear at least every 250 words in long-form content
Body text line-height is 1.5 or greater
Visual breaks (images, quotes, callouts) used in content over 500 words
Readability score (Flesch-Kincaid) appropriate for target audience (aim for grade 8–10 for general audiences)

issues.issue_title: Poor typography hierarchy
issues.user_problem: Lack of visual distinction between heading levels and body text
signals_to_detect: Headings same size or barely larger than body text
No clear visual hierarchy from h1 to h6
Body text size inconsistent across pages
Insufficient differentiation between text styles
negative_signals: Clear size progression from h1 (largest) to h6
Headings visually distinct from body text (size, weight, spacing)
Consistent body text sizing throughout site
Proper use of font weights and styles for hierarchy
issues.recommendation: Establish a clear typographic hierarchy where the H1 is visibly the largest element, followed by a clear size reduction at each heading level, with body text clearly smaller than the smallest heading. Use font weight, size, and spacing — not just size alone — to differentiate levels. Codify the type scale in the design system to prevent inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: H1 is the visually largest text element on every page
Each heading level (H2, H3, H4) is clearly smaller or lighter than the level above
Body text is visually distinct from H4 and H5 headings
Font size and weight scale documented and applied consistently across all page types
No instances of heading tags used for visual styling rather than semantic structure

issues.issue_title: No table of contents on long pages
issues.user_problem: Users cannot navigate or skim long-form content efficiently
signals_to_detect: Articles >2000 words lack table of contents
Long documentation without jump links
No anchor links to major sections
Users must scroll entire page to find specific topics
negative_signals: Table of contents for articles >1500 words
Jump links to major sections or headings
Sticky/fixed TOC for easy navigation
Progress indicator showing position in long content
issues.recommendation: Add an auto-generated or manually curated table of contents to all pages or articles exceeding 1,500 words. Each TOC entry should be a jump link (anchor) to the corresponding section heading. For very long pages, consider a sticky TOC in a sidebar or a fixed floating TOC on desktop.
acceptance_criteria: Table of contents present on all pages/articles exceeding 1,500 words
Each TOC entry is a working anchor link that jumps to the relevant section
TOC appears near the top of the content, before the main body begins
Sticky or floating TOC available on pages exceeding 3,000 words
TOC updates automatically if section headings change (e.g., CMS-generated)

issues.issue_title: Outdated content without date indicators
issues.user_problem: Users cannot determine content freshness or relevance
signals_to_detect: Articles lack publication dates
Last updated date not shown
Outdated information not flagged
No indication of content age
negative_signals: Publication date clearly displayed
Last updated timestamp shown when applicable
Outdated content flagged or archived
Date formats consistent and unambiguous
issues.recommendation: Display a visible 'last updated' or published date on all content pages (articles, guides, policies, FAQs). For time-sensitive content (news, reports, regulations), show the date prominently near the title. Implement a content review schedule and archive or update pages that have not been reviewed in over 12 months.
acceptance_criteria: Published and/or last-updated date visible on all articles, guides, and policy pages
Date displayed near the page title or byline, not hidden in page metadata
Content older than 12 months reviewed, updated, or marked as archived
Date format is unambiguous (e.g., '14 March 2025' not '03/04/25')
Schema.org datePublished and dateModified markup present in page structured data

issues.issue_title: Missing author attribution
issues.user_problem: Credibility reduced by lack of author information
signals_to_detect: Articles or blog posts lack author names
No author bio or credentials shown
Multiple authors not distinguished
No contact or social links for authors
negative_signals: Author name displayed prominently
Author bio with credentials available
Multiple authors clearly attributed
Links to author profiles or social media
issues.recommendation: Add a clear author byline to all editorial, blog, and guide content showing the author's name, role or credentials, and a link to their author profile or bio page. For collaborative content, attribute all contributors. Author attribution is particularly important for YMYL (Your Money Your Life) content categories (health, finance, legal).
acceptance_criteria: Author name visible near title or top of page for all editorial content
Author's role or credentials stated alongside their name
Author profile page accessible via link from the byline
Multiple contributors credited where applicable
Schema.org author markup present in page structured data

issues.issue_title: Broken internal links
issues.user_problem: Navigation disrupted by links pointing to non-existent pages
signals_to_detect: Links return 404 errors
Internal links point to moved or deleted content
Anchor links don't jump to correct page section
Redirects chain through multiple URLs
negative_signals: All internal links functional and tested
Redirects in place for moved content
Anchor links work correctly
Regular link checking process implemented
issues.recommendation: Run a full crawl of the site using a tool such as Screaming Frog or Sitebulb to identify all internal 4xx links. Fix broken links by updating destinations to the correct current URL, setting up 301 redirects for moved pages, and implementing a scheduled monthly link audit to catch regressions. Set up Google Search Console monitoring for crawl errors.
acceptance_criteria: Zero 4xx internal links identified by a crawl tool post-fix
301 redirects in place for all moved or renamed pages
Monthly scheduled crawl or automated monitoring configured
Google Search Console shows no internal 404 crawl errors
Anchor links (in-page) verified to point to existing section IDs

issues.issue_title: Content width too wide for comfortable reading
issues.user_problem: Line length exceeds optimal range causing reading fatigue
signals_to_detect: Text content exceeds 90 characters per line
Full-width text on large screens
No max-width constraint on content columns
Reading experience uncomfortable on desktop
negative_signals: Text content 60-75 characters per line optimal
Max-width applied to content areas (600-750px)
Comfortable reading experience across screen sizes
Proper column width for text-heavy pages
issues.recommendation: Apply a max-width of 65–75 characters (approximately 600–750px at 16px base font size) to all body text columns. On large screens, use CSS max-width on the content container rather than constraining the full-page layout, so the overall page can be wider while reading columns remain comfortable. Test across viewport sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Body text columns constrained to a max-width of 65–75 characters per line
max-width applied to text containers, not the full page layout
Line length comfortable on desktop (1280px), laptop (1024px), and tablet (768px)
No full-width paragraphs of text on viewports wider than 1200px
Reading experience tested and validated at 1440px wide viewport

issues.issue_title: No scannable content format (bullets, lists)
issues.user_problem: Information difficult to scan due to paragraph-only format
signals_to_detect: Key points buried in paragraphs
No use of bulleted or numbered lists
Comparisons not presented in tables or lists
Step-by-step instructions in paragraph form
negative_signals: Key points highlighted in bulleted lists
Numbered lists for sequential information
Comparison tables for multiple options
Scannable format improves information findability
issues.recommendation: Reformat long-form content to use bulleted lists for 3+ parallel items, numbered lists for sequential steps, and comparison tables for multi-option information. Break dense paragraphs into shorter ones with clear topic sentences. Ensure that key takeaways, steps, and features are visually scannable without requiring the user to read every word.
acceptance_criteria: Lists of 3+ items formatted as <ul> or <ol> rather than comma-separated prose
Step-by-step instructions use numbered lists
Comparison information presented in a table, not paragraph form
Key points or takeaways highlighted in a callout box or bulleted summary
Users can extract the key information from any page section by scanning (no full-read required)

issues.issue_title: Unclear site structure and information architecture
issues.user_problem: Users cannot understand how content is organized or find what they need
signals_to_detect: No clear hierarchy or organization visible
Related content not grouped logically
Category structure confusing or overlapping
Users cannot predict where to find information
negative_signals: Clear, logical information hierarchy
Related content grouped in obvious categories
Category structure intuitive and non-overlapping
Predictable navigation patterns throughout site
issues.recommendation: Conduct a card-sorting exercise or tree test with representative users to validate the current information architecture. Restructure navigation categories so they are mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive, and labelled in user language (not internal jargon). Limit top-level navigation to 7 ± 2 items and ensure each section label clearly predicts its contents.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level navigation items limited to 5–7 categories
Category labels use customer-facing language, not internal product names
Each category contains only logically related content (no overlap)
User testing with 5 representative users shows successful task completion rate of 80%+ for key navigational tasks
Site map updated to reflect new IA and reviewed with stakeholders before implementation

issues.issue_title: Missing sitemap (HTML and XML)
issues.user_problem: Users and search engines cannot discover all site content
signals_to_detect: No HTML sitemap for users
No XML sitemap for search engines
Sitemap not linked from footer or help
Sitemap outdated or incomplete
negative_signals: HTML sitemap available for users
XML sitemap submitted to search engines
Sitemap linked in footer or accessible area
Sitemap regularly updated with new content
issues.recommendation: Create an HTML sitemap page listing all key site sections and pages, linked from the footer. Submit an XML sitemap to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. Keep the XML sitemap updated automatically via the CMS and exclude noindex pages. Verify the sitemap is listed in the robots.txt file.
acceptance_criteria: HTML sitemap page exists and is linked from the footer
XML sitemap submitted to and verified in Google Search Console
XML sitemap auto-updates when new pages are published
Sitemap listed in robots.txt (Sitemap: directive)
Sitemap excludes noindex pages, redirects, and 4xx URLs

issues.issue_title: Mega menu too complex or cluttered
issues.user_problem: Overwhelming navigation menu reduces findability
signals_to_detect: Mega menu shows 50+ links simultaneously
No visual grouping or categorization in mega menu
Mega menu covers entire viewport
Users overwhelmed by navigation choices
negative_signals: Mega menu organized into clear categories
Visual grouping and hierarchy in menu structure
Reasonable number of links per section (<15)
Featured or popular items highlighted
issues.recommendation: Simplify the mega menu by reducing the number of top-level categories, removing rarely used links, and grouping remaining items into clearly labelled sub-columns of no more than 6–8 items each. Add visual hierarchy through column headings and consider featuring a hero image or promotional tile in the menu to guide users to priority sections.
acceptance_criteria: Each mega menu column contains no more than 8 links
Column headings clearly label the category of links beneath them
Total number of items across all columns is under 40
Menu dismisses on Escape key and clicking outside the menu area
Mobile version of menu is a simplified, fully collapsible accordion — not a scaled-down mega menu

issues.issue_title: Footer missing essential links
issues.user_problem: Important site functions difficult to find
signals_to_detect: Contact page not linked in footer
Privacy policy or terms not in footer
About page not easily accessible
Help or support links missing
negative_signals: Contact information in footer
Legal pages (privacy, terms) linked in footer
About/Company info accessible from footer
Help, FAQ, or support clearly linked
issues.recommendation: Audit the footer and ensure it contains links to: About Us, Contact, Help/FAQ, Shipping Information, Returns Policy, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and social media profiles. Organise links into logical groups with clear column headings. Ensure the footer is consistent across all page templates including checkout.
acceptance_criteria: Footer contains links to all essential policy pages (Privacy, Terms, Returns, Shipping)
Contact information or link present in footer
Footer organised into labelled column groups
Social media profile links present with accessible labels
Footer consistent across all page types including checkout and account pages

issues.issue_title: No 'Back to Top' button on long pages
issues.user_problem: Excessive scrolling required to reach navigation on long pages
signals_to_detect: Long pages (>3 viewports) lack back-to-top button
Users must scroll all way back up manually
No quick navigation to top of page
Back to top button not visible during scroll
negative_signals: Back to top button on pages >2 viewports tall
Button appears/becomes sticky after scrolling down
Smooth scroll animation to top
Button clearly labeled and accessible
issues.recommendation: Add a 'Back to Top' button that appears after the user has scrolled at least 600px down any page taller than 2x the viewport height. The button should be fixed or sticky in the bottom-right corner, visually unobtrusive but clearly identifiable, and animated smoothly back to the top on click.
acceptance_criteria: Back to Top button appears after scrolling 600px or more
Button fixed in bottom-right corner and does not obstruct main content
Button only visible on pages and at scroll depths where it is useful
Smooth scroll animation on click (respects prefers-reduced-motion)
Button accessible via keyboard (Tab-focusable) and announces correctly to screen readers

issues.issue_title: Search not prominent on content-heavy sites
issues.user_problem: Users cannot easily search when browsing fails
signals_to_detect: Search hidden on sites with 50+ pages
Search icon too small or difficult to find
No search on documentation or blog sites
Search not accessible from all pages
negative_signals: Search prominently placed in header
Search icon recognizable and adequately sized
Search available on all pages of content sites
Search encouraged as alternative to navigation
issues.recommendation: Move the search input to a prominent position in the primary header navigation, visible on all pages without any interaction needed to reveal it. On mobile, show a clearly labelled search icon that expands to a full-screen search overlay. Avoid burying search in hamburger menus or secondary navigation on content-heavy sites.
acceptance_criteria: Search input or icon visible in the header on all page types without scrolling
Mobile search expands to a dedicated search overlay or page
Search bar is one of the first 3 interactive elements in the header
Search is reachable in 1 click or tap from any page
Search field receives focus automatically when the search icon is tapped

issues.issue_title: Pagination without page numbers or controls
issues.user_problem: Users cannot navigate multi-page content efficiently
signals_to_detect: Only 'Next/Previous' without page numbers
Cannot jump to specific page number
No indication of total pages or current position
Infinite scroll with no pagination option
negative_signals: Page numbers displayed and clickable
Can jump directly to page number
Total pages and current position shown
Both pagination and 'load more' options available
issues.recommendation: Replace numbered-page-only pagination with a combination of: numbered page links (showing current page and ±2 adjacent pages), a visible total page count, Previous/Next buttons with clear labels, and an optional 'jump to page' input for very long result sets. Ensure the current page number is clearly indicated and that pagination controls are accessible by keyboard.
acceptance_criteria: Numbered page links visible with current page clearly highlighted
Previous and Next buttons labelled with text, not only icons
Total number of pages or results shown
Pagination controls keyboard-navigable (Tab + Enter)
Pagination state reflected in the URL (e.g., ?page=3) for shareability and browser back support

issues.issue_title: No related content or recommendations
issues.user_problem: Users cannot discover related information after consuming content
signals_to_detect: Articles end with no next steps
No 'related articles' or 'you might like' sections
Dead-end pages after content consumption
Missed opportunity to keep users engaged
negative_signals: Related content suggested after main content
Recommendations based on current page topic
Clear next steps or calls-to-action
Cross-linking between related pages
issues.recommendation: Add a 'Related Articles', 'You Might Also Like', or 'Read Next' section at the end of every content page, surfacing 3–5 topically relevant items. Use tag-based or category-based matching at minimum, with algorithmic personalisation where available. Related content should be visually engaging (thumbnail + title + brief description).
acceptance_criteria: Related content section present at the end of all article and content pages
Minimum 3 related items shown with image, title, and brief description
Recommendations are topically relevant, not random or purely popular
Related content section does not contain the current page as a suggestion
Section visible above the footer without excessive scrolling on desktop

issues.issue_title: Navigation doesn't indicate current section
issues.user_problem: Users cannot tell which section of site they're in
signals_to_detect: Active navigation item not visually highlighted
No indication of current section in menu
All navigation items look identical
Users must rely on page content to know location
negative_signals: Active navigation item clearly highlighted
Current section visually distinct in menu
Consistent indication of location across site
Visual cues reinforce user's current position
issues.recommendation: Highlight the active section in the main navigation by applying a visually distinct active state (bold text, underline, colour change, or background highlight) to the current section link. Ensure this state is applied consistently across all navigation levels and is not removed by hover states.
acceptance_criteria: Active/current section link is visually distinct from inactive navigation links
Active state uses at least 2 visual cues (e.g., bold + colour, or underline + background)
Active state persists and is not overridden by hover styles
Active state applied to all navigation levels (primary nav, mega menu columns, mobile menu)
Current-page state programmatically set using aria-current='page' for accessibility

issues.issue_title: Search results do not prioritise exact matches
issues.user_problem: Users searching for a specific item by its exact name receive it ranked below less relevant results, reducing trust in search
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Searching for an exact product title returns that product ranked 2nd or lower
Partial keyword matches ranked above exact title matches in search results
Searching for a known item by its precise name does not surface it on page 1
Search results order appears arbitrary or algorithm-driven without relevance weighting for exact matches
issues.recommendation: Configure the search engine to boost exact title matches to rank first above partial or fuzzy matches. In Elasticsearch or Solr, use a match_phrase query with a higher boost value for title fields than body/description fields. Add a 'best_fields' or 'cross_fields' multi-match strategy ensuring exact title hits are always surfaced before broad keyword matches. Regularly audit search result order by running known exact-match queries and verifying top placement.
acceptance_criteria: Searching for an exact product or content title surfaces that item as the first result
Exact phrase matches outrank partial keyword matches in all result sets
Search relevance audit using 20 known exact-match queries shows top-1 accuracy of 90%+
Search configuration documented with boost values for title, description, and tag fields
Search result quality monitored via zero-click rate and position-1 CTR in analytics
negative_signals: Exact title search returns that item as the first result
Search engine configuration shows title fields have highest boost weight
Search audit confirms top-1 accuracy for known exact-match queries
issues.context_notes: Test by searching for a known exact product or article title and checking its rank position. Do not flag: Sites with very small catalogues where ranking variation is negligible. Industry context: Poor exact-match ranking is a significant trust issue, particularly for returning users who know what they are looking for.

issues.issue_title: Search result count not shown at top of results
issues.user_problem: Users cannot assess the size of a result set before scrolling, making it impossible to know if they need to refine their search
signals_to_detect: No result count shown at the top of search results or product listing pages
Result count only displayed at the bottom of the page after all results
Pagination shows page numbers but not total result count
Filter application does not update a visible result count
issues.recommendation: Display the total result count prominently at the top of all search results and product listing pages, immediately above the first result. Format as: 'X results for "[search term]"' for search, and 'X products' for category PLPs. Update the count dynamically when filters are applied so users always know how many items match their current selection.
acceptance_criteria: Total result count displayed at the top of all search results pages before the first result
Result count shown at the top of all PLPs above the product grid
Count updates dynamically when filters are applied without page reload
Format communicates both count and context (e.g., '42 results for "blue coat"' not just '42')
Result count visible on both desktop and mobile without scrolling
negative_signals: Result count visible at top of search results before first result
Count updates dynamically when filters change
Format includes search term or category context alongside the number
issues.context_notes: Check both search results and category PLP pages. Do not flag: Sites where result count is shown inline within the filter panel but not above the grid — flag as secondary recommendation only. Industry context: Result count is a standard ecommerce and search UI pattern that sets user expectation before they invest time browsing.

issues.issue_title: Accordion component unclear grouping and multi-open behaviour
issues.user_problem: Users cannot easily find content in accordions when multiple sections open simultaneously or when spacing fails to communicate which content belongs to which header
signals_to_detect: Multiple accordion sections can be expanded simultaneously creating a wall of content
Accordion header and its expanded content not visually grouped — insufficient spacing or border
No clear indicator (chevron, +/− icon) showing which sections are open vs closed
Accordion expand/collapse icon does not change state visually when activated
Sections with no content are clickable and expand to show nothing
issues.recommendation: Implement accordion components with single-expand behaviour by default (opening one section closes others) unless multi-open is explicitly justified by the content. Use a visible chevron or +/− icon that rotates or changes on expand. Apply a clear visual boundary between accordion rows using borders or background colour shifts. Increase the internal padding so the expanded content is clearly associated with its header. Disable or visually mute accordion items that have no content.
acceptance_criteria: Opening one accordion section closes any previously open section (single-expand mode)
Accordion toggle icon visually changes state between open and closed (e.g., chevron rotates 180°)
Expanded content visually grouped with its header via border, background, or padding
Accordion items with no available content are visually muted or non-interactive
Accordion is keyboard navigable: Tab to focus header, Enter/Space to expand, Escape to collapse
negative_signals: Only one accordion section open at a time
Chevron or icon clearly indicates open/closed state
Content visually grouped with its accordion header
Empty accordion items non-interactive or clearly labelled as unavailable
issues.context_notes: Check accordion components on PDP (product details, FAQs, specifications) and any content pages using accordions for navigation. Do not flag: Multi-open accordions used intentionally for comparison-style content where seeing multiple sections simultaneously is the user need. Industry context: Poorly implemented accordions are particularly damaging on mobile where vertical space is limited.

issues.issue_title: Entire card or row not clickable — only title or icon is interactive
issues.user_problem: Users who click the image, background, or body of a content card receive no response, creating confusion about whether the element is interactive
signals_to_detect: Clicking the product image on a card does not navigate to the product page
Only the title text link on a card is interactive — surrounding area is not
Row-based list items only have a small arrow or chevron as the interactive target
Table rows or data cards are highlighted on hover but only part of the row is clickable
Cursor does not change to pointer when hovering over non-title card areas
issues.recommendation: Wrap the entire card or row in a single anchor element or apply a click handler to the full card container, making the whole area a consistent tap/click target. Use CSS to ensure the cursor shows as pointer on hover across the full card. If a card contains multiple distinct links (e.g., product name + 'Quick view'), use the anchor overlay technique: make the primary link cover the full card with position: absolute, and layer secondary links on top with a higher z-index.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking anywhere on a product or content card navigates to the correct destination
Cursor changes to pointer on hover across the full card area, not just the title
All interactive table rows are fully clickable — not only the trailing arrow
Cards containing multiple links use the anchor overlay pattern with correct z-index layering
Full-card click tested on desktop (mouse) and mobile (touch) — both work correctly
negative_signals: Clicking anywhere on the card navigates correctly
Pointer cursor visible on hover across the full card area
Table rows fully interactive — not only the arrow target
issues.context_notes: Test by clicking the image, padding, and non-title text areas of product cards. Do not flag: Cards with a deliberate 'Click the title to open' design pattern where the card serves as an information display, not a navigation element — but this must be visually obvious. Industry context: Clickable cards are a fundamental ecommerce pattern; partial clickability significantly increases mis-tap rates on mobile.

issues.issue_title: File type icons unrecognisable and file size not shown on downloads
issues.user_problem: Users cannot identify what type of file they are about to download or how large it is, leading to unexpected downloads and wasted time
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Download links show a generic icon that does not indicate the file format (PDF, XLSX, DOCX, etc.)
File size not displayed alongside download links or buttons
Multiple file types presented with identical icons creating ambiguity
Download CTA label says only 'Download' with no format or size context
Hovering over download link does not reveal file type or size in tooltip
issues.recommendation: Display a recognisable file-type icon (use the widely recognised PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint iconography) alongside every downloadable file link. Show the file size in human-readable format (e.g., '2.4 MB') adjacent to the link. Include the file extension in the link label or as a badge (e.g., 'Download Report [PDF, 1.2 MB]'). For multiple downloads on one page, use a consistent card layout with icon + title + format badge + file size.
acceptance_criteria: Every downloadable file displays a recognisable file-type icon (PDF, Word, Excel, etc.)
File size shown in human-readable format (KB or MB) adjacent to every download link
File extension included in the link label or as a visible badge
Multiple file types on the same page use distinct, recognisable icons — not the same generic icon
Download links tested with 5 users who can identify file type and size before clicking
negative_signals: Recognisable file-type icons visible on all download links
File size shown adjacent to all download links
Format badge or extension included in download label
issues.context_notes: Check pages with downloadable assets: product spec sheets, policy documents, reports. Do not flag: Single-type download pages where the format is obvious from context. Industry context: File size is particularly important for mobile users on limited data plans. File type clarity reduces accidental downloads of wrong formats.

issues.issue_title: Chart and graph data labels missing on hover
issues.user_problem: Users cannot read specific data point values from charts without hover labels, making data visualisations decorative rather than informative
signals_to_detect: Hovering over chart data points shows no tooltip or data label
Charts display trend lines or bars but no numeric values are visible anywhere
Data labels only visible in a legend with no way to tie them to individual data points
Charts have interactive states (cursor changes) but no data is revealed on interaction
Chart axis labels too small or absent, leaving scale uninterpretable
issues.recommendation: Implement hover tooltips on all interactive chart data points showing: the exact numeric value, the data series name, and the x-axis category or date. For bar and column charts, consider always-on data labels for the most important values. Ensure charts meet WCAG contrast requirements for all text and graphical elements. Provide a table view alternative for complex charts so users can access the underlying data without relying on visual interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering over any data point on a chart reveals a tooltip with: value, series name, and axis label
Tooltip appears within 300ms of hover on desktop and on tap on mobile
Chart axis labels are legible at default zoom (minimum 12px font, sufficient contrast)
A data table view or 'View data' toggle is available for charts with more than 10 data points
Chart tooltips and labels pass WCAG 2.1 AA colour contrast for text on tooltip background
negative_signals: Hover tooltips present on all chart data points
Tooltips show value, series, and axis context
Data table alternative available for complex charts
Axis labels legible at default zoom level
issues.context_notes: Test by hovering over all chart types on the page. Do not flag: Static charts used as purely decorative illustrations with no data value. Industry context: Particularly important for data-heavy sites (analytics dashboards, statistics portals, financial data pages). Inaccessible charts are also a WCAG 2.1 failure (non-text content without text alternative).

issues.issue_title: Broken or non-functional CTA styled as interactive
issues.user_problem: Users click elements that appear to be buttons or links but nothing happens, causing confusion and eroding trust in the interface
signals_to_detect: Button or link styled with hover state (colour change, underline) but no action fires on click
CTA element present in the DOM but event handler missing or JavaScript error prevents execution
Link element with href='#' or href='' that scrolls to top instead of navigating
Download or action button present but returns 404 or produces no output
Element has pointer cursor on hover but click produces no visible response
issues.recommendation: Audit all interactive elements across key page templates by clicking every button and link and verifying a response occurs. Check the browser console for JavaScript errors on click. Remove or visually disable any CTAs whose functionality has not yet been implemented — use a disabled state with a tooltip explaining when the feature will be available. Never style an element as interactive if it has no current function.
acceptance_criteria: Every button and link on all key pages produces a visible and expected response on click
No JavaScript errors in the browser console triggered by CTA interactions
Non-functional elements use a visually disabled state (greyed out, no pointer cursor)
href='#' links either removed or replaced with a correct anchor or page destination
Regular CTA audit conducted as part of QA before each release
negative_signals: All buttons and links produce a consistent and expected response on click
No JavaScript console errors on CTA interaction
Non-functional elements visually disabled and explained
issues.context_notes: Open browser DevTools console while clicking all interactive elements. Do not flag: Intentional disabled states that are visually communicated (grey, no pointer cursor, aria-disabled). Industry context: Broken CTAs on checkout or payment pages are critical severity — flag as Critical if found in conversion flow.

issues.issue_title: Page title does not match the navigation label that triggered it
issues.user_problem: Users who click a navigation item arrive on a page with a different title, making them uncertain whether they are in the right place
signals_to_detect: Navigation menu item label and the H1 or page title of the destination page differ significantly
Breadcrumb label for a page does not match the page's own H1 heading
Category page title shows a generic term (e.g., 'Products') instead of the specific category clicked
Sub-navigation items link to pages with different or more generic titles than the link text
issues.recommendation: Audit all primary and secondary navigation items by clicking each one and comparing the navigation label to the destination page H1 and browser tab title.
