issues.recommendation: Replace star-based voting on individual reviews with a simple binary upvote/downvote or 'Was this helpful? Yes / No' mechanism. Position the helpfulness vote beneath the review text with a clear label. Reserve star ratings exclusively for product ratings — never use them for review-level interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Review helpfulness uses 'Yes/No' or thumbs up/down — not a star rating
'Was this review helpful?' label visible adjacent to the voting control
No star rating control on individual review cards — stars reserved for product ratings only
User testing confirms 100% of users correctly understand the review helpfulness control
Helpfulness vote counts visible to show most-upvoted reviews
negative_signals: Helpfulness voting uses binary Yes/No or thumbs
No star rating on individual review cards
Label clearly identifies control as review helpfulness
issues.context_notes: Check review sections on PDPs for any star-based voting on individual reviews.

issues.issue_title: Important information buried within promotional content and easily overlooked
issues.user_problem: Operational or trust-building information (delivery details, policy highlights, USPs) embedded within promotional banners is missed by users who apply banner blindness
signals_to_detect: Delivery promise, returns policy, or trust signal placed inside a promotional offer carousel or banner
Key USP placed between product offers in a scrolling section
Policy or support information only accessible through a rotating banner
Important operational update placed in a promotional content zone
issues.recommendation: Separate operational and trust information from promotional content. Use a dedicated 'benefits bar' or 'USP strip' (a persistent horizontal bar above or below the hero) for free delivery thresholds, returns policies, and trust signals. Never embed operational messages in rotating carousels. Place time-sensitive operational updates in a dedicated, non-promotional site notice bar.
acceptance_criteria: Free delivery threshold, returns policy, and key USPs in a dedicated persistent benefits bar — not inside promotional banners
No operational or trust information exclusively accessible through rotating carousel content
Time-sensitive service notices in a dedicated site notice bar above the main navigation
Benefits bar visible without scrolling on desktop and mobile
User testing confirms key USPs noticed and recalled by 80%+ of homepage visitors
negative_signals: USPs and trust info in dedicated persistent benefits bar
No critical information only in promotional carousels
Service notices in dedicated notice bar
issues.context_notes: Check whether delivery information, returns, or trust signals are only accessible via carousel slides. Industry context: Information inside carousels is missed by 40–60% of users due to banner blindness.

issues.issue_title: Partial translation — English content persists on pages in a non-English language
issues.user_problem: Pages in a non-English language contain untranslated English strings, undermining the localisation experience
signals_to_detect: Product specification labels on an Arabic page rendered in English
Newly added UI component text not included in the translation workflow — shows in the default language
Error messages appearing in English on a localised Arabic or French page
Category filter labels or sorting options untranslated on non-English pages
Technical metadata imported from a supplier in English with no translation applied
issues.recommendation: Add a translation completeness audit to the release process for all non-English locales. Implement automated string detection that flags any hardcoded or missing translation keys before deployment. Ensure all product data import pipelines include a translation step for spec attributes and labels. For supplier-imported technical content, use a translation workflow or machine-translation fallback with human QA.
acceptance_criteria: All user-facing strings on non-English pages are in the correct locale language
Automated translation key coverage check runs before every deployment
Product spec attributes translated for all localised pages
Translation workflow covers all content types: UI strings, product data, error messages, metadata
Language QA checklist completed for all new features before release in any non-English market
negative_signals: No English strings visible on fully localised pages
Translation key coverage check passes before deployment
Product specs fully translated on all localised pages
issues.context_notes: Switch to a non-English language and check product specification sections, filter labels, and error messages. Do not flag: Internationally recognised brand names or product model numbers — these are conventionally left in original form.

issues.issue_title: Multiple overlays or banners simultaneously block content with no way to close
issues.user_problem: Multiple UI components (chatbot, promo coupon, cookie banner, feedback widget) appear simultaneously on the same screen, blocking primary content with no obvious way to dismiss them all
signals_to_detect: Two or more overlay components simultaneously visible on the same page
Primary page content blocked by stacked overlays where none can be individually dismissed
At least one overlay has no visible close or dismiss button
Overlays from different systems stack without coordination
Page cannot be used for its primary purpose without dismissing multiple overlays first
issues.recommendation: Implement an overlay coordination system so only one non-critical overlay appears at a time. Priority order: (1) legal/consent, (2) critical errors, (3) everything else. Non-critical overlays (promos, chatbot, feedback) should be collapsed by default and expand only on user interaction. All overlays must have a visible dismiss control. Chatbots and feedback widgets must be collapsible.
acceptance_criteria: No more than one overlay type visible simultaneously — an overlay queue or priority system in place
All overlay components have a visible and functional close/dismiss control
Chatbot and feedback widgets collapsible to a small icon by default
Promo/coupon overlays do not appear until after cookie consent is acknowledged
Primary page content (above the fold) fully visible without dismissing any overlay on first load
negative_signals: No simultaneous stacked overlays on any page
All overlays have dismiss controls
Chatbot/feedback widgets collapsed by default
Primary content visible on load without overlay dismissal
issues.context_notes: Load key pages in an incognito window and observe how many overlays appear simultaneously. Industry context: Multiple simultaneous overlays are a common consequence of different teams deploying widgets without coordination.

issues.issue_title: Promo or coupon panel auto-expands and obscures page content — cannot be closed
issues.user_problem: A promotional coupon panel opens automatically when the page loads, covers primary content, and has no close or dismiss option
signals_to_detect: A coupon or promotional panel expands automatically without user interaction
Expanded promo panel overlaps the main content banner or product listing
No close, dismiss, or minimise button on the auto-expanded promo panel
Panel re-expands every time user navigates to a new page
Panel appears while user is reading product details or filling a form
issues.recommendation: Change the promo/coupon panel to a collapsed default state — show a small persistent tab or banner with the offer summary, and expand only when the user taps it. Add a close button to dismiss or minimise the panel. Do not re-expand the panel after the user has dismissed it within the same session. Remove promo panels from checkout pages entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Promo panel collapsed by default — visible as a tab or small banner only
Panel expands only on user tap — never auto-expands on page load or scroll
Visible close/minimise button dismisses the panel
Panel stays dismissed for the remainder of the session after close
No promo panel visible on cart, checkout, or form pages
negative_signals: Promo panel collapsed by default
Expands only on user interaction
Has a dismiss button
Stays dismissed for session
Not shown on checkout pages
issues.context_notes: Check whether a promo or coupon panel auto-expands on page load. Industry context: Auto-expanding promo panels interrupt browsing flow and can actually reduce coupon redemption by irritating users.

issues.issue_title: Language change reloads the homepage instead of refreshing the current page
issues.user_problem: When a user switches language, they are redirected to the homepage instead of staying on the page they were viewing, causing loss of context
signals_to_detect: Changing language navigates user to homepage instead of reloading the current page in the new language
Translated URL structure cannot preserve the current page path across language changes
No warning given that changing language will navigate them away from the current page
User loses their place in a product listing, search results, or article when changing language
issues.recommendation: Implement language switching as a page-level reload: preserve the current URL path and switch the language parameter only, reloading the current page in the new language. For URL structures where direct translation is not possible, navigate to the equivalent page in the new language. If homepage redirect is technically unavoidable, alert the user before the switch.
acceptance_criteria: Language change reloads the current page in the new language — not the homepage
URL language parameter changes without changing page path where possible
If homepage redirect unavoidable, a confirmation dialog warns the user first
User position preserved or approximated after language switch
Language switch tested on PDP, PLP, search results, and account pages
negative_signals: Language change reloads current page in new language
No unexpected homepage redirect
Warning shown if redirect unavoidable
issues.context_notes: Test language switching from a PDP or PLP and verify the destination after the switch.

issues.issue_title: No account creation option during checkout — only login or guest
issues.user_problem: Users going through checkout who do not have an account and do not want to check out as a guest have no way to create a new account, missing an opportunity to save their details
signals_to_detect: Checkout entry page offers only 'Sign in' and 'Continue as guest' — no 'Create account' option
New users who want to create an account during checkout cannot do so
Account creation only accessible from a separate registration page outside the checkout flow
Post-purchase account creation not offered on the order confirmation page
issues.recommendation: Add a third option at checkout entry: 'Create an account'. Communicate benefits of creating an account (order tracking, faster future checkout) alongside the CTA. Alternatively, implement post-purchase account creation on the order confirmation page using the email entered during checkout. Ensure new account creation during checkout does not restart the checkout flow.
acceptance_criteria: Checkout entry page offers three options: Sign in, Create account, Continue as guest
Create account flow completable within checkout without leaving the purchase journey
Account benefits listed adjacent to the Create account CTA
Post-purchase account creation offered on order confirmation as an alternative
New account creation during checkout does not restart the checkout flow
negative_signals: 'Create account' option visible at checkout entry
Account benefits communicated adjacent to CTA
Post-purchase account creation offered on confirmation page
issues.context_notes: Test checkout as a new user and check whether account creation is offered.

issues.issue_title: Loyalty or reward points benefit communicated only after user has already opted out
issues.user_problem: Users who choose guest checkout are only told about loyalty points after making their selection, when it is too late to influence their decision
signals_to_detect: Loyalty points notification appears only after user has selected 'Guest checkout'
'You would have earned X points with an account' message shown after guest selection — too late to change decision
Account sign-in benefits not visible on checkout entry screen before user makes their choice
Points or reward information hidden in secondary copy below the checkout options
issues.recommendation: Surface loyalty points and account benefits before the user makes their checkout method choice. On the checkout entry screen, show adjacent to the sign-in and create-account options: 'Earn [X] points on this order worth [£Y]'. The benefit should be specific to the current order value. Do not show this message only after the guest option is selected.
acceptance_criteria: Account benefit statement visible on checkout entry screen before any option is selected
Benefit is order-specific (e.g., 'Earn 120 points on this £40 order') — not generic
Benefit shown adjacent to the Sign in and Create account CTAs — not below Guest checkout
User testing shows loyalty benefit influences checkout method selection measurably
Benefit message does not appear only as a consequence of selecting guest checkout
negative_signals: Account benefit shown before checkout method selection
Benefit is order-specific and shown adjacent to Sign in / Create account CTAs
User testing shows benefit influences checkout method decision
issues.context_notes: Check the checkout entry screen for loyalty/points messaging timing. Do not flag: Sites with no loyalty scheme.

issues.issue_title: Add to cart or buy CTA requires multiple unexpected steps to complete
issues.user_problem: Clicking 'Buy now' or 'Add to cart' triggers multiple intermediate steps or popups that users do not expect, causing confusion and drop-off
signals_to_detect: Clicking 'Buy now' opens an overlay requiring additional selections before anything is added to cart
'Add to cart' triggers a multi-step drawer requiring clicking 'Continue' multiple times with no progress indication
Users must confirm optional add-ons before the core product is added to cart
CTA label says 'Buy' or 'Add to cart' but triggers a configuration flow not a direct cart add
Users in testing express surprise that the CTA did not directly add the item
issues.recommendation: Ensure 'Add to cart' performs exactly what the label says — adds the item to the cart immediately. Move any accessory or add-on upsell to the cart page itself, not as a blocker within the add-to-cart flow. If configuration is required before adding, require it before the CTA becomes active — not after clicking it. 'Buy now' should go directly to checkout, not to an intermediate configuration step.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking 'Add to cart' immediately adds the item to cart
No mandatory multi-step overlay appears after clicking 'Add to cart' for configured products
Add-on and accessory upsells presented on the cart page — not as a blocker in the add-to-cart flow
'Buy now' goes directly to checkout with no intermediate steps after variant selection
User testing confirms 100% of users understand what 'Add to cart' will do before clicking
negative_signals: Add to cart performs immediately on click
No mandatory multi-step overlay post-click
Add-ons offered on cart page not in add-to-cart flow
Buy now goes directly to checkout
issues.context_notes: Test by clicking Add to Cart and Buy Now on multiple product types. Do not flag: Required variant configuration that must be completed before the item can be added — this is correct behaviour.

issues.issue_title: Cart icon badge shows items but cart page is empty — state mismatch
issues.user_problem: Users see a count on the cart icon indicating items are in their cart, but when they open the cart it is empty, creating confusion and loss of trust
signals_to_detect: Cart icon in header shows a non-zero badge count but the cart page shows no items
Cart badge count does not update after items are added or removed
Add to cart action updates the cart icon count but cart page remains empty on navigation
Cart page shows empty state despite the session having active cart items
issues.recommendation: Synchronise the cart badge count with the cart page item count using the same data source. Both must read from the same cart state — never independently. Implement real-time or near-real-time sync between cart state and badge count using the same API call or store state. Test by adding items, navigating away, and returning to confirm count and cart contents match.
acceptance_criteria: Cart icon badge count exactly matches number of items in cart at all times
Adding an item updates both the badge and cart page simultaneously
Removing an item from cart page immediately decrements the badge count
Cart state persists correctly across page navigations within same session
Automated test verifies badge count equals cart item count after add, remove, and page navigation
negative_signals: Badge count matches cart page item count at all times
Adding/removing items updates badge immediately
Cart state consistent across page navigations
issues.context_notes: Add items to cart, navigate to multiple pages, then check the cart — verify badge count matches cart contents.

issues.issue_title: Multi-step product configuration requires manual scrolling — steps not auto-advanced
issues.user_problem: In a sequential configuration flow, completing one step does not scroll the user to the next step, so users who do not scroll miss required options and become stuck
signals_to_detect: After selecting a product option (colour, storage, size) the page does not scroll to the next option
Required subsequent steps are below the fold and users do not realise they need to scroll
CTA remains disabled with no indication that more options below must be selected first
Users in testing fail to complete configuration because they missed steps below the fold
issues.recommendation: After a user completes a configuration step, automatically smooth-scroll to the next step so it enters the viewport. Use a subtle animation or visual pulse on the newly revealed step to draw attention. For mobile, ensure the next step is fully visible after the auto-scroll. Alternatively, use a step-by-step modal or wizard pattern presenting one step at a time.
acceptance_criteria: Completing a configuration step triggers auto-scroll to the next required step
Auto-scroll brings the next step fully into the viewport
Smooth scroll animation used (not instantaneous jump)
Visual pulse or highlight draws attention to the next step
User testing shows 100% of users complete all configuration steps without missing any
negative_signals: Completing a step auto-scrolls to the next step
Next step fully visible after auto-scroll
All users in testing complete configuration without missing steps
issues.context_notes: Test by completing the first step in a product configuration flow and checking whether the page advances to the next step. Do not flag: Short configuration flows where all steps are visible simultaneously.

issues.issue_title: Out-of-stock or 'get stock alert' CTA shown without communicating the item is unavailable
issues.user_problem: A 'Get stock alert' CTA appears on a product without any visual indication that the item is out of stock, leaving users confused about why they cannot add it to cart
signals_to_detect: 'Get stock alert' or 'Notify me when available' CTA present without an 'Out of stock' or 'Currently unavailable' label
Add to cart button absent with no explanation of why
Product status not communicated — page appears functional but cart add is disabled
Stock alert CTA present in product listing without item being flagged as unavailable
issues.recommendation: Always pair a 'Get stock alert' CTA with an explicit, prominent 'Out of stock' or 'Currently unavailable' status label. The status must appear near the top of the product detail area. The Add to Cart button should be visually replaced (not just disabled) by the 'Notify me' CTA so users understand why the primary action has changed.
acceptance_criteria: 'Out of stock' or 'Currently unavailable' label prominently displayed near product title before the CTA area
Add to Cart button visually replaced by 'Notify me when back in stock' — not just disabled
Stock alert CTA only present on items where stock status is simultaneously communicated
Out-of-stock status communicated on product listing card before users click through to PDP
User testing shows 100% of users understand why Add to Cart is absent
negative_signals: Out of stock label prominently shown near product title
Add to Cart replaced (not just disabled) by Notify Me CTA
Status communicated on PLP before user clicks through
issues.context_notes: Check any product showing a stock alert CTA and verify whether an out-of-stock label is also shown. Industry context: Absent stock status combined with a 'Get alert' CTA creates a broken-looking experience.

issues.issue_title: Primary CTA styled as inactive or disabled — visually misleads users
issues.user_problem: The main action button uses a grey or muted visual style that makes it appear disabled, causing users to not click it even when it is the required next step
signals_to_detect: The primary CTA button uses a grey fill or low-contrast style associated with disabled states
'Continue' or 'Proceed' button visually indistinguishable from disabled buttons elsewhere on the page
Users in testing hesitate to click the primary CTA because it looks inactive
Primary CTA does not have a pointer cursor on hover reinforcing the impression it is non-interactive
issues.recommendation: Apply the highest-contrast, most visually prominent style to the primary action button at every step. Never use grey, muted, or low-contrast styling for an active, clickable primary CTA. Reserve those styles exclusively for genuinely disabled states. If a primary CTA must remain inactive until conditions are met, clearly communicate what must be done to activate it.
acceptance_criteria: Primary CTA button uses the highest-contrast style on the screen — never grey or muted
Pointer cursor on hover confirms interactivity of primary CTA on desktop
Disabled state styling exclusively reserved for genuinely non-interactive buttons
If CTA is inactive pending an action, an inline message explains what must be done to activate it
User testing confirms 100% of users immediately identify and click the primary CTA without hesitation
negative_signals: Primary CTA uses high-contrast active styling
Disabled style only used for genuinely non-interactive buttons
Inactive CTAs include explanation of what to do to activate them
issues.context_notes: Check all checkout step CTAs and form submit buttons. Do not flag: CTAs that are genuinely disabled and correctly styled as such.

issues.issue_title: Checkout not quarantined — off-path products and CTAs shown during purchase
issues.user_problem: During checkout, users are shown other products, promotional banners, or navigation CTAs that distract them from completing their purchase, increasing abandonment
signals_to_detect: Product recommendations or cross-sell sections visible on checkout pages
Promotional banners with links to category pages shown within checkout flow
Full site navigation accessible during checkout steps
'Continue shopping' CTAs present on checkout pages
Cart icon with active link to PLP visible during checkout payment step
issues.recommendation: Quarantine the checkout experience: remove full site navigation, product recommendations, and promotional content from all checkout pages. Replace the standard header with a minimal checkout header showing only the logo and a 'secure checkout' trust indicator. Keep the cart floating icon hidden on checkout pages.
acceptance_criteria: Full site navigation hidden on all checkout pages — replaced by minimal logo + secure checkout header
No product recommendations, promotional banners, or category CTAs on any checkout step
Cart floating icon hidden or non-functional on checkout pages
Order summary always visible but no cross-sell on checkout steps
User testing confirms checkout completion rate improves after quarantine implementation
negative_signals: Full navigation removed from checkout pages
No promotional content on checkout steps
Cart icon hidden during checkout
Minimal checkout header in place
issues.context_notes: Check all checkout step pages for any off-path navigation, promotional content, or product recommendations.

issues.issue_title: Complimentary or free item displayed as a regular cart item causing confusion
issues.user_problem: A free gift or promotional add-on appears in the cart as a standard line item with £0 price, making users confused about whether they accidentally added it or are being charged
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Free gift appears in cart with £0.00 price but same visual weight as purchased items
Complimentary add-on displayed identically to regular cart items with no 'Free' or 'Gift' visual differentiation
Users in testing attempt to remove the free item thinking they added it by mistake
Cart line item for a bundle freebie has a 'Remove' button suggesting it is optional
issues.recommendation: Visually differentiate free and complimentary items from regular cart items: use a 'Free' or 'Gift' badge, a different background colour or section, and a label explaining why the item is included. Disable the remove button for items automatically included as part of a promotion. Group free items in a separate 'Your free gifts' section below the purchased items.
acceptance_criteria: Free and promotional items shown in a visually distinct section ('Your free gifts' or equivalent)
'Free' or 'Gift' badge applied to all complimentary cart items
Explanation of why the item is free shown
Remove button disabled or absent on automatically-included promotional items
User testing confirms 100% of users correctly identify free items as complimentary
negative_signals: Free items in visually distinct section with 'Free' badge
Explanation of why item is included shown
Remove button disabled for auto-included promotionals
issues.context_notes: Check the cart when a free gift or promotional add-on is included. Industry context: Free item confusion is particularly common in electronics bundles and subscription welcome offers.

issues.issue_title: Promotional offer persists after it has already been redeemed
issues.user_problem: A promotional banner or CTA continues to display even after the user has already claimed the offer, creating confusion about whether the offer was applied or can be claimed again
signals_to_detect: A 'Get free gift' or 'Claim offer' CTA remains visible after offer has been added to cart
Promotional banner advertising an offer the user has already redeemed still shows
'Add free accessory' CTA active after accessory already added
Discount code field still shows 'Redeem' CTA after code has been successfully applied
issues.recommendation: Update all promotional CTA states after redemption: change 'Claim offer' to 'Offer applied ✓' and disable the CTA, or hide the banner entirely once the offer is in the cart. For discount codes, replace the 'Apply' CTA with a confirmation state. Use the cart/order state to conditionally render promotional CTAs — only show them when the offer is not yet in the user's session.
acceptance_criteria: Promotional CTAs update to a confirmation state ('Applied ✓') immediately after redemption
'Claim offer' CTAs disabled or hidden after offer is in the cart
Discount code field shows confirmation state after successful application
Offer banners hidden or replaced with confirmation messaging when offer already applied
State change triggered in real time — no page refresh required to update promotional CTA state
negative_signals: Promotional CTAs update to confirmation state after redemption
Offer banners hidden or confirmed after claim
Discount field shows confirmation state after application
issues.context_notes: Add a free gift or apply a promo code and verify that relevant CTAs and banners update their state.

issues.issue_title: Product variant selection not reflected in related imagery
issues.user_problem: When a user selects a product variant, the supporting imagery (gallery, what's in the box) continues to show the default variant rather than the selected one
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Selecting a colour variant does not update the product gallery images to the chosen colour
'What's in the box' section shows contents for default configuration regardless of user selection
Product title updates on variant selection but images remain unchanged
Cart shows a product image for the wrong variant that was not selected
issues.recommendation: Bind all variant-dependent visual content (gallery images, 'what's in the box' contents, colour swatches, technical diagrams) to the variant selector state so they all update simultaneously when a selection is made. In the cart, ensure the thumbnail shown matches the selected variant.
acceptance_criteria: All gallery images update to show the selected variant when a colour, model, or configuration is chosen
'What's in the box' contents update to reflect the selected variant
Cart thumbnail shows the correct variant image matching the user's selection
Variant-dependent content updates within 300ms of selection change
User testing confirms selected variant consistently represented across all visual content on PDP and in cart
negative_signals: Gallery images update on variant selection
What's in the box reflects selected variant
Cart thumbnail shows correct variant
All visual content updates within 300ms
issues.context_notes: Test by selecting different colour or model variants and observing all visual content on the page.

issues.issue_title: Product comparison tool requires page refresh to change selection
issues.user_problem: Once users have selected products to compare, they cannot swap a product out for another without refreshing the entire page, losing their other selections in the process
signals_to_detect: Removing a product from comparison tray requires a full page refresh
Adding a new product to an existing comparison selection refreshes the page clearing other selections
'Compare' checkboxes reset when navigating between PLP pages
Comparison state not preserved in URL — lost on back navigation
issues.recommendation: Implement the product comparison feature with client-side state management so products can be added to and removed from the comparison tray without page reloads. Store comparison state in the URL query string. Allow individual item removal via an X button on the comparison tray without affecting other selected items.
acceptance_criteria: Products added to comparison tray without page reload
Individual products removable from comparison tray without affecting other selections or triggering a reload
Comparison state persists in URL query string across PLP page navigation
Comparison tray accessible and editable from any PLP page without losing selections
User testing confirms users can modify comparison selection without losing current selections
negative_signals: Comparison tray updates without page reload
Individual items removable without affecting other selections
Comparison state persists in URL
issues.context_notes: Test by adding 2 products to compare, then trying to swap one out. Industry context: Comparison tools requiring page refreshes are a significant barrier in electronics and appliances.

issues.issue_title: Comparison table difficult to read — excessive spacing or missing visual differentiation
issues.user_problem: When comparing products side-by-side, users must scroll excessively or struggle to match spec rows across columns because the table layout has too much whitespace or insufficient visual alignment
signals_to_detect: Comparison table has excessive vertical spacing between rows making it hard to read across columns
No row striping (alternating row background colours) to help eyes track across the table
Key differentiating specs visually indistinguishable from identical specs
No visual highlight on specs where products differ
Table requires excessive scroll to reach key comparison points
issues.recommendation: Design the comparison table with: alternating row striping, compact row heights (32–40px), visual highlighting on rows where products differ, and sticky column headers showing product names while scrolling. Prioritise key differentiating specs at the top. Use icons (✓, ✗) instead of text ('Yes', 'No') for binary attributes to speed scanning.
acceptance_criteria: Comparison table uses alternating row striping
Rows where compared products differ are visually highlighted
Row height compact (32–40px) — no excessive whitespace
Binary attributes shown as ✓/✗ icons rather than text
Key differentiating specs prioritised at top of table
negative_signals: Row striping present for horizontal tracking
Differentiating rows visually highlighted
Compact row heights — no excessive spacing
Binary attributes shown as icons
issues.context_notes: Access the comparison table and assess row readability. Industry context: Electronics and appliance comparisons involve many spec rows — table readability is critical.

issues.issue_title: Product images pixelated, blurry, or poor quality
issues.user_problem: Product images are low resolution or visibly pixelated at standard size, reducing confidence in the product and the platform's credibility
signals_to_detect: Product images appear pixelated or blurry at standard display size on PLP or PDP
Images visibly low resolution when not zoomed
Supplier-provided images used without quality checking or upscaling
Product thumbnail on PLP noticeably lower quality than hero image on PDP
Images appear stretched or blurry on retina/high-DPI displays
issues.recommendation: Establish minimum image quality standards: minimum 800×800px for product thumbnails, minimum 1600×1600px for PDP hero images. Implement automated image quality checking in the product publishing workflow. For existing low-quality images, prioritise retaking or sourcing higher-resolution versions for top-selling products first. Use srcset and WebP format.
acceptance_criteria: All product images meet minimum resolution standards (800px thumbnail, 1600px hero)
Automated quality check in publishing workflow flags sub-standard images before they go live
No pixelated or blurry images visible on PLP at standard viewing size
Images sharp on retina displays (2x resolution assets provided via srcset)
Image quality standards documented and provided to all suppliers/content teams
negative_signals: All product images sharp and clear at standard viewing size
Minimum resolution standards met across catalogue
Automated quality check in publishing workflow
Images sharp on retina displays
issues.context_notes: View PLPs and PDPs without zooming and assess image sharpness at standard display size. Do not flag: Images that only appear pixelated when zoomed beyond 200%.

issues.issue_title: Wrong font used for Arabic content — causes text to break or render incorrectly
issues.user_problem: Arabic text is displayed using a Latin font that does not support Arabic glyphs, causing letters to appear disconnected or in incorrect positions
signals_to_detect: Arabic text rendered with disconnected letters (each letter appears as an isolated glyph)
Arabic characters displayed in incorrect visual positions
Arabic UI content using a font that does not include Arabic Unicode ranges
Mixed font usage where some Arabic text renders correctly and some does not
Arabic text in dynamically loaded components uses a different font from static content
issues.recommendation: Specify an Arabic-compatible font as the primary font for all pages served to Arabic-locale users. Use a font stack that includes a high-quality Arabic web font (Noto Sans Arabic, Cairo, IBM Plex Arabic, Almarai) with an Arabic system font fallback. Apply the font to all elements including dynamically loaded components. Test Arabic rendering in all major browsers before deploying any font change.
acceptance_criteria: All Arabic text rendered with a connected, readable Arabic script font on all pages
Arabic font applied to dynamically loaded content (search results, chatbot, notifications) as well as static pages
Font stack includes at least one web font and one system fallback both supporting Arabic glyphs
Arabic rendering tested and confirmed correct in Chrome, Safari, and Firefox on iOS and Android
No broken or disconnected Arabic characters visible on any page or component
negative_signals: All Arabic text rendered with correct connected script
Arabic font applied consistently across static and dynamic content
No broken glyphs on any page or device
issues.context_notes: Switch to Arabic language and check all page types for disconnected Arabic characters.

issues.issue_title: Checkout error provides no description or recovery path
issues.user_problem: An error occurs during checkout and the user sees an error state with no explanation of what went wrong or what they should do to resolve it
nielsen_heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
signals_to_detect: Generic 'An error occurred' message with no specifics during checkout
Error message contains a technical code or system message with no plain-language explanation
No recovery action available from the error state — no retry button, no support link
Checkout error clears the form data forcing users to re-enter all information
Error appears during payment step with no clarity on whether the payment was processed
issues.recommendation: Design specific error messages for all known checkout failure modes: payment declined (with suggested next steps), address not recognised (with correction prompt), session timeout (with session restore), and general server error (with retry + support link). Each error must include: (1) plain-language description of what happened, (2) whether any charge was made, (3) a specific recovery action. Never clear form data on checkout errors.
acceptance_criteria: Every checkout error shows a plain-language description of what went wrong
Error messages for payment steps clarify whether the card was charged
Each error includes at least one specific recovery action (retry, correct field, contact support)
Checkout form data preserved on error — no data cleared on payment or validation failures
Error monitoring in place to track checkout error rates by type
negative_signals: All checkout errors show plain-language description and recovery action
Payment errors clarify charge status
Form data preserved on error
Error monitoring active
issues.context_notes: Test checkout with an invalid card number and an invalid address to trigger validation errors. Industry context: Checkout errors without recovery are the leading cause of lost sales that are never recovered.

issues.issue_title: Single-option dropdown not auto-filled — user must select the only available option
issues.user_problem: When a dropdown has only one available option based on prior selections, users must still manually open the dropdown and select it rather than having it auto-fill
signals_to_detect: A district or postcode area dropdown shows only one available option after a city is selected but does not auto-populate
Country selected pre-fills city options but a single-city result still requires manual selection
Form field with a single available value renders as a dropdown requiring user interaction
Users in testing open and close single-option dropdowns mechanically because they have no real choice
issues.recommendation: When a dependent dropdown has only one valid option based on prior selections, auto-fill it immediately and show it as a read-only confirmed field. Display the auto-filled value with a small 'Pre-filled based on your [city/country] selection' note. Allow the user to override it if they need to. Do not render a dropdown at all when there is only one option — use read-only text instead.
acceptance_criteria: Dependent dropdowns with a single valid option are auto-filled without user interaction
Auto-filled fields displayed as read-only with a note explaining why they were pre-filled
Override option available for auto-filled fields where the user may need to change them
No dropdown with a single option renders as a selectable dropdown — shown as read-only text
User testing confirms no unnecessary interaction required for auto-fillable fields
negative_signals: Single-option dropdowns auto-filled without user interaction
Auto-filled fields shown as read-only with explanation
Override available if needed
issues.context_notes: Test by selecting a city or country and checking whether the subsequent district/area dropdown auto-fills when only one option exists.

issues.issue_title: Favourite or wishlist action cannot be undone inline — requires navigating to a separate page
issues.user_problem: After adding an item to favourites or a wishlist, users who change their mind cannot deselect it on the same screen — they must navigate to a separate favourites page to remove it, adding unnecessary friction
signals_to_detect: Tapping the favourite/heart/bookmark icon on a PLP card adds the item but tapping again does nothing
The icon state changes on addition but does not toggle off on a second tap
Users must visit a separate favourites page to remove an item they just added
No undo or remove option appears in the confirmation feedback after adding to favourites
Favourite icon in the selected state is not clickable on PDP
issues.recommendation: Implement the favourite/wishlist icon as a true toggle on both PLP cards and PDP — one tap to add, one tap to remove. The icon should visually reflect both states (outline = not saved, filled = saved) and both states must be interactive. On removal, show a brief undo snackbar (e.g., 'Removed from favourites — Undo') so accidental removals can be reversed without navigating away.
acceptance_criteria: Favourite icon on PLP and PDP is a true toggle — tapping when filled removes the item from favourites
Both add and remove interactions work without navigating away from the current page
Icon state (filled/outline) updates immediately on tap with no delay
Brief undo snackbar appears for 3 seconds after removal allowing accidental removal to be reversed
User testing confirms users can add and remove favourites without leaving PLP or PDP
negative_signals: Favourite icon toggles correctly on both PLP and PDP
Remove works without leaving the current page
Undo option available post-removal
issues.context_notes: Test by adding an item to favourites on a PLP card and then tapping the icon again to check if it removes. Do not flag: Platforms where favourites are intentionally managed from a dedicated wishlist page and this is communicated clearly. Industry context: Non-toggleable favourites icons are a common mobile UX issue that makes the save feature feel broken.

issues.issue_title: Product specifications layout identical across all product types — unsuited to product-specific attributes
issues.user_problem: The product specifications section uses a one-size-fits-all template (the same fields and layout for every product type), displaying irrelevant attributes for some products and missing critical attributes for others
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: A laptop PDP shows the same spec fields as a pen or stationery product
Critical category-specific attributes missing — e.g., no screen resolution on a monitor, no battery life on a laptop
Blank or 'N/A' values appearing in spec fields because the template field does not apply to the product
High-priority specs buried below low-priority or irrelevant fields
Spec field labels use technical jargon not matched to how customers search or compare (e.g., 'RAM' shown as 'System Memory')
issues.recommendation: Define product-type-specific specification templates for each major product category. Each template should: (1) show only the attributes relevant to that category, (2) order attributes by purchase-decision importance for that category, (3) use the terminology customers recognise. Work with the product data team to ensure supplier feeds map to the correct template. Hide or suppress any spec field with a null or N/A value unless the absence of that feature is itself meaningful (e.g., 'No optical drive').
acceptance_criteria: Distinct spec templates defined for each major product category (electronics, stationery, books, software, etc.)
Each template shows only relevant attributes — no blank/N/A spec fields visible to users
Category's most purchase-critical specs appear in the first 5 visible rows without scrolling
Spec field labels use consumer-recognisable terminology aligned with how users search and compare
Template completeness audited — top 10 products per category show all expected critical specs
negative_signals: Product type-specific spec templates in use
No blank or N/A spec fields visible
Critical specs visible without scrolling
issues.context_notes: Compare the spec section across 3 different product categories (e.g., laptop, pen, book) and assess whether the fields and order match the category's key decision attributes. Do not flag: Platforms with a small, homogeneous catalogue where a universal spec template is genuinely appropriate. Industry context: Spec template misalignment is most severe in multi-category retailers (electronics + stationery + books) where a single template cannot serve all product types.

issues.issue_title: Multiple review types displayed together without differentiation — customer vs expert reviews conflated
issues.user_problem: Customer reviews and expert or editorial reviews are displayed in the same visual format and location, causing users to not understand which opinions are from verified buyers and which are from paid reviewers or the brand
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: Customer reviews and expert/editorial reviews appear in the same feed with the same visual style
No visible badge, label, or section separation distinguishing verified buyer reviews from professional/expert reviews
Expert reviews mixed into the customer review star-rating calculation
Users in testing unable to distinguish which reviews are from real customers vs paid/editorial sources
Review source (platform, publication) not shown for expert reviews
issues.recommendation: Separate customer reviews and expert/editorial reviews into clearly labelled sections. Customer reviews should use a 'Verified purchase' or 'Verified buyer' badge. Expert reviews should show the reviewer's name, publication/source, and date. Use distinct visual styling (background, section heading) to make the separation immediately clear. Do not blend expert reviews into the customer rating calculation — keep ratings separate.
acceptance_criteria: Customer reviews and expert reviews in separate, clearly labelled sections with distinct visual styling
Customer reviews show 'Verified purchase' badge where purchase is confirmed
Expert reviews show reviewer name, source/publication, and date
Expert reviews not included in the customer star rating aggregate
User testing confirms 100% of users can distinguish customer reviews from expert reviews
negative_signals: Customer and expert reviews in separate clearly labelled sections
Verified purchase badge on customer reviews
Expert reviews show source and not blended into star rating
issues.context_notes: Check the reviews section of PDPs for any products that have both customer and editorial/expert reviews. Do not flag: Platforms that only have one type of review. Industry context: Mixing review types without differentiation is a consumer trust issue — expert reviews funded by the brand can be mistaken for independent customer feedback.

issues.issue_title: Password show/hide toggle missing from password input field
issues.user_problem: Users cannot verify what they are typing in a password field because there is no option to reveal the characters, leading to input errors, failed logins, and frustration
signals_to_detect: Password input field has no eye/show icon to toggle character visibility
Confirm password field also lacks a show/hide toggle
Users must retype a password from memory with no way to verify what they have entered
Login error rate is high — inability to verify password input is a likely contributing factor
Mobile keyboard on password field cannot be confirmed before submission
issues.recommendation: Add a show/hide password toggle (eye icon) to all password input fields across: login, registration, password change, and any checkout password creation fields. The icon should be positioned inside the input field on the right side. Toggle between showing the actual characters and masking them. Ensure the toggle is keyboard-accessible and has an appropriate aria-label ('Show password' / 'Hide password').
acceptance_criteria: Show/hide password toggle (eye icon) present on all password input fields across the entire site/app
Toggle positioned inside the input field on the trailing edge
Toggle keyboard-accessible and has aria-label 'Show password' / 'Hide password'
Character visibility toggles immediately on icon tap/click
Confirm password field also has independent show/hide toggle
negative_signals: Show/hide toggle present on all password fields
Toggle keyboard accessible with correct aria-label
Works on both login and registration fields
issues.context_notes: Check login, registration, and password change forms. Do not flag: Platforms where the show/hide toggle is already implemented correctly on all password fields. Industry context: Password show/hide is a WCAG 2.1 Level AA success criterion (1.3.5) and a universally expected pattern — its absence is a basic usability failure.

issues.issue_title: Transactional confirmation sent in a different language than the one used during the interaction
issues.user_problem: A user who completes a registration, purchase, or action in one language receives the confirmation email or notification in a different language, creating confusion and a disconnected experience
signals_to_detect: A user registers using the English interface and receives the OTP or confirmation email in Arabic
A user places an order in Arabic and receives the order confirmation in English
System-generated notifications use a default language that does not match the user's selected interface language
Language preference not captured at sign-up and not stored against the user's communication preferences
Post-purchase emails use a template language independent of the checkout language used
issues.recommendation: Capture the user's language preference at the point of first interaction (registration or first session) and store it as a communication preference. Use this preference to determine the language of all outbound communications (email, SMS, push notifications). Where a language preference is not explicitly set, default to the language of the user's last active session, not the system default. Allow users to update their communication language preference in account settings.
acceptance_criteria: Language preference captured at registration and stored against the user's profile
All outbound communications (email, SMS, push) sent in the user's stored language preference
Where no preference is set, communications default to the session language at time of action
Users can update communication language preference in account settings
Tested end-to-end: register in English → receive English confirmation; register in Arabic → receive Arabic confirmation
negative_signals: Confirmations and notifications in user's selected interface language
Language preference stored and editable in account settings
No language mismatch between UI and outbound communications
issues.context_notes: Test by completing registration in each supported language and verifying the language of the confirmation message received. Do not flag: Minor cosmetic differences (brand name in original language) in otherwise correctly localised communications. Industry context: Language mismatch in transactional emails is a common consequence of using a single-language email template without localisation integration.

issues.issue_title: Promotional banner text truncated with no way to read the full message
issues.user_problem: A promotional or content banner has its text cut off mid-sentence because it overflows its container, with no expand, scroll, or 'read more' mechanism to access the complete message
signals_to_detect: Promotional banner text visibly cut off with ellipsis (...) and no expand option
Arabic text in a banner designed for English overflows and is clipped
Text in a banner is truncated on smaller screen sizes with no responsive reflow
A promotional offer or condition is partially hidden — users cannot read the full terms
Banner text is cut off in RTL (right-to-left) mode but displays correctly in LTR
issues.recommendation: Design all promotional banners to accommodate the full text in the longest supported language. For Arabic in particular, ensure the banner dimensions account for Arabic text being typically 20–30% longer than the English equivalent. If a banner cannot expand to fit all text, use a 'View offer details' link that opens a modal with the complete message. Never truncate text that contains promotional terms, conditions, or calls to action.
acceptance_criteria: All promotional banner text fully visible without truncation on all supported screen sizes
Arabic banners tested specifically for text overflow — dimensions accommodate longer Arabic strings
If a full-text display is not possible, a 'Read more' or 'View details' link provides access to the complete message
No promotional condition or CTA text is truncated or clipped on any device size
RTL and LTR modes both tested — no text overflow in either direction
negative_signals: All banner text fully visible on tested screen sizes
Arabic banners accommodate longer text without truncation
No promo conditions hidden by text overflow
issues.context_notes: Check banners in both English and Arabic by switching language. Particularly check smaller screen sizes (375px). Do not flag: Intentionally short teaser banners where truncation is by design and 'View full offer' is provided. Industry context: Truncated Arabic text in banners designed for English is extremely common in MENA e-commerce due to Arabic strings being longer than their English counterparts.

issues.issue_title: No social or third-party sign-up option — registration is email/password only
issues.user_problem: Users who prefer to sign up using Google, Apple, or another identity provider they already trust cannot do so — they must create a new platform-specific account with a new password, adding friction and increasing abandonment
signals_to_detect: Registration and login pages offer only email/password or phone/OTP — no social sign-in buttons
No Google, Apple, Facebook, or other OAuth provider options visible on sign-up or login screens
Users in testing or feedback mention abandoning sign-up due to not wanting to create another password
Competitor platforms in the same market offer social sign-in options
Registration form has multiple required fields that social sign-in would pre-fill automatically
issues.recommendation: Implement at minimum Google Sign-In and Apple Sign-In (Apple is required for iOS apps that offer social login). For MENA markets, also consider adding a government SSO option if available (e.g., UAE Pass, Nafath). Present social login options prominently above the email/password form on both registration and login screens, separated by an 'or' divider. Always maintain the email/password option as a fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Google Sign-In implemented and visible on both registration and login screens
Apple Sign-In implemented on iOS (required by App Store guidelines if any social sign-in offered)
Social sign-in buttons displayed above the email/password form with an 'or continue with email' divider
Social sign-in creates an account if the user is new, or links to an existing account if the email matches
Email/password option retained alongside social sign-in — not replaced
negative_signals: Google and/or Apple sign-in options visible on registration and login
Social sign-in buttons prominently placed
Email/password option still available as alternative
issues.context_notes: Check registration and login screens for social sign-in options. Do not flag: Platforms in regulated industries (banking, healthcare, government) where social SSO is prohibited by compliance requirements. Industry context: Social sign-in reduces registration drop-off by 20–40% in most consumer app contexts — it is particularly impactful on mobile where typing a new password is most cumbersome.

issues.issue_title: No in-app customer support channel — users forced to external contact methods
issues.user_problem: Users who need help while using the app cannot access support without leaving the app to call, email, or visit a website, creating friction and loss of context for their support request
signals_to_detect: No chat, messaging, or support contact option accessible from within the app
Help section in the app only contains FAQs — no way to contact a human
Support requires leaving the app to use a phone number or external email client
Users in testing or reviews cite inability to get in-app support as a key frustration
Support link in-app opens an external website in a browser, losing app context
issues.recommendation: Implement at least one in-app support channel: a live chat (or async messaging), an in-app support ticket submission form, or a click-to-call button that passes context. The support entry point should be accessible from any screen via a persistent help icon or from the account menu. For async support, show the average response time upfront. Ensure the support channel is contextual — it should pre-fill the user's account, device, and current screen information so they do not have to re-explain.
acceptance_criteria: At least one in-app support channel accessible without leaving the app
Support entry point reachable from any screen within 2 taps
Support form or chat pre-populates user account info and current screen context
Average response time displayed for async channels
User testing confirms users can initiate a support request without leaving the app
negative_signals: In-app support channel accessible without leaving app
Support reachable within 2 taps from any screen
Support pre-populates user context
issues.context_notes: Check whether any support option in the app can be used without opening an external browser or phone dialler. Do not flag: Apps where a well-functioning chatbot or FAQ resolves the majority of support requests and human escalation is accessible as a secondary option. Industry context: In-app support is a standard expectation in consumer apps — apps that force users to external contact lose users who abandon their issue rather than leave the app.

issues.issue_title: Product specs and key features buried — only accessible by scrolling past extensive content
issues.user_problem: Users who want to check specific product specifications or key features before purchasing must scroll past a long product description, video, or other content blocks to reach them, causing them to miss the specs or abandon the page
signals_to_detect: Product specification table or key features section appears below the fold after scrolling through full description, video, and editorial content
No tab or anchor navigation to jump directly to specifications
Users in testing spend excessive time scrolling to find specs and express frustration
Search-intent users arrive on PDP looking for a specific spec and cannot find it quickly
PDP content order puts marketing/lifestyle content before technical specifications
issues.recommendation: Move the key specifications section above the product description on PDPs for categories where specs drive purchase decisions (electronics, appliances, technical products). Alternatively, use a sticky tab bar (Overview, Specifications, Reviews) allowing users to jump directly to specs. For feature-rich products, show the 3–5 most critical specs as a 'key features' summary near the price/CTA area, with a link to the full specification table below.
acceptance_criteria: Key features summary (3–5 critical specs) visible near the price/Add to Cart area without scrolling on tech/electronics PDPs
Sticky tab navigation ('Specs', 'Reviews', 'Overview') present on PDPs for complex products
Tapping 'Specs' tab scrolls immediately to the full specification table
Full specification table accessible within 2 taps or 1 scroll stop from the product title
User testing with 5 task-oriented users confirms all can find a specific spec within 15 seconds
negative_signals: Key specs visible near price/CTA area without scrolling
Sticky tab navigation to specs available
Users locate specific spec within 15 seconds in testing
issues.context_notes: Test on tech/electronics PDPs by trying to find a specific spec (e.g., RAM, battery life) and measuring how much scrolling is required. Do not flag: Lifestyle or fashion PDPs where specs are not the primary decision driver. Industry context: Spec findability is a primary driver of the high PDP-to-cart drop-off in electronics — users who cannot find specs abandon rather than add to cart.

issues.issue_title: Payment method logo or icon unrecognisable — users cannot identify if their preferred method is supported
issues.user_problem: A payment method available at checkout is represented by an unrecognisable or generic logo, meaning users do not realise it is supported and may abandon checkout believing their preferred payment method is unavailable
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: A payment method logo is displayed but users in testing do not recognise what it represents
Generic icon or company name used instead of the recognised brand logo for a payment provider
Payment method available but users in testing mention they would abandon because they don't see their preferred method
Logo is too small to be recognisable at the display size used
Payment method listed as text only with no recognisable logo or icon
issues.recommendation: Use the official, current brand logos of all supported payment methods at a minimum size of 40px height. For less well-known local payment methods (e.g., mobile wallet brands), supplement the logo with the name as text. Show all accepted payment methods as a row of logos early in the checkout flow and also on the PDP/cart near the CTA so users can confirm their method is supported before starting checkout.
acceptance_criteria: All payment method logos use official brand assets at minimum 40px height
Less well-known payment methods show both logo and name label
Accepted payment methods displayed on PDP/cart near the CTA — not only on the checkout page
User testing confirms 100% of users correctly identify all displayed payment methods
Payment method logos updated when brands update their visual identity
negative_signals: All payment logos use official brand assets
Less well-known methods show logo + name
Payment methods shown on PDP/cart before checkout begins
User testing confirms 100% recognition
issues.context_notes: Check payment method logos on PDP, cart, and checkout pages. Show them to a test user unfamiliar with the platform and ask what payment methods are available. Do not flag: Widely recognised global brands (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal) where logo recognition is near-universal. Industry context: Unrecognised payment logos cause pre-emptive checkout abandonment — users abandon before attempting checkout if they believe their method is unsupported.

issues.issue_title: CTA label uses unfamiliar or formal language — users unsure what action it triggers
issues.user_problem: A call-to-action button uses a label that is technically correct but unfamiliar to the target audience — particularly when the language is formal or legalistic where colloquial language is expected — causing users to hesitate or not click
nielsen_heuristic: Match between system and real world
signals_to_detect: CTA label uses a formal or technical term where a simpler term is universally understood (e.g., 'Redeem' vs 'Apply', 'Submit request' vs 'Apply code', formal Arabic vs colloquial Arabic)
Users in testing hesitate on a CTA or ask what it means before clicking
The action label does not describe what will happen when the button is pressed
CTA uses a noun where a verb is expected (e.g., 'Application' instead of 'Apply')
Localised CTA label uses a translation that is accurate but not the term users recognise from daily usage
issues.recommendation: Use the simplest, most action-oriented label for every CTA. The label should describe the action the user is taking, using the most familiar term for that action in the target language and dialect. For Arabic specifically, prefer colloquial Arabic terms (e.g., 'تطبيق' for Apply, 'تأكيد' for Confirm) over formal Modern Standard Arabic where the audience is everyday consumers. Test CTA labels with 5 target users — if any hesitate or ask for clarification, the label should be revised.
acceptance_criteria: All CTAs use action-verb labels describing what happens when clicked
Localised CTA labels reviewed by a native speaker of the target dialect — not translated literally from English
CTA labels for coupon/promo application use 'Apply' or the locally recognised equivalent (not 'Redeem' or formal variants)
User testing with 5 target users confirms 100% understand every CTA without hesitation
CTA labels reviewed as part of any localisation update or new market launch
negative_signals: All CTAs use action-verb labels
Localised labels reviewed by native dialect speaker
User testing confirms zero hesitation on CTA labels
issues.context_notes: Check all CTA labels, particularly in checkout, cart, and form contexts. Pay special attention to translated CTAs — these are most likely to use technically correct but user-unfamiliar terms. Do not flag: CTAs where the formal term is the recognised standard in the specific context (e.g., 'Submit' on a government form). Industry context: CTA label clarity is especially important in Arabic localisation where formal MSA and colloquial dialects have different registers — consumer platforms should use the dialect their audience recognises.

issues.issue_title: No note-taking or content-saving mechanism within learning or content platform
issues.user_problem: Users consuming structured learning content (videos, articles, lessons) have no way to highlight, annotate, or save specific sections within a piece of content for later reference — they must rely on external tools or memory
signals_to_detect: Video or article content has no note-taking panel, annotation tool, or highlight mechanism
Users in testing take notes in an external app because no in-platform note-taking exists
No 'Save this section' or 'Bookmark moment' feature within video or article content
Completed lessons have no revision notes or highlights that users can review later
Competitor learning platforms (Udemy, Coursera) offer in-video note-taking that this platform does not
issues.recommendation: Implement a lightweight note-taking feature alongside lesson content: a collapsible notes panel that is time-stamped to video position for video content, or attached to paragraphs for text content. Notes should be auto-saved, searchable, and accessible from the user's account/dashboard. At minimum, provide the ability to bookmark a specific video timestamp or article section with a personal label.
acceptance_criteria: Notes panel accessible alongside lesson or article content without leaving the content page
Video notes auto-linked to the timestamp at which they were taken
Notes auto-saved — no manual save action required
All notes for a course or content item viewable from the user's account/dashboard
Notes searchable across all content a user has accessed
negative_signals: Note-taking panel accessible within content pages
Video notes linked to timestamps
Notes auto-saved and accessible from dashboard
issues.context_notes: Applicable specifically to learning management systems, course platforms, documentation portals, and content-heavy platforms where revisiting specific sections is a core use case. Do not flag: Transactional platforms (e-commerce, booking) where note-taking is not a relevant user need. Industry context: Note-taking is a consistently requested feature in learning platforms and directly correlates with course completion rates — users who take notes complete courses at higher rates.

issues.issue_title: Already purchased or enrolled items not visually distinguished on listing pages
issues.user_problem: Users who have already purchased or enrolled in a product see it listed identically to items they have not purchased, leading to accidental duplicate purchases or wasted time investigating items they already own
signals_to_detect: A product the user has already purchased appears on a listing page with no visual indicator of prior purchase
Add to Cart CTA shown for items already in the user's account or order history
Users in testing attempt to add a course or product they already own, only discovering the duplicate in the cart
Logged-in users see purchased items with the same Add to Cart CTA as unpurchased items
No 'Already purchased', 'In library', or 'Enrolled' badge on relevant items
issues.recommendation: For logged-in users, mark any product or content item they have already purchased or enrolled in with a persistent badge or label (e.g., 'In your library', 'Already enrolled', 'Purchased'). Replace or supplement the Add to Cart CTA with a 'View' or 'Continue' CTA for already-owned items. Apply this consistently on listing pages, search results, and recommendation sections.
acceptance_criteria: Already-purchased or enrolled items show a visible badge or label for logged-in users on all listing contexts
CTA for owned items changed from 'Add to Cart' to 'View' or 'Continue' — purchase CTA removed
Badge consistent across PLPs, search results, and recommendation sections
Applies to all product and content types that can be owned or enrolled in
User testing with logged-in users confirms zero accidental duplicate purchase attempts
negative_signals: Purchased/enrolled items clearly badged for logged-in users
CTA changed from Add to Cart to View/Continue for owned items
No accidental duplicate purchase attempts in user testing
issues.context_notes: Test as a logged-in user who has a previous purchase history and browse PLPs for previously purchased items. Do not flag: Platforms where users are expected to purchase the same item multiple times (consumables, subscriptions, gifts). Industry context: Duplicate purchase prevention is particularly important on learning platforms and digital goods stores where items are single-purchase and re-buying adds no value.

issues.issue_title: No personalisation or interest-gathering step at onboarding — homepage shows generic content to all users
issues.user_problem: New users who sign up see the same generic homepage content as all other users — their interests, goals, or preferences are never asked, meaning the platform cannot surface relevant content and the user must discover everything by browsing
signals_to_detect: No interest selection, preference quiz, or goal-setting step in the onboarding flow
Homepage for a newly registered user is identical to the homepage for a returning user or anonymous visitor
Platform has categories or content types relevant to different user segments but does not ask which segment the user belongs to
Users in testing express a desire for the platform to surface relevant content to them rather than requiring manual browsing
Personalisation data (browsing history, purchases) available but not used to customise homepage content
issues.recommendation: Add a brief personalisation step to the post-registration onboarding flow (3–5 taps maximum): ask users their primary goal, interest areas, or preferences using a visual card-selection format. Use these inputs to immediately personalise the homepage content order and featured recommendations. Make it skippable but incentivised ('Select interests to see courses tailored for you'). Allow users to update their preferences from account settings at any time.
acceptance_criteria: Post-registration onboarding includes an interest or preference selection step
Selection uses a visual format (image cards or icon+label) — not a form
Step is skippable with a visible 'Skip for now' option
Homepage content immediately reflects interest selections after onboarding
Preferences editable from account settings at any time
negative_signals: Interest selection step present in onboarding flow
Homepage reflects selections immediately post-onboarding
Preferences accessible and editable in account settings
issues.context_notes: Check the post-registration flow for any preference or interest collection step. Do not flag: Platforms with a very small catalogue where personalisation would not meaningfully change what is shown. Industry context: Onboarding personalisation is a standard feature on learning platforms (Duolingo, Coursera, LinkedIn Learning) — its absence means the platform cannot demonstrate relevance to new users.

issues.issue_title: Text over images has insufficient contrast — illegible for many users
issues.user_problem: Text placed directly over product images or hero images has insufficient contrast between the text colour and the background image, making it hard or impossible to read — particularly for users with visual impairments or in bright ambient light
signals_to_detect: White text on a light-coloured or white product image area — contrast ratio below 4.5:1
Dark text on a dark hero image without a scrim or overlay to increase contrast
Text overlay colour not adapting to the lightness of the underlying image
Text over images that fails the WCAG AA contrast requirement (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text)
CTA button or headline text on a banner that is readable on some images but illegible on others as the image changes
issues.recommendation: Apply a semi-transparent dark scrim (gradient or solid overlay) beneath any text placed over an image. The scrim should ensure the contrast ratio between the text and its immediate background meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large headings). Alternatively, place text in a solid-colour text box over the image rather than directly on the image. Test contrast using a contrast ratio tool on the actual rendered output, not on design mockups.
acceptance_criteria: All text placed over images meets WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text)
A dark scrim, gradient, or solid text box applied beneath all text-over-image instances
Contrast tested on the actual rendered page using a contrast analyser — not on mockups
Contrast maintained when images change (carousel, product variants) — the scrim is applied at the container level
Passes automated accessibility scan (Axe, Lighthouse) with no contrast violations on image-overlay text
negative_signals: All text-over-image instances pass WCAG AA contrast ratio
Scrims or solid text boxes applied consistently
Automated accessibility scan confirms no contrast violations
issues.context_notes: Specifically test text placed over images — this is a distinct issue from UX-011 (general text contrast) and UX-042 (colour contrast). The specific challenge here is that the background is variable (an image) rather than a flat colour. Do not flag: Text placed next to images in a white/solid background container. Industry context: Text-over-image contrast failures are among the most common WCAG violations in retail — hero banners and product cards are the most frequent offenders.

issues.issue_title: Card component design inconsistent — same card type has varying information density across the page
issues.user_problem: Product or content cards of the same type display different amounts of information (some with title only, some with title and subtitle, some with price and rating, others without) on the same page, making comparison and scanning inefficient
signals_to_detect: Product cards on the same PLP have varying numbers of information fields — some show price, some do not
Cards in the same grid have different heights due to inconsistent content rendering
Some cards show a subtitle or secondary label while others of the same type do not
Rating stars appear on some cards but are absent on others of the same type in the same context
CTA buttons appear on some cards but not others in the same grid, with no logical differentiation
issues.recommendation: Define a fixed card template for each card type used on a page: specify exactly which fields are shown, their order, and handling for missing data (show a placeholder, default value, or hide the row consistently). All cards of the same type on the same page must use the same template. For missing data (no price, no rating yet), use a consistent empty state (e.g., 'Price on request', '—' or hide the field with preserved spacing) rather than omitting the row entirely.
acceptance_criteria: All cards of the same type on the same page have identical structure, field count, and field order
Missing data shown consistently — either with a placeholder value or hidden with spacing preserved to prevent layout shift
Card height consistent within card type across the same grid — no variable height due to content difference
CTA presence follows a consistent rule — either all cards of a type show the CTA, or none do
Card template documented in design system and enforced via component props, not ad-hoc overrides
negative_signals: All cards of the same type have identical field structure on the same page
Missing data handled consistently with placeholder or uniform omission
Card heights consistent within type in same grid
issues.context_notes: Scan a PLP or homepage grid and compare card content across multiple items of the same type. Do not flag: Intentionally differentiated card types (featured vs standard card) where the difference is by design and visually signalled. Industry context: Card inconsistency is a common consequence of product data incompleteness — the UI renders whatever data exists rather than enforcing a fixed template.

issues.issue_title: Persistent floating widget or button cannot be collapsed or dismissed — covers page content
issues.user_problem: A persistent floating element (chat widget, feedback button, support icon, floating cart) cannot be minimised or dismissed by users, covering page content and interactive elements throughout the browsing session
signals_to_detect: A floating chat, support, or feedback widget visible on every page with no close or minimise option
Floating element covers CTAs, text, or product content at certain scroll positions
Users must work around the floating element to interact with content it is obscuring
Floating widget is in an expanded state by default and cannot be collapsed to a smaller icon
On mobile, the floating element occupies a significant portion of the screen with no way to move or dismiss it
issues.recommendation: All persistent floating elements must be collapsible to a small icon (maximum 56px diameter) that users can minimise at any time.
